# The ownership checker v2 — design and implementation plan

*Normative design and implementation plan. Part of #1006. The WHAT is
[`ownership-requirements.md`](ownership-requirements.md) (R-n.m below); this document is the HOW. Where they
disagree, the requirements win. End state: lists and records enforced on every platform; no copy fallback,
warning or resource-triggered coarsening; deterministic output; the `Ref` loan model (#981); ordered `Dict`
only (#961); room for #587 and an in-place shared cell type.*

**Decided resource contract [O 2026-10-25].** Precise ordinary callback labels stay. The one analysis-size
resource, `ownership_summary_size`, defaults to 65,536 **growth** records per owning declaration. Source-proportional records and unchanged
import reads have proved, nonfungible baseline lanes; nested classes, environments, contexts, sets and memo
records outside those lanes all count (§4.1). It is charged before expansion and
fails with `ownership_limit`; an attribute can raise it (§4.4). Genuine recursive summary dependencies use
§2.10's graph backreferences, never a merge of ordinary invocation contexts. §4.1 proves the total bounded
cost and identifies the fragments with stronger linear bounds; it makes no general source-linear claim.
The structural measurement's maximum **10** at `o/LimitOwnedAtoms.beni:45` counts callback labels, not the
complete new resource; S3a must measure the latter (#1056). The resource bounds explicit label growth; it does not make that growth linear.

**The local value domain [O 2026-11-02, #1685].** The shape domain this document first specified (shape nodes, cells, κ, views, fold-first propagation) is replaced by the slot domain: §2.3 (slots, positions, roots, values, leaves, choices as tags), §2.9 (the selection, the one relation, the distinct check), §2.10 (contracts), §2.11 (calls, callbacks, closures), §2.12 (⊥, deliveries, validation), §3.2–§3.6 and §5. Text elsewhere that speaks of a cell, a node, κ, a class or a view reads as a leaf, a value, a selection, a contract or a call's instantiation (§2.3's note).

**Reading order for an implementer.** §1 says why the slot domain; §2 is the semantics every module obeys and
§2.14 the lemmas each rule must keep; §3 the layout of every table; §5 the files and the layering gate; §8 the
slice you are on. Appendix A maps every requirement to its section; Appendix B every pending fixture to its slice.

**Sources cited.** Papers in `/home/canassa/src/github.com/canassa/ownership-library/` (`SOURCE-STUDY.md` for
file:line into the vendored checkers; `papers/`, `catalogue/`), `docs/design/research/68`, `69`,
`docs/thesis/ownership/` (thesis §n), the frozen v1 (`src/own/`, `ownership-checker.md` = oc §n), its review
(`~/.cache/beni-agents/ownership-review-fable/report.md`) and the two reviews of this document's first draft.

---

## 1. The choice of family

### 1.1 What the requirements demand of the domain

| | Property | Forced by |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | per-field, per-path liveness at any depth; a later read of an untouched field is no use | R-4.1.2, R-4.8.2, R-4.3.5 |
| P2 | per-path reads and writes of a callee (`changed` never reads `.todos`; a W at `π2.todos` only) | R-2.6, R-4.3.5, R-4.8.5, R-5.1.1 |
| P3 | provenance: the result *is* argument 1 / is fresh / holds `cb_j`'s answer; fresh cells numbered so two result paths naming one number are one object | R-4.10.1–R-4.10.3, R-5.1.2, R-5.2.4 |
| P4 | callbacks: what a callee supplies (owned or borrowed), needs of a result, keeps; folds' feedback | R-5.2, R-5.3, R-5.8 |
| P5 | exclusive contents of a container, per written path, kept through destructive reads, refuted by a taken element stored back | R-4.6, R-4.10.7–R-4.10.13 |
| P6 | levels of a recursive value told apart where the text does, folded finitely where it does not | R-4.7 |
| P7 | directional aliasing (`ys = xs` then a write through `ys` with `xs` dead is accepted), branches that keep the old value | R-4.1.5, R-4.2 |

Plus a soundness argument per rule (R-3), the proved-fragment and resource bounds (R-7.2–R-7.4), modular summaries hashed with the
interface (R-5.7), and a three-place diagnostic (R-6.6).

### 1.2 The four candidates, judged

**(b) Inferred uniqueness types, Clean-style** (`src/clean/frontend/refmark.icl`, `unitype.icl`; research 69
§2.1). Attributes on every type position, inferred by coercion inequalities solved eagerly; sharing by counting
occurrences per field (`SelectiveUse`, R:33-37), sequencing marking earlier uses non-unique (R:804-830). P1 yes.
P7 no: `[ …xs, List.length xs ]` (R-4.1.3) counts two occurrences and refuses; a unification-based attribute
poisons every value a shared one touches (Emre et al., thesis §3.4). P2/P3 no: an attribute never says "the result
is argument 1" (R-4.10.1) or "fresh number 2". P4: function types force invariance (U:840-864). P5: deep uniqueness
`*[*a]` exists (Barendsen–Smetsers) but no materialisation (R-4.6.9). Diagnostics name one place (R:913).
**Rejected as the core.** Taken: the demand in the library's types, and uniqueness as a predicate of one type
position. `excl` claims exclusivity at the path it names, never at every descendant (§2.9, I-κ); Clean's deep
`*[*a]` is not taken.

**(c) Borrow inference plus a static contract** — Lean 4 (`InferBorrow.lean`), Koka `fip` (`CheckFBIP.hs`), Roc
(`arc_solve.zig`). Per-variable owned/borrowed, per-SCC fixpoint, borrowed by default. P1 partial (Lean per
variable, 378-380; Roc `ret_unique_fields`). P3 none; reuse rests on run-time reference counts, which R-1.2
forbids. P4: Koka warns on higher-order (F:264-279). P5/P6 no. Koka's `fip` is the one contract that *fails loudly*
when reuse cannot be proved. **Rejected as the core.** Taken: the loud contract; borrowed-by-default callbacks; a
driver whose facts only grow and re-visits a member only when a dependency changed (Lean 263-326; Roc
arc_solve.zig:25-29).

**(d) Morphic per-slot modes with `u ≤ v` constraints** (`annot_modes.rs`, `inequality_graph2.rs`). Slots per type
shape, recursive types parameterised per type SCC (`SccParameterizer`, A:295-432); lifetimes as path trees;
constraints solved in one topological pass over the condensed graph (I:114-171). P1 yes; P6 the right place set.
P3/P4/P5: a mode is *owned or borrowed*, not *which object*; first-order IR, no closures. **Rejected as the core.**
Taken: type-shaped slots folded per type SCC (our places), signature variables (our atoms over arrivals), and the
condensed-graph propagation for the fixpoints that carry cells along inclusion edges (§2.12).

**(a) A shape graph: abstract interpretation with materialisation** — Chase–Wegman–Zadeck (`papers/1990-chase-…`),
Sagiv–Reps–Wilhelm (`1996-sagiv-…`, `1998-…toplas`: the `is` sharing predicate, *focus*), Whaley–Rinard escape
graphs composed by grafting (`1999-whaley-…` §4), Sălcianu–Rinard write effects per parameter path
(`2005-salcianu-…`), Deutsch's folded access paths (Mazur's type selector, `ctgc.selector.m:417-541`). Nodes stand
for objects at the paths of a type, labelled with provenances; a summary is such a graph over parameters and
result; a call grafts; a taken element is *materialised* out of its summary node. P1–P7 are all expressible;
soundness is the standard per-rule over-approximation argument; diagnostics fall out of provenance. Its known
cost, and v1's failure, is representation: enumerated paths exponential in value depth (#856), unbounded through
cyclic types (#955), pairwise in width (#693), instantiated as lists (#716).

### 1.3 The choice

*Replaced 2026-11-06 (#2143). Until then this section chose family (a) with structurally interned shape nodes,
`delta`, a lazy `union`, widening onto the place graph, and κ per path. The owner replaced that carrier on 2026-11-02
(#1685; report 109), and §2.3–§2.12 changed then. This section did not. The old text is in git history.*

**v2 is a type-indexed slot domain: family (a)'s provenance and per-rule over-approximation, over (d)'s finite
vocabulary of type paths, with (c)'s loud contract and driver. A selection replaces κ.**

1. **Places are type-shaped and folded per type SCC**, derived from the solved type graph, which `unify` builds
   coinductively (`checker-v2.md` §7.3): a cyclic type with no name (#955) is one place (§2.1).
2. **Objects are named by slots.** A slot is a canonical path of a place (§2.3.1). The types fix the vocabulary before
   the walk starts, so every fixpoint ranges over a finite set, and nothing widens.
3. **A value is a small tree, not a history** (§2.3.3): what this frame built, with references at its leaves to subtrees
   of what it did not build. Its leaves say where its objects can come from (§2.3.4).
4. **Conditions are one kind of thing**, the selection (§2.9.1): a set of parameter slots, each object of which occurs
   once among them. Conjunction is a union. No table of pairs exists.
5. **One relation compares two leaves** (§2.9.2): no, under a selection, or may. Choices are tags on leaves (§2.3.5): two
   arms of one `case` never coexist, because a frame runs each instruction at most once.
6. **A contract describes a code over slots** (§2.10): arrivals, reads, writes, escapes, stores, labels and conditions.
   A call instantiates it once (§2.11.2). A function parameter is a label, resolved where the code is known (§2.11.3). A
   function in a result has a called contract. A contract names no declaration: the room #587 needs.
7. **One fixpoint shape**: ⊥, deliveries of facts along edges, then one validation walk that trusts nothing the
   deliveries computed (§2.12). Rounds end by the finite vocabulary. A resource cap of 4 096 rounds stands behind that
   (`Groups.zig`) and fails `ownership_limit`: it accepts nothing (R-7.4, O11).
8. **The contract fails loudly** (Koka `fip`): every unprovable write is an error with a named fix; a resource limit is
   an `ownership_limit`; nothing is ever a copy. Rows are data (§2.13.6), and no Zig names a declaration.

**Why this family.** The shape carrier was indexed by values, with no bound known in advance, and representation was
§1.2's named risk: `Dict.removeMin` passed 1.15 M growth records against a limit of 65 536 (#1372, #1590), and two
experiments refuted fixes inside the model (§2.3). The slot experiment took generic `removeMin` to 20 214 records with
growth 0 (report 109, §6, recommendation 1). A vocabulary the types fix is what buys that bound. Report 109's
recommendation 5, a soundness argument per rule over the slot carrier, was not taken on 2026-11-02. §2.14 is that argument.

**What the requirements get from it.**

| | Property | How the slot domain meets it | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | per-path liveness | a use at its path, §2.7, read against a hold's path | a hold is by slot, so two objects at one slot are one hold |
| P2 | per-path callee effects | `reads`, `writes` as trees over slots, §2.10 | exact to the slot; a `⟲` is every level |
| P3 | provenance | arrivals, and `fresh` as one atom per call | an atom names every object of the call, so a call never tells two of its fresh objects apart by name |
| P4 | callbacks | labels: supplies, `kept`, `sep`, `below`, `each`, `calls`, answers | a code no label names has escaped |
| P5 | exclusive contents, per written path | a selection at the written slot; `taken` rows and `each` supplies ask the written slot plain and the family apart | a fold's element: `lost`, C.9 gap 3 |
| P6 | levels told apart where the text does | positions within a frame; a first return is a plain step, §2.1 | below a first return, levels fold onto one `⟲` |
| P7 | directional aliasing | the relation is asked of live holders only, §2.8 | none |

**What the implementation gave up,** beyond those limits:

- **Materialisation as a fact of the value.** The refinements `elem`, `others`, `level` and `below·s` are gone (not
  `below(p)`, the slot set of §2.3.1). A position says what the source projected, in one frame. Across a call only a selection separates two objects of one slot.
- **`delta`.** A record update copies (§2.11.5), so R-4.8's `update` demand, O7 and O12 wait for S5. Records are not
  written in place today, and no sanitiser pass checks them.
- **Non-regular types.** A non-regular type folds at its head (§2.1), so a place stands for instantiations that differ
  in structure. What lies below the fold has no slot. Whether beni supports these types is the owner's open decision. §2.14
  states this as an open hole.
- **Precision against v1.** R-8.3 is not met: `tests/blackbox/ownership-v2-known.txt` carried 361 rows where v1 accepts and
  v2 refuses at `1550a68d61`, and eight amendments of §2 end in *Refused that a perfect checker accepts*.
- **Size.** The first plan named 21 modules and 19 050 lines. `src/own2/` has 121 files and 32 537 lines, without S5,
  S7, S8b, S9 or S10.

## 2. The semantic core

Notation: `ε` the empty path; steps `.f`, `.i`, `C#i`, `[*]` (list/dictionary position), `◇` (closure
environment), `◆` (`Ref` contents), `⟨n⟩` (opaque slot), `⟲` (one or more levels below a recursive place), `…` (a record's row, §2.1).
`A(e)` the value of `e` (§2.3.3); `Σ` the frame state (§2.4); `γ` concretisation (§2.14.2). BIR = `src/bir/Bir.zig`: a declaration
is a contiguous instruction range in evaluation order, every binding a distinct local index (`Lower.bindLocal`
appends; nothing rebinds).

### 2.1 Places

A **place** is a node of the type-shaped graph, with children by step. Structural store nodes and nominal
constructor applications supply its nodes; lexical closure environments add accounted edges. A type variable,
function type, crossing primitive or foreign type without published slots is a leaf. **The graph source**
combines the solved structural store with each nominal type's *constructor templates*:
`Walk.structural`'s successors of an `app` are its type arguments, and a constructor's payloads are not in the
store at all. For a type of the module being checked the templates are its BIR `ctors` over `declTypeParams`; for
an imported type they are the interface's `arg_terms` (what `Schemes.instantiateCtorWith` reads), an opaque type
read through its published slots. A record, tuple or function type is read off the store variable as before.
The walk substitutes the argument *places* for the type parameters — an environment over places, never fresh store
variables (`Instantiate.ctorType` allocates flex variables per use, needs a live checker frame and would unfold a
recursive type forever) — and memoises on `(head TypeId, argument PlaceIds)`, which is this section's own
structural identity `(kind, head, children)`: so a recursive type, named or not, folds onto itself at its head,
a *different instantiation* (`Tree (Tree (List Int))`'s inner tree, `Maybe (Maybe a)`, `Dict String (Dict String …)`'s
inner dictionary) is another place (R-4.7.3), and a non-regular nested type (`Nest a = Cons a (Nest (List a))`),
whose instantiations never repeat, folds at its head after the first level — one place for every `Nest`, the
argument places joined — so the graph stays finite. `Place.zig` is a pure graph walk over a `Place.Source`
interface that describes one node as `(kind, head, children)`; the adapter from the checker's tables is built at
the `Enforce`/`Groups` boundary (§8, S3a) and is the one piece of `own2/` that reads a type's structure (§5).

| Place kind | Steps | Holds a cell of kind | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `record` | `.f` per field, and `…` when the row is open | `record` | every record type (R-4.8.1); `…`: *The row of a record*, below |
| `tuple` | `.i` | none | never written |
| `ctor` | `C#i` per constructor and argument | none | **a sum**: paths through different constructors are alternatives (§2.2); a record-alias constructor is a `record` |
| `list` | `[*]` | `list` | `[*]` is a *summary* place (positions merged); supplied for List and Builder by `sequence` metadata (§2.13.6) |
| `dict` | `[*]` (values) | `dict` | keys cross (R-4.10.9); `Set` is `Dict k ⊤` |
| `ref` | `◆` | `ref` | types carrying `cell` metadata, including Ref/Deferred; `◆` is a barrier (§2.13.7) |
| `closure` | `◇` | `closure` | the environment; children are the captured paths; carries a class slot (§2.10) |
| `opaque` | `⟨n⟩` per published slot | `opaque` | `Js.Value`, `Html`, a program (R-4.6.5) |
| `var` | none | any | a type variable may hold anything (R-5.5.11); a record's row is one |
| `cross` | none | none | primitives, `⊤`, `⊥`, a nominal type reaching no tracked place, a crossing foreign type |

**A step past a fold** (#1957). A `var` place a non-regular type folded to has no steps, yet its value has structure: `Wrap
(Leaf [ ys ])` of `T (List Int)`, where `T a = Leaf a | Wrap (T (List a))`, steps past the `var` at `Leaf`'s payload. No other `var` place
is ever stepped, because code cannot take a type variable's value apart. So a value projected by a step such a place cannot name is `⊤`: no slot says
what is below the fold, so a write of it is refused `unknown`, and a `⊤` that leaves as a result arrives at its slot and open below it,
since a step of it is no more fresh than it is. A value *at* the `var` slot, not stepped past it, is a parameter's as ever: a write of it is
deep, since the slot's own object may be a list of lists. A result
that leaves by a concrete type over the fold (`pick t = case t of Wrap (Leaf ys) → ys`, `List (List Int)` over `var`) arrives at its slot
and open below it, deep, and a caller's suffix past its own argument's fold reads what arrived whole (`Relation.arrivalLeaves`). Only a
slot below a root counts: a lambda's own parameter is a `var` place too, with no fold in it. A call's or an answer's value mapped so is `⊤`
below that slot, since its contract names none. Before this,
the step read as a scalar: no demand was made, no write reached the contract, and the build emitted a copying push, a silent fallback
`PolyRecCps`'s `useCps` shows (Appendix B, the `cps` site). Refused that a perfect checker accepts: any write past the fold, over fresh data too (#2038). Fixtures `run/SanitiserFoldedType`, `run/SanitiserFoldedTypeApart`.

A level read on a built value is read at the place the path names, not the value's own. A non-regular type's instantiations never repeat, so
`Wrap (Wrap (Leaf k))` of `T (List Int)` sits at a place of its own, and `#1.0⟲` met no kid on a cycle, read empty, and `k` was edited in place (#2062). The path's
steps from the value it starts at reach the place of the `⟲` (`LevelCycle.of`), the fold here, and the literal's kids are walked along that place's cycle. So an
element `a` of a literal, which reaches the type's own nominal only by what `a` stands for, is no level, and a type with both a plain recursion and a fold reads the
fold when the path does. Where two paths of one read part (`RouteWalk`), the rest of each goes on from the place the walk has reached, never the kid's own (`Eval.tail_place`): `Wrap (Wrap x _) (Wrap y _)` read `wr x + wr y` at `x`'s own place, met no level, and edited `k` (#2062, `run/SanitiserLevelPart`). Refused that a perfect checker accepts: `⟲` takes every kid on the cycle, so a literal that holds an unwritten sibling twice is refused `disjoint` at the write, as a regular type's is.
*Amended 2026-11-07 (#2192): every route.* A part of a literal that this frame did not build, a reference, can stand on the cycle at another place than the `⟲`'s: `x` of `P (Wrap x) 0` in `type T = Leaf (List Int) | Wrap Box | P T Int`, `type Box = Bx T T`. Its next levels were the shortest steps to the `⟲`'s place and the levels below them: one route, `#Bx.0`, so a write at `#Bx.1` was never read and `k` there was edited in place. A `⟲` covers every level, so a reference's next levels are **every first arrival** at the `⟲`'s place, each canonical path once (`StepsTo.of`: it walks the cycle's steps only, folds by `extend`, so a middle type's own loop ends, and does not go on past an arrival), and for each the arrival and the levels below it (`RefRead.levels`). A level below one route can fold onto another's arrival (`#L2.0#L1.0#Wrap.0#L1.0` is `#L2.0⟲#L1.0`), and one slot read twice is two objects at one write, refused `disjoint`, so each slot is read once. A sibling the `⟲` does not reach stays apart: a position is read only by the routes below it, never by `↓x`.
The `⟲` of a contract says nothing of how far the callee went: `wp` that stops at `Wrap` and `wr` that goes on write one slot, `#P.0⟨T⟩#Leaf.0`. So a read of that slot covers `Wrap`'s routes whichever it is, and `wp (P (Wrap x) 0)` with a live `k` at any route is refused; it was already at the shortest. Off the cycle, which is a non-regular instantiation only, the shortest route stays (G2). Cost: the slots read are named by route (§2.1, *One position, one name*), so the read is linear in those slots and a type that doubles on its cycle doubles them per level. A narrow callee over `d` such types, wrapped in a literal: the caller's total is 2 129, 15 527, 124 351, 1 040 615, 8 901 863 records for `d` = 1…5, where one route was 1 083, 3 914, 15 587, 65 108, 278 333. That is 2^`d` times, the ratio of the slots named, and the summary-size limit stops it past `d` = 2 (a recursive walker over all of them stops at `d` = 2 at its own declaration). Fixtures `run/SanitiserLevelRoutes`, `run/SanitiserLevelRoutesLoop`, `run/SanitiserLevelRoutesMutual`, `run/SanitiserLevelRoutesFolded`, `run/SanitiserLevelRoutesApart`.
*Amended 2026-11-07 (#2195): a call's result.* A result tree is keyed by canonical slots, and a slot below an open node can fold out of the node's words: in `hg t0 = case t0 of P (Wrap m) _ → P (Wrap m) 0; _ → Leaf []` the arrival `π1#P.0#Wrap.0` is open at `#P.0#Wrap.0`, a middle place, and `#P.0⟲#Leaf.0`, a slot below it, does not start with those words. `Forest.atSlot` walks a slot's words from the root, so it met no kid at the `⟲`, and the read said fresh. So an open arrival is also said at each level above its slot, on its cycle's suffix, the topmost of them (`LevelWide.of`, from `Put.arriveWide`; a walk of the path, not `Place.foldsUp`, whose fill every account would pay for a read that adds nothing): at target `t`, the arrival's slot by every route to `t`'s place, and by the levels below each, replayed from the arrival's path as a reference's read is (`Replay.replay`), so a third lap of a middle type's own loop is a canonical slot and not a longer word, and two routes that fold together are said once. The rest of the words then goes on from there, and every reader of a tree, a supply's included, reads it without knowing. An arrival no step goes on from is said as it is: an atom, a deep arrival at a type variable, an opaque or `self`. A label's answer has no path, and it comes here only as what a `⊤` lies inside (`ReadOff.describeOrigin`), which is said at every target first, so a reader can only gain by it. An escape can reach a told leaf after the read-off said it (`ReadOff.escapeFacts`: a closure handed to a label runs last), and that `host` goes the same way (`Put.wideLevels`). A subtree described once per place holds no cycle (`ReadOff.canNode`), so it has no fold target. A cycle of one place has no middle: a first return's levels fold below it, so its tree does not change. Fixtures `run/SanitiserLevelResult`, `run/SanitiserLevelResultHeld`, `run/SanitiserLevelResultSupply`, `run/SanitiserLevelResultApart`, `run/SanitiserLevelResultLaps` and its twin, `run/SanitiserLevelResultAst` and its twin, `run/SanitiserLevelResultEscaped` and its twin.
A function past the fold is a value no slot names, and it runs: `pf t a = case t of Wrap (Leaf [ f ]) → f a`, or `ap f a`, or `List.map fs λf → f a`. No label can
name it. The `⊤` a step past a fold gives keeps the value at the fold, its **origin** (§2.3.4), so a run of it runs what the fold holds: the origin's objects escape whole
(`FnRun.expanded`), a caller's closure there has escaped, and a writer is refused `unknown` (§2.11.3). A `var` slot read by a run is the same fact reached without a step, as in `List.head fs` of
`fs` at the fold, and only a fold's `var` holds a function, since code cannot call another type variable's value (`Want.fold`). Before this `pf` said nothing of `f`, and a writer edited what it was handed in place (#2069). Fixtures
`run/SanitiserFoldFunction`, `run/SanitiserFoldFunctionApart`, `run/SanitiserTopOrigin`, `run/SanitiserTopOriginApart`.

**A record alias's constructor** (#2056). `type alias Pt = { xs : List Int, n : Int }` declares a constructor of its fields, argument `i` being field `i` in declaration order, and `Pt k 1` is the record, at a `record` place, which has field steps and no `C#i`. So the walk builds a record of the fields those arguments name, a pattern `Pt ys _` takes the field's step, and a constructor used as a function hands each argument to its field by declaration, not by the order of the place's steps, which is the text's. Before this `(Pt k 1).xs` named no step, read as a scalar, and `k` was edited under it. Fixtures `run/SanitiserRecordCtor`, `run/SanitiserRecordCtorApart`.

**A step no place names** (#2043). A fold is not the only such step. `Q { r | a : List Int }` in a template drops its row, so `Q { b : List Int }` has a
record place with no `.b`, and a schema member inside a nominal type is read through a template that cannot name its fields. A step a place
cannot name is `⊤` at any place but `cross`, which holds no object, and a schema member in a template is a `var` place, as a fold is. *Amended 2026-11-06 (#2057): a template no longer drops its row (*The row of a record*, below), so this is what remains: a schema member, and an argument the template's walk cannot read as a record, such as a knot of a cyclic type.* Refused
that a perfect checker accepts: any write through such a step, over fresh data too (#2038). Fixtures `run/SanitiserUnnamedStep`,
`run/SanitiserUnnamedStepApart`.
*Amended 2026-11-05 (#2047):* an arrival read past an argument's fold reads empty, and an empty reading tells a caller the object is fresh, so
the value at the fold is read whole: a parameter's deep, any other root's as `⊤` (`FoldRead.zig`), and an open arrival at a `var` slot is
read deep whatever it says (`Subtree.readAt`); a read that runs past a fold is that fold's slot, in each arm of a choice (`FoldRead.prefix`). `f t c = if c then t else Leaf []`, whose result is wide, and `PW (PW _ x) _ → List.concat x`,
whose own slot runs past the fold, are refused.

**The row of a record** (#2057). `{ r | a : List Int }` is a record with a field the type names and fields it does not. A record place has one more
step for those, the **row step** `…`, whenever its row is open: its child is a `var` place, and its slot, the **row slot**, is an ordinary object slot.

- *What it means at run time.* A record value at such a place is a JavaScript object with the named fields and any others. The row slot stands for every object held by a
  field the place does not name, at any depth: a slot no step below can name, so deep (§2.9.1). **Every object in a record is at exactly one of them**: a field the
  place names is reached by that field's step, and any other field's objects are at `…`. So no object of a record is unnamed, and the argument is total.
- *What it is related to.* `.a` and `…` are two steps of one place, so two distinct positions (§2.3.2): their objects are apart only where a selection says so. `up rec = { rec | a = List.push rec.a 9 }` keeps
  `…` as an update's base holds it, so the write of `.a` asks `π1{.a,…*~}`, and `up { a = k, b = k }` is refused at the call.
- *The step carries the names it excludes.* A contract's slot is relative steps, read at another record (§2.11.2), and the caller's record may name more. So a row step's payload is the **set of field names its place names**,
  interned per module, by name in a block (§3.6). `…{a}` is printed `…`. At most one row step leaves a place, so nothing orders two of them, and it sorts after every field step.
- *Reading a row at a caller.* `…` from a record place is each field step its names do not hold, and the place's own `…` if it has one; each read deep. So `π1…{a}` at `{ a, b, c }` is `.b*`, `.c*`; at `{ s | a, b }` it is `.b*`, `…{a,b}*`;
  at a closed `{ a }` it is nothing, which is true: the record has no other field. At a `var` or `opaque` place it is that place's object, as any step a place cannot follow (§2.13.9). A built value reads the same way over its kids.
- *A caller's step into a callee's row.* A row is parametric: `r` is one type, and a callee cannot move an object between fields of it. So a caller slot `.b` of a result whose callee says `… π1…` is `π1.b`, not all of `π1…`. **A row step followed by a field or row step is that step** when the names admit it, and names nothing when they do not (`π1…{a}.a`).
  Reading a slot of a result tree (`Forest.atSlot`), a caller's `.f` the tree has no kid for, or a caller's row step, meets the node's `…` kid as an open entry at the kid's parent. So `idr { a = k, b = j }`'s `.b` is `j`, and `.b` of `idr { a = x, b = j, c = k }` holds nothing of `k`.
- *A template.* `type Q r = Q { r | a : List Int }` substitutes the row as it does any parameter: the argument's fields join `a`, its row is the record's. An argument that is no record leaves the row open.
- *An update.* `{ rec | a = x }` of a base at an open place keeps `…` as it keeps every field it does not write: a `record` value's kids are by step, and one is the row's, the base projected by `…`. So a whole read of the copy, a holder of it or a return of it reaches the row, and a read of `.a` does not.
- *A pattern.* A record pattern names fields, so it takes field steps. A variable pattern takes the record whole, at a place with its row.
- *A callback.* A supply is a tree as `res` is, read by the same reader: `appR { a = x, b = k } λr → List.push r.b 1` delivers `π1…` at the lambda's `.b` and a write reaches the actual's `.b`. A closure in a row is a function's slot in a caller's frame, where the type names it.
- *What a contract says.* `idr rec = rec` is `res ε π1ε, .a π1.a, … π1…*`. A reader of `.status` still reads `π1.status` and nothing else; a whole read of `rec` reads `…` too.

- *One comparison, and one rule per reader.* `…` and `.b` are unequal words and may be one object, so a slot's words are compared in one file: `SlotWords.under` (how much of a caller's words an entry covers, a row reading the step after its parent), `SlotWords.overlaps` (one slot at or below the other, a row read at the other's steps), and the two that say a row changes nothing: `SlotWords.same`, an identity, and `SlotWords.startsAt`, for two slots of one frame or where a miss only keeps a fact a hit would leave out. `rules_test` refuses a `std.mem` compare or search of anything but bytes in `src/own2/`, however it is spelled, an alias of `std.mem`, `std.meta.eql`, and a slice of words as bytes, each with a named exception for what is no slot (a fixed key, an id list, a whole stored selection). So a new compare of a slot's words by `std.mem` must name one of the four. That rule is syntax, and it does not close the class: a hand-written loop over words, a compare of two `Rel` ids (`a.slot == b.slot`), a word to a place (`Place.child`, `extend`) and `Forest.at` pass it. The first three are decided by reading them, and the last by `kid_readers`. A reader that keeps a hash of a slot's words (`PlainReach`) reads by `SlotWords.overlaps` when a row is among them, because a miss there relaxes the check. The rest is by reader. A reader that walks a caller's words down a callee's tree takes `Trees.rowKid`, which holds the row's names, so a read of the row is no read of a field it excludes; `rules_test` names the files that read a kid by a word, so a new one decides too. A reader of a row step and the step after it takes `SlotWords.collapse`. A reader of a built record's kids takes `RecordKid.holds`: `project`, `Captures`, `recordKid`. A `⟲` read through a row stays at the record's place (`LevelCycle.of`): the row step names the field after it. A step a frame's place has no child at in `Graft`'s fold keeps its occurrences, which are read at the caller; `Graft`'s other readers of steps refuse a row step and take the general path. A slot's draft holds arrivals, never a node, at a row (`Put.emitPart`).
- *A selection moved onto a wider record.* A condition moved to a caller by its steps (`MovedReq`, §2.11.2) reads a row at the frame's record, by `Replay`, as any caller does: `π1…{a,z}*` at `x : { a, z, b, c }` is `π1.b*`, `π1.c*`. Copied as words it was a slot that overlaps the `.b` the same selection names, so one object was asked apart from itself. A condition renamed whole (`CallGraft`) needs no reading: its callee's and its caller's places are one place. A supply passed on at a site that names more (`ReadOff`) reads the same way, each of the row's steps paired with the argument's own step, so `app`'s `.b` is `π1.b` and not the whole row.
- *A result's row is counted.* A call that does not vouch for a one-entry result is read through what its slots come from, except a slot whose arrivals are one set (#1710). A row is not such a slot (`OneSet`): a caller reads a row at its own steps, each on its own, so what a cast put at two fields of a row is two entries there, and a row's arrival is asked deep. An open record costs no more here than a closed one.
- *Its limit.* A row read at a wide record is every field it leaves, each read through a contract, so a call at a record of about 2 000 fields passes a declaration's allowance and fails with `ownership_summary_size`, loud and named (§4.4).

*Why it is sound.* Take a record `o` at a place `P` of a callee, called with `o` at the caller's place `P'`, whose names hold `P`'s by typing. Any object below `o` is below a field `f`. If `P` names `f`, the callee's slot `.f` reads it at the caller, as before. Otherwise it is in `γ(π…)`, which the caller's reading makes `.f` of `P'` deep. A write the callee makes through `…`, an escape, a read, an arrival and an occurrence all instantiate by that reading, so each reaches every object the row can hold (O1: a holder is added, never removed). The narrowing of a caller's `.b` to `π1.b` removes only objects of other fields, and it rests on parametricity: a function of type `{ r | a } → { r | a }` holds no operation that moves one field of `r` to another; a callback, a `foreign` and a worded row have their own arrivals at the result, which are read as they are. Refused that a perfect checker accepts: any two objects of one row asked apart from a named field when only one of them is written or held, as the row is one slot; and a write of a row's object reached by a fold's `var` (§2.1). *Rejected:* reading an open row as a `var` place. It refused 17 positions v1 accepts, and because an update copies kept fields from the place's steps, it lost what the update kept (`RecordUpdateEscapes`). The row is a step, so the named fields keep their slots.
Four whole reads that a closed record meets reach the row too, and are refused where a perfect checker accepts: a closure holds what it captures whole (#2136); a `case` reads its whole scrutinee (https://github.com/canassa/beni/issues/2140); a callback's answers condition asks the whole element (https://github.com/canassa/beni/issues/2141); a function a lambda reads from a supplied record is unknown (https://github.com/canassa/beni/issues/2142). Fixtures: `run/SanitiserRow`, `run/SanitiserRowApart`, `run/SanitiserRowAcrossModules`, `run/SanitiserRowWide`, `run/SanitiserRowWideApart`, `run/SanitiserRowClosure`, `run/SanitiserRowClosureApart`, `run/SanitiserRowSetter`.

**Identity.** Initial construction uses a dense `by_var` memo for structural source nodes and the adapter's
`(head, argument places)` memo for nominal applications. Each source graph node and outgoing edge is visited
once; no global structural interning is required to construct its cycles. SCC/reverse-edge work computes
`holds` in O(nodes+edges), never by rescanning the whole graph until unchanged. Constructor-template
substitution and non-regular joins are charged adapter operations, not free solved-store edges.
Structural identity compares `(kind, head, children)` where the head is the session `TypeId` of a nominal or
foreign type, the field names (by text) of a record, the arity of a tuple. Comparisons/re-interning needed by an
owner or codec use charged graph-pair tasks, not an unproved linear structural-isomorphism operation. §36's
type keys are *not* used: they exist only for closed, non-wild types of application modules
(`check/TypeKeys.zig:20-28`, `682-688`; `check/Module.zig:432`), so neither core nor `Schema` nor a polymorphic
type has one. Across modules and the cache a place is named **structurally**: a block (§3.6) writes a place as
`(kind, head name as package·module·type, children)` and the reader re-interns it onto its own graph, which is
the same graph because both were built from the same definition. A cast (§2.13.9) compares places by this
structural identity. Opaque types are read through the interface's slots (thesis Change 9; R-5.7.1): the defining
module computes its opaque type's slots as the canonical paths of its representation type that may hold a cell,
numbered in canonical-path order, each published with its kind and the structural identity of what it holds; an
importer's opaque place has one child `⟨n⟩` per slot, so two slots are told apart without the definition.

**Canonical paths.** From a root place, a step sequence in which a place appears at most once: a step that
re-enters a place already on the path pops the path back to that place and appends `⟲` (if not already last).
`⟲` means *one or more levels below*. For `type Tree = Node Tree (List Int) Tree`: `#Node.1` is the root's list,
exact; `#Node.0` re-enters the `Tree` place and so is `⟲` — the subtrees of either side are one representative,
and `⟲#Node.1` is a list at some level below the root. Left and right are told apart only by `below`
materialisation at a match (§2.13.3), which is where the text names them. Length ≤ 2·|places|. Canonical paths
name symbolic cells (§2.2) and block entries (§3.6); `⟲` is what folds recursive values finitely (thesis §3.1).

*Amended 2026-10-30 (#1253 item 1, the owner's decision, option B): the first return stays a plain step.* The
rule above made `l` and `r` of `Node l xs r` one path, `π1⟲`. So a write to `l`'s list met `r` as a holder
(`both t = case t of Node l _ r → ( kids l, r )` was refused `alias`), a call's other operand at `π1⟲` read both
subtrees of the actual (`UnusedSubtree` 36:5), and once groups were solved every tree writer's own recursive
calls were refused (`MarkerAcross.incAll` 18:19 and 18:47, `LevelRecursiveUpdates` 15:19 …). v1 keeps the
route: its level marker folds only *below* the region's first step (`π1#Node.0⟨Tree⟩#Node.1`, its §16.7). The
rule is now:

- **The fold** (`extend`). A step from path `p` onto a place `P` that `p`'s cycle suffix holds (the walk of
  #1236) is a **return**. Walking up from `p`, let `q` be the deepest node at `P`:
  - when `q` is a `⟲` node, the result is `q` (deeper levels fold onto the one marker, as before);
  - when an earlier node at `P` lies above `q` on the walk, `q` is a **first return**, and the result is
    `q·⟲`: the levels below a first return fold onto it;
  - otherwise `q` is `P`'s first occurrence on the cycle, and the step is itself a first return: a **plain
    step**, kept as it is (`PathNode.ret` marks it).

  So for `Tree`, `π1#Node.0` is `l` and `π1#Node.2` is `r`, two exact paths; `π1#Node.0#Node.1` is `l`'s own
  list; `π1#Node.0#Node.0` and `π1#Node.0#Node.2` are `π1#Node.0⟲`, one or more levels below `l`; and
  `π1#Node.0⟲#Node.1`, every list strictly below `l`, is printed as v1 prints it, `#Node.0⟨Tree⟩#Node.1`. For
  `Rose (List Rose)`, `π1#Rose.0[*]` is a child, exact, and `π1#Rose.0[*]#Rose.0[*]` is `π1#Rose.0[*]⟲`. A `⟲`
  given to `extend` directly (a use's or a hold's route) folds onto a path that ends in one and is the next
  step otherwise, as before.
- **`⟲` keeps its meaning**, one or more levels below the node it follows, which is now a first return and not
  the place's first occurrence. Every place of a cycle has its own first return, so a path names a place at
  most twice and holds at most one `⟲` per first return: its length is at most 3·|places|.
- **The closure stays linear** (§2.7's walks, `Place.hits`, `levelsOf`, the graft's levels). A K-wide type has
  K first returns at the root, each with K recursive steps, so walking each first return's steps one by one is
  K² (a deep read of a 32-wide tree cost 8 988 records, through a `Maybe` 19 420). A first return is **sealed**
  when no place of its cycle above it has returned yet (`Place.sealed`, a walk of its cycle suffix). Below a
  sealed first return every fold lands inside its own subtree and every return to its place lands on its one
  `⟲`, so its `hits` are none and its levels are itself and its `⟲`: the walks take it whole, and the closure of
  a K-wide type, plain or through a `Maybe`, is linear in K again (1 756 and 1 980 records at 32, the
  *K-wide recursive type* build test).
- **What is told apart, and what is not.** The child the route left the place by: two subtrees of one node, and
  through intermediate places too (`type A = A B (List Int) B`, `type B = B A`: `π1#A.0#B.0` and
  `π1#A.2#B.0`). Below a first return every route folds, as in v1: `l`'s left and right subtrees are both
  `π1#Node.0⟲`. A `⟲` keyed by the last step back (v1's `#Node.0⟨Tree⟩#Node.2`) would tell those apart too, at
  a `⟲` per recursive step below each first return, K² for a K-wide type; it is not built. The corpus
  difference it was thought to close, `LevelRecursiveUpdates` 64:5, is closed instead at the call, where
  the actual is a value and its written positions are told by path (§2.11 item 3, *the written position*,
  #1253): the answered right subtrees below `l` there hold no list of the left spine.
- **Who reads what.** Nothing that reads a `⟲` changes meaning: `alias`, `below`, the cycle anchors, κ's links,
  a call's readers of a `⟲` through an actual. A first return is a plain path and is read as one. Three readers
  learn of it: widen opens a union, choice or positions node at a first return as at a `⟲` (both are returns on
  the cycle being folded) and keys it to its own class (§2.3); a holder's text climbs back over a first return
  as over a `⟲` (v1's `kids holds it`, §6); and §2.7's `hits` tells what is inside a path's subtree by prefix,
  since a fold can now land below a first return inside it.

*Amended 2026-10-31 (#1253): one position, one name.* On a cycle of two places or more, the rule above can
name one set of positions twice. In `T = T (List T)` the root is `T`, `#T.0` its list, `#T.0[*]` the first
return to `T` (a level's node) and `#T.0[*]#T.0` the first return to the list (that node's list). Built
step by step, the lists below it are `#T.0[*]⟲#T.0`: the step from `#T.0[*]#T.0` by `[*]` folds onto
`#T.0[*]⟲`, and its list is a step from there. A callee's `⟲` re-rooted at the list's first return
(`incTs`'s `[*]#T.0⟲` under `incT`'s `#T.0`) was `extend`'s direct `⟲`, `#T.0[*]#T.0⟲`: the same lists
under a second name. `incT`'s summary wrote one name and read the other (`RW` and `R`), and a call met
the written lists at the read path as another path of the argument. The rule is now:

- **A direct `⟲` names the levels as the walk does.** At a path that is not a `⟲` and not a sealed first
  return, the levels below it are `levelsOf` of it: the paths at its place one or more steps around its
  cycle, each as `extend` makes it. When there is one, `extend(p, ⟲)` is that path, so a callee's `⟲`
  re-rooted at a first return lands where a step-by-step walk lands (`#T.0[*]⟲#T.0`). At a sealed first
  return the levels are its own `⟲`, as before (`levelsOf` of it is `p⟲`), so `extend` is unchanged there,
  and `levelsOf` reads `extend` only at sealed paths, so neither calls itself.
- **Several level paths are a join.** Where the levels fold through more than one route,
  `levelsOf` gives several paths (`B (List B) (List B)`: below a level's list `#B.0[*]#B.0` they are
  `#B.0[*]⟲#B.0` and `#B.0[*]⟲#B.1`). `extend(p, ⟲)` stays `p⟲` there, the name of their **join**,
  because a path is one id and a cell names one path. `Place.levelPaths(p)` returns them when they are
  several, and three readers take each:
  - a projection of a leaf by `⟲` (`Shape.projectLeaf`) makes a symbolic cell at each level path, and a
    refinement's part one at each (`Cell.projectRefinedLevels`); a leaf's cells are a set, so the
    projection is one leaf holding all of them;
  - a graft of a callee's use at a join (`Walk.Graft.compose`) installs it at each level path
    (`Place.expandLevels`, which rewrites every `⟲` on a path that is a join and takes the steps after
    it again from each level path);
  - a call's written positions (§2.11 item 3) are the expansion of its write path.
  A reader that keeps one cell keeps the join (a refinement's `unrefined` cell, a demand's text, a use
  mark at a parameter's join path). `Cell.alias` reads a `⟲` on a cycle as overlapping every path of that
  cycle at its place, so the join is never taken as apart from the level paths it stands for.
- **Cost.** `levelsOf` is memoised per path and walks a place's strongly connected component once, so a
  direct `⟲` costs one memo hit after its first use; a join's expansion is the product of the joins on a
  path, one per `⟲`, and a canonical path has at most one `⟲` per first return (above). The K-wide build
  test is unchanged (1 814 / 2 038 records at K = 32, plain and through a `Maybe`; master 1 812 / 2 036).

### 2.2 Cells

*Replaced 2026-11-02 (#1685).* Cells — symbolic cells keyed by origin and canonical path, sites, results,
marks, their trie, their refinements and parts, and `Cell.alias` — were the shape domain's names for objects.
The slot domain names objects by **leaves** (§2.3.4) and compares them by **the one relation** (§2.9.2).
What this section required of cells holds of leaves: unknown provenance is `⊤`, never empty; an allocation is
one identity at every path (an atom); two values of one type are never one identity because of their type;
and a recursive slot names a family, never one object.

### 2.3 Abstract values: the slot domain

*Replaced 2026-11-02 (#1685, the owner: "That's enough prototyping. Start building this."). Until then this
section specified shape nodes (`leaf`, `node`, `delta`, `recast`, `union`, `choice`, `positions`, `view`,
`cyclic`), their widening, their stable images and their fold certificates. Generic `removeMin` could not be
checked inside the record budget with them (#1372, #1590), and two experiments refuted fixes inside that model.
The slot-domain experiment (branch `exp-slot-domain`, `c4a9db803`; Astra's second review §2, §6) passed, and
this section is now its domain. The old text is in git history; §2.9 and §2.11 were replaced at the same time.
Elsewhere in this document a "cell" of a value reads as a **leaf** (§2.3.4), a "node" as a **value**
(§2.3.3), a "κ condition" as a **selection** (§2.9), a "class" or "summary" as a **contract** (§2.10), and a
"call view" as a **call's instantiation** (§2.11).*

The local analysis computes, for each value of a frame, *where its objects can come from* and *which of them
may be the same object*, over a vocabulary that the types fix. It never builds a value's history. A value
is a small tree: what this frame built, with references at its leaves to subtrees of values it did not
build. Objects are named by **slots** (the type's canonical paths), at **positions** (the source's own
projections) of **roots** (the sources of values). One relation compares two leaves (§2.9), and one kind of
condition, the **selection**, states what that relation relies on.

#### 2.3.1 Slots

A **slot** is a canonical path of §2.1 from a root place. An **object slot** is a slot whose place holds an
object: a `record`, `list`, `dict`, `ref`, `closure`, `opaque` or `var` place. A `tuple`, `ctor` or `cross`
place holds none; its object slots are below it.

- **The canonical name of a slot** is its expansion through `Place.expandLevels`: a `⟲` that joins several
  level paths (§2.1, *One position, one name*) stands for each of them, and the steps after it are taken again
  from each. Two slots **meet** exactly when their expansions share a path. A **slot set** is a sorted run of
  expanded object slots, interned per module; two sets meet when the runs share an element, found by one merge.
- **`below(p)`**: the object slots at and below `p`, the closure of `p` under `extend` over each place's
  steps. It is one module table, filled once per path when first asked, and charged to every account
  that reads it, at the entry's stored fill cost on that account's own first read (§4.1, *A module table's
  entries*). A slot that holds a `var` place stands for anything below it.
- **The row slot** (§2.1, *The row of a record*) is an object slot at a `var` place, so `below` holds it and every reader of `below` needs nothing more.
- **Relative steps.** A contract (§2.10) names a parameter's or a result's slot by its step words from the
  root, `π2#Node.0⟲#Node.1`. Constructor steps are `(ordinal, argument)` pairs and field steps are field
  names, so the words mean the same in every module (§3.6).

A recursive slot (`⟲`) names a **family** of occurrences: every object one or more levels below. It never
names one object, and two values of one type never become one identity because their slots are equal.

*Amended 2026-11-02 (#1706, the manager's decision): a subtree held whole.* §2.1's paths fold only where a step
returns to a place already on the path, so a strongly connected group of types has a path for every order of
visiting it: `below(π1)` of a group of five types that each name every other one is a run of over 10⁸ slots
(`MutualCycles`; three types: 535 paths, four: 22 224). Written out, it passed the summary limit, while
master's v2 read the same deep read by prefix (`Place.hits`, §2.7's `Up(p)`). The naming of §2.1 is
unchanged; a slot set may now hold `below(p)` **symbolically**:

- **The symbol `↓p`.** A slot set is a sorted run of explicit object slots, then **exclusions** `¬q`, then
  **symbols** `↓p`. `↓p` is every object slot of `below(p)`. `¬q` takes the explicit slot `q` out of the
  set's symbols; it is kept only beside a symbol. `below(p)` is written out while it has at most
  `below_min` (16) object slots, and is `{↓p}` past that. *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714, the manager's
  decision):* whether it is past that is a column of the place graph, `Place.objectsBelow`: each place's
  count of the object places at and below it, saturating at `below_min + 1`, which it also is when a place
  on a cycle below it holds an object (a cycle unfolds into paths without end). It is set when the
  strongly connected components are settled: a component pops after every one below it, so a place on no
  cycle adds its children's counts, and a cycle that holds an object saturates. `below(p)` is `{↓p}` when
  the count at `p`'s place is past `below_min`, with no walk; else the walk fills it, counts a path's slots
  when it finds the path and still stops at the seventeenth (a `⟲` above `p` that stands for several level
  paths names each slot below once per level). It is filled once per path. A reader that reads a whole subtree through one key or one
  effect at its top (`below_min`, §2.10 *Read-off*) does so exactly when the set is `{↓p}`.
- **Anchors.** The anchors of `p` are `p` and `Up(p)` (§2.7: the `⟲` paths above `p` that its levels fold
  into, closed over theirs), each with its canonical names (`Place.expandLevels`). Every slot of `below(p)`
  lies at or under an anchor. Memoised per path.
- **Meet by prefix.** An explicit slot `q` is in `↓p` when an anchor of `p` is a prefix of `q`, and in a set
  when the set names it, does not exclude it, or one of its symbols holds it. Two symbols meet when an anchor
  of one is a prefix of an anchor of the other at or below which something holds an object. Two sets meet by
  one merge of their explicit runs and these tests for the rest; a symbol is never written out to meet. An
  exclusion is read against explicit slots only (a symbol meets a symbol whatever either excludes), and a
  union drops exclusions: both answer *may* where they cannot tell, never *apart*.
- **The other operations** read the symbol without writing it out. `below` of `↓p` is `↓p`. A family
  (§2.9.3) is a set holding a slot below a `[*]` or a `⟲`: for `↓p`, read off the place graph (a list's
  or dictionary's elements, or a place on a cycle, reachable from `p`'s place that hold an object). An effect
  on `↓p` is one deep effect at `p` (§2.10); a selection's occurrence at `↓p` is the **deep occurrence**
  `(j, p)*` (§2.9.1); a call's leaf at `↓p` is read through one key below `p` (§2.11.2); a holder's leaf
  without the target's slots keeps `↓p` with the target's explicit slots excluded (§2.8).
- **Written out where a contract names each slot.** A contract's result names its slots one by one (§2.10,
  §3.5): an arrival the same at every slot below a cast, a parameter's or a label's subtree read by
  structure, a constructor's or a worded declaration's identity and its occurrences, a call's arrival read
  slot by slot below an open entry. There `↓p` is written out (`belowAll`): the full walk of `below`,
  filled once per path and charged per account like it. An atom (`fresh`, `⊤`, a shared value)
  is the same at every slot and stays one wide entry. A wide entry for any other arrival is not used: read
  back over a call's result, it needs the call's whole subtree described by structure at each slot, which
  cost `Schema.shapeOf` 540 000 records where the slots written out cost 215 000 (measured 2026-11-02).
  Nothing on a deep read's path writes a symbol out: `MutualCycles` `f` and `g` check in 1 898 and
  1 805 records, and a group of n such types costs 359, 841, 914, 781, 918, 1 062, 1 215 records for
  n = 2…8 (1 906 at 12, 2 726 at 16). With the count in the place graph (2026-11-03), a K-wide recursive
  type costs `f` 456 / 568 / 792 records at K = 8 / 16 / 32, and 512 / 680 / 1 016 through a `Maybe`
  (900 / 1 411 / 2 371 and 1 620 / 1 812 / 3 156 with the walk).
- *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714, owed test (c)): a path read off its node.* A canonical path is a node of the
  trie (§2.1), and three facts about it are now part of the node, made with it in O(1): its **jump pointer**
  (a skew-binary list, Myers 1983: the parent, or the parent's jump's jump when the two spans below it are
  equal), whether a `⟲` is on its way (`levels`), and nothing else (the node stays 24 bytes: its depth and
  three flags share one word, the depth capped by `path_steps`). So `ancestorAt(p, d)` and a prefix test of
  two paths are O(log depth) reads, and the readers that charged a test of an anchor against a slot one record
  a step of their depth difference (`inBelow`, `subsMeet`, `hits`) charge the jumps read. A path with no `⟲`
  on its way is its own canonical name: `canon` reads it off the node, no walk and no table entry (one record).
  And whether `below(p)` holds a family is a column of the place graph, set with each strongly connected
  component as `objectsBelow` is (a member on a cycle that holds an object, an element that holds one, or a
  component below that does), one record, never a walk of the places below. A deep path's prefix tests, its
  canonical name and its family question no longer cost a record a step.

#### 2.3.2 Roots and positions

A **root** is a source of a value in a frame:

| Root | What it is |
|---|---|
| `param j` | parameter `j` of the frame; a lambda's or local function's captures are parameters after its own (§2.11.4) |
| `call k` | the result of the `k`th call site the walk evaluated; its objects are what the callee's contract says (§2.11) |
| `cb L` | the result of callback label `L` (§2.11.3): a call of a function this frame was handed |
| `site ι` | the object built by literal, record, constructor-record or lambda instruction `ι`, one per activation |
| `fresh k` | the objects call `k`'s callee allocated (one atom per call site: one allocation is one identity at every slot) |
| `shared d` | the top-level value `d` of some module; a write of it is refused (`top-level`, §2.8), and a cell it holds is written only behind its barrier (§2.13.7) |
| `⊤` | unknown provenance; never empty, and a write to it is refused `unknown` |

A **position** is a projection of a root by the source: `(root, parent position, step)`. A step is a plain
step of §2.1 (a field, a tuple index, a constructor argument, `[*]`, `◆`, `◇`), or a list step: `front i`
(the `i`th element from the front), `back j` (the `j`th from the back) or `slice a b` (the elements left after
`a` from the front and `b` from the back). A list pattern `[ x, …rest, y ]` binds `x` to `front 0`, `rest` to
`slice 1 1` and `y` to `back 0`. Positions are **normalised so that a slice is only ever the last step**:
`slice a b · front i` is `front (a+i)`, `slice a b · back j` is `back (b+j)`, and two slices add. A position's
**slot** is its parent's slot extended by the step (`[*]` for the list steps; a slice keeps its parent's
slot). Positions are interned per walk by `(parent, step)`, so two names bound to one projection share one
identity, and a position is never copied.

**Two positions of one root are related** when one is a prefix of the other, or when they may name one
element: at the first step where they differ, `front i` and `back j` are related (the list's length is not
known), `front i` and `slice a b` are related when `i ≥ a` (symmetrically for `back`), and two slices are
related. Every other difference (two fields, two tuple indices, two constructor arguments, two
constructors, `front i ≠ front j`) makes them **distinct**. Distinct positions are different places in the
structure. They hold different objects only where the root's **separation** (§2.9) holds: `Node l xs r` may
have `l` and `r` be one tree unless the caller separates them.
*Amended 2026-11-05 (#1956):* the plain step `[*]` and a list step at one parent are **related**: `[*]` names every
element, a `front`, `back` or `slice` one too. They were distinct, so `[ …l, p ]` with `p` bound to `front 0` of `l`
had its two copies of `p` apart under `l`'s separation, and an edit of position 0 changed position 1 in place
(PatternStoredBack's `viaL`: the sanitised run trapped; `[ …xs, el ]` likewise, `PushedPositions`' `editSpread`).
Sound because the objects at a `[*]` position are the elements, each list step's among them. To keep `[ el, …xs ]`
then `[ _, …rest ]` precise, a slice of a list literal with spreads drops the kids it skips before the first spread
and after the last (each stands at its own index), and holds every kid from a spread on (`Walk`). Fixtures:
`run/SanitiserPatternStoredBack` (refused) and `run/SanitiserPatternStoredBackApart` (`[ …rest, p ]`, and a slice
past a prepended element: accepted).
*Amended 2026-11-05 (#1963): one relation for the pairs and the indices.* The amendment above reached the pairwise
check only: three indices that file positions under their parent by the step that leads to them still kept `[*]`
apart from a list step. The distinct check's index (§2.9.3, past eight members) filed no plain step and asked only
the other list steps at a `front`'s parent, so `[ …l, a1, …, a6 ]` with `a1` the head of `l` was accepted and its
sanitised run trapped, while five fronts were refused; the holder buckets (§2.8, `Sweep.zig`) and the pending
operands (`Stack.zig`) asked no list step for a `[*]` and no `[*]` for a list step. Now one step relation
(`Steps.stepRel`) answers the first differing step for `Frame.related`, and every index of positions keeps one
protocol (`Steps.fileUnder`, `Steps.askFor`): lists per position, one for what is at it and one per class of the
step below it (`[*]`, another plain step, `front`, `back`, `slice`). A position is filed at itself and, at each
step's parent on its way, under the step's class; a query at `P` asks every list at `P`, and at each step's parent
on its way the list at the parent and the classes that may meet the step's (`Steps.meetClasses`). A unit test
checks that `meetClasses` lists exactly the classes of some related pair of steps, and that over a tree of every
step class the indices' storage (`Steps.PosLists`, the holder buckets' and the pending lists') and the distinct
check's keys meet every pair `Frame.related` relates, and an unrelated one only where a slice's indices part them. The call operands' index (`Holders.Operands`) asks
`Frame.related` itself, and the tag, route and descent indices (`TagTree`, `Coexist`, `Descent`, `HoldAt`) file no
position. Fixtures:
`run/SanitiserWideDistinct` (after the spread, before it, and from the back: refused) and
`run/SanitiserWideDistinctApart` (a slice and the fronts or backs it skips, as wide: accepted).

#### 2.3.3 Values

A value is an entry of the walk's value table:

| Kind | Fields | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `scalar` | — | crossing: holds no object |
| `bot` | — | no value: the result of a recursive call whose candidate returns nothing yet (§2.12). Strict: a construction or a call with a `bot` operand is `bot`; a `case` drops a `bot` arm |
| `top` | — | objects of unknown provenance |
| `built` | `form`, `site`, `kids` | what this frame built: a tuple, a constructor application (`form` = its head), a list literal, a record, a closure (§2.11.4). A list, record or closure has the `site ι` object as its own storage; a tuple and a constructor have none |
| `ref` | `root`, `position`, `family` | the subtree at a position of a root. `family` is a slot set when the value was reached through a step the position cannot name exactly (a `[*]` of a family, a `⟲`): every object at those slots, at or below the position |
| `alt` | `choice`, `arms` | one value of several, by the arm that ran (§2.3.5) |
| `shared` | `d` | a top-level value |

*Amended 2026-11-06 (#2143, #2149): as built, no value has a `family`.* `Walk.Walker.project` sets one only from one, so every
position names its step exactly, and a `⟲` or a `[*]` is a position of its own slot. §2.14 reads no family.

*Amended 2026-11-03 (#1713): a top-level value that holds no object.* A reference to a parameterless
declaration whose contract returns and says no arrival at any slot (`Dict.empty`, which is `Dict Leaf`) is `scalar`,
not `shared d`: there is no object to name, so a write a callee makes of a slot below it (`#Dict.0#Node.2`, a path
the value does not have) names nothing, where it was refused `top-level` (`run/SanitiserEmptyValue`). A value whose
contract has an arrival, or that has none yet (a group still solved), stays `shared d`; a parameterless `foreign` is
`host` (§2.10, *host objects*).

Projection by a step: a `built` value gives its kid (a list literal's `front i` its `i`th item, `[*]` an `alt`
over its items keyed by the literal); a `ref` gives the child position (or, for a family, the family
extended by the step); an `alt` projects each arm and keeps its choice; `scalar`, `top` and `shared` give
themselves. A projection that cannot match (another constructor of a literal) gives `bot` in that arm.

#### 2.3.4 Leaves

The **leaves** of a value are its objects, each said once:

| Leaf | Names |
|---|---|
| `ref(root, position, slots, tags, at_position)` | the objects at `slots` (a slot set) inside the subtree at `position` of `root`. `at_position`: the leaf is the position's own storage only (a shallow write target) |
| `site ι`, `fresh k` | the atom's objects |
| `shared d` | the top-level value's objects |
| `⊤` | unknown objects. With an **origin** `v`, a value of the frame: objects inside `v` that no slot names |
| `host` | objects JavaScript made, beni objects that escaped (§2.10, *host objects*), or what a top-level value's call answers and no block names (§2.11.1): a `foreign`'s unknown result, an escaped object a callee answers, or such a call's result |

A deep read of a value reaches every leaf of it: for a `ref`, `below` of its slot, a symbol `↓p` past
`below_min` slots (§2.3.1). **Shallow storage and
payloads are different slots**: a list's own storage is the list's slot, its elements are its `[*]` slot, so a
write of a list's storage meets an element only where the element is a list of that slot. Leaves are interned
per walk; `tags` is a tag set (§2.3.5).

*Amended 2026-11-02 (#1714): a value's leaves are part of the value.* Until then every reader that wanted a
value's deep leaves walked the value's kids again: a read-off pass read each use's value deep, the holder
index listed each binding's leaves, and a value built over another (`r₁ = Rose [ r₀ ]` … `rₙ`) was walked
once per use, Σ depth = n² records (`Rose [ r ]` at 10 / 40 / 160 levels: 892 / 8 234 / 109 836). A value
that two kids share (`( t, t )`) was walked once per route, 2ⁿ. Master's v2 kept a persistent reach set per
node. The slot domain now does the same:

- **The leaf set.** Every value carries its **leaf set**, made with the value from its kids' sets (kids are
  always made before their parent) and never recomputed, and a second set, its **storage**'s (a shallow
  write's targets). A set is a persistent set over a leaf's id **with no tags**: a big-endian Patricia tree,
  its nodes hash-consed per walk, so equal contents are one node, a set built over a kid's shares the kid's
  nodes, and adding a leaf copies at most one path (33 nodes). An element is `(leaf, routes, many)`: its
  **routes** are the tag sets under which it is reached (§2.3.5), and `many` says that two routes that
  coexist reach it (one value placed twice, *saturated at two*). Records: one per node made or met, reserved
  before it is made; a join of two sets that share a subtree pays for the path to it, not for the subtree.
- **What each value's set is.** `scalar`, `bot`: empty. `top`, `shared`: their one leaf. `ref`: one
  element whose slots are named when the set is read: `below` of its family or of its position's slot
  (§2.3.1) for the leaf set, the family or the position's own canonical slots for the storage. A position
  whose place holds no object has an empty leaf set. So a set made with every projected position walks no
  `below` that nothing reads: a crossing tuple of 2¹⁶ type variables at a call's result is never walked,
  and `MutualCycles`' `f` keeps its 1 898 records (named eagerly, 26 660). `built`: its site's leaf, the
  storage of the value it is built over (a list construction, §2.13.2), and every kid's set, joined as
  coexisting; its storage is its site's leaf and its base's. `alt`: §2.3.5. **Coexisting join**: a leaf in
  both sets keeps both sides' routes, and is `many` when a route of one side and a route of the other can
  hold together.
- **A deferred storage.** The storage of a prepend `[ x, …xs ]` is `xs`'s base only where the item put in
  front may be a re-cons (§2.13.6, `prepended`), which a call's contract decides, and a walk makes values
  before an evaluation reads contracts. Such a storage is the set's element `recons ι` (a leaf of its own
  kind): a reader replaces it with the base's storage when the evaluation says the prepend may re-cons,
  and with nothing otherwise. The rest of the set is the same in every evaluation.
- **Reading.** A deep read of a value is its set's elements, one leaf per route with the reader's outer
  tags merged in (a route that conflicts with them is dropped); a `many` element is two entries of the
  distinct check (§2.9.3). A **pass** that reads many values' leaves for one purpose (the read-off's deep
  reads, §2.10) visits each set node once: a node met again in the pass with no outer tags adds nothing,
  since every leaf below it was taken. *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714):* nor does one met again under outer
  tags that cannot filter it. Each node keeps its **span**, the earliest and latest choice that filters an
  element below it (its wraps' tags, its route wraps' and its leaves' routes), made with the node; a leaf
  whose reading merges the reader's tags in (a call's or a supply's, expanded under them, or a deferred
  storage) spans every choice. Outer tags whose choices all lie outside the span drop no element, so the
  node gives the keys it gives with no outer tags, and a pass's reader keeps the keys (a parameter's read
  is its slots), not their tags: the pass takes it once. Without it, an inline chain `x_k = if c then
  x_{k-1} else [ 1 ]`, every node of `x_{k-1}` under `x_k`'s wrap, read all k leaves at each use (Σk:
  24 988 / 225 397 / 2 846 209 records at 100 / 400 / 1 600 links; now 14 992 / 65 401 / 286 213). Each
  node carries one bit, whether a leaf below it is a `ref` or a
  deferred storage, and the pass skips a node without it (a read reads parameters' objects only), so a
  tower of literals costs its parameters' leaves, never its atoms. A pass never fills what is kept: an
  instantiation or an expansion (§2.11.2) made under it is made whole.

*Amended 2026-11-05 (#2069): a `⊤` keeps what it lies inside.* A step no place names (§2.1) gives a `⊤` whose origin is the value it stepped from, and the origin is part of the leaf,
so it goes wherever the value goes: into a record, a literal, a cell, a capture, a callee's argument. A `⊤` on the value alone was lost at the first of these, since `project` makes a leaf per read.
A write of it stays `unknown`, and an overlap stays `may`. Three readers read through the origin, each at its deep leaves under the leaf's tags, the rest of its use being `⊤`'s as ever:

- **A run** (`FnRun`): every object of the origin goes, whole, wherever its slots stop, since no slot says which one runs. So a step a record place cannot name (§2.1, *A step no place names*) is covered with a fold's.
- **A read-off** of a result or a supply (`ReadOff`): the `⊤`'s arrivals, and the origin open at that slot, so a caller that runs `pick t` reads its own argument there. Sound by O1: a holder is added, never removed. Precise as before, since a `⊤` result already overlaps everything.
- **An escape** (`ReadOff.paramEffects`): the origin's objects escape with it, or a caller's closure handed on through a cell would be nobody's. A write of a `⊤` adds no write effect: it is refused where it stands.

This is the value's representation, not a memo: a set is made exactly once, when its value is, and stored
in a column of the value table by the value's id (§3.3).

#### 2.3.5 Choices as tags

A `case` value is an `alt` keyed by the `case` instruction, the **choice**, with one arm per branch that can
return. Projections keep the key, and the leaves of an arm carry the **tag** `(choice, arm)`. Two leaves whose
tags give one choice two different arms never coexist: the relation of §2.9 answers *no* for them. Two
different choices are never compared arm by arm. So `if c then ( p, [] ) else ( [], p )` keeps its two parts
apart, and `( if c then p else q, if c then q else p )` does not, since its two `if`s are two choices. A `[*]`
projection of a list literal is a choice keyed by the literal: one element at a time.

Joins at a `case` keep each arm's value whole; they never merge arms' leaves into one set, so a separation
that holds in every arm holds of the `alt`.

*Amended 2026-11-02 (#1714): a leaf reached by several routes keeps every route, once.* Until then a reader
enumerated an `alt` DAG as a tree, so one object reached through two arms was two leaves, and a tower whose
level is a choice of the level and the level below (K, `rₖ = if c then Rose [ rₖ₋₁ ] else rₖ₋₁`) multiplied its
leaves by four a level (n = 8: 744 671 records; master's v2 5 431 at n = 5 and 10 152 at 8). Now:

- **A tag names a set of arms.** A tag is `(choice, arms)`: the leaf is there only when one of `arms` ran.
  An arm's leaves gain `(choice, {arm})`. Two tags of one choice hold together when their arms meet, and
  together they are the arms they share; a tag naming every arm of its `alt` says nothing and is dropped.
- **Routes.** An element's routes are a set of tag sets, interned. Two routes that differ only in one
  choice's arms are one route over the arms of both, and a route that another implies (a tag of each of
  its choices, with fewer arms) is dropped: it answers *no* to less. Nothing is dropped for size, so the
  routes say exactly when the leaf is there.
- **An `alt`'s leaf set** is its arms' sets: what every arm has alike (one node, by hash-consing) is kept as
  it is, and the rest of each arm gains its arm's tag before the arms are joined. A leaf that several arms
  reach under one route ends with that route and a tag of those arms, so a field that every arm of a wide
  `update` keeps but one is one route (`WideModel`), and a leaf every arm reaches alike costs nothing: K
  costs a level's own leaves. `many` is the arms' maximum, never their sum: two arms never coexist.
- **Why this is sound.** A leaf is read once per route, and a route holds exactly when one of the routes
  that reached it held: no *no* is answered that every route did not answer.
- **What it costs.** A leaf has as many routes as distinct ways its arms reach it; the arms-alike rule and
  the route join keep that at one for K and for wide updates. Tagging a set is one **wrap** node,
  `wrap(tags, set)`, opened one level only where a join looks inside it, and a join of routes compares a new
  route only with the ones it meets. K is linear: n = 8 / 16: 1 097 / 2 486 (master's v2: 10 152 / 23 197).
- *Amended 2026-11-02 (#1714, the manager's decision: exact routes, shared, never merged):* **routes share
  their tails.** A leaf that every `then` arm of an `else if` chain of D arms reaches has D routes of up to
  D tags; written out one by one they cost the chain D² to D³ records (D = 8 / 16 / 32 / 64: 3 468 /
  14 998 / 87 023 / 598 764). Every route is still kept; what changed is how routes are stored:
  - *A tag set is a list* of `(choice, arms)` pairs sorted by choice, earliest first, one node per
    `(pair, tail)` by dense id, hash-consed (`Routes.zig`). An enclosing `case` is made after its arms,
    so its choice comes later: a reader going down a set meets the outer wraps first and puts each inner
    tag in front of the list it has, and the leaves below one wrap share its tags as their tail. A merge,
    a conflict test or an implication walks two lists only to where they meet. *Amended 2026-11-03:* a
    list also has a jump pointer down its tail (Myers’ skew-binary rule, one word a node), so a conflict
    test passes a run of one list’s choices the other does not name in steps logarithmic in its length.
  - *A wrap inside a wrap* is kept as two wraps when every choice of the inner one comes before the outer
    one's, so tagging a tagged set is one node; opening a set pushes its wraps down one level, innermost
    first.
  - *An element's routes are a route set* by dense id: `flat`, a normalised run of lists; `wrap(tags,
    set)`, every route of a set with an enclosing choice's tags after it (one node, where every choice of
    the tags comes after the set's); `join`, the routes of an `alt`'s arms. An arm's routes join
    another's only where they are one node under both (`wrap`s of one set, whose tags `combine` or one
    implies the other), and a set that holds the unconditional route is that route. A reader walks a set
    from its top, outer tags first, so the routes it lists share their tails too. Coexisting joins write
    both sides out and normalise them, as before.
  - *The distinct check reads the lists' shape* (§2.9.3): two entries of one atom whose lists part at two
    pairs of one choice with no arm in common never coexist, and are not merged.

  The chain is then linear: D = 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 256: 2 204 / 4 524 / 9 339 / 19 208 / 39 431 /
  80 720 records (×2.05 a doubling), and a call over it (`chainCallCold`) 1 967 / 3 711 / 7 159 / 13 975
  (before: 2 617 / 8 445 / 42 717 / 287 821). K costs 1 149 / 6 727 at n = 8 / 32 (before: 1 097 / 6 135).
  No verdict and no summary moved over the 2 177 roots.
- **Walks over a value's structure.** The read-off's `describe` (§2.10) visits each `(value, result slot)`
  once: it reads no tags and its arrivals are a set. A projection of a whole `alt` read deep is the alt's
  leaf set. A holder's paths (§2.8, `Resolve.holds`) still walk the structure: that is the holder lane's.
- *Rejected, measured.* The tags common to every route (an intersection, the #1714 report's proposal)
  changed no verdict over the 2 177 roots, but weakened the result separation of nested `case`s whose inner
  arm keeps the outer value to `no` (`dropWhile`, `SameVariant.update`). Two routes, intersected past two,
  still weakened `UnknownElements.update`. Neither is used.
- *Specified 2026-11-03 (#1714, the manager's decision): a key's leaf carries its route set.* An instantiation's
  leaf (what a key of §2.11.2 holds, `instAt`/`instBelow`, and what `Eval.expand` gives) is a `Value.Leaf`
  whose field `routes` is a route set of this section, **relative to the leaf's `tags`**, 0 for none: the
  same field and the same meaning as a write target's (`Routed.ofWrites`) and a projection's output
  (`Relation.Proj.routes`). The leaf stands for the leaves `l` with `tags := tags ⊓ r`, one for each route
  `r` of the set (a route that conflicts with `tags` stands for none); `routes = 0` is the leaf under its
  tags alone, as before.
  - *Made by* the projection of an arrival `π_j·s` onto argument `j` (`arrivalLeaves`). Its walk is the
    selection's walk (§2.11.2, *a projection carries a route set*) with `⟲` one of its shared steps: the
    descent items `(value, place, below)` below a `⟲` are merged under route sets as the path items are. A
    key reads no literal route, so there items merge whatever their literal routes; where routes are read
    (the distinct check's own projections) the literal route stays part of the item. Each output is one
    leaf, its set the item's.
  - *Identity.* A leaf's id includes `routes` (`Frame.leaf`), so a key holds a leaf once per route set; two
    sets for one leaf are two leaves of the key, never united after the walk. A key is a set of leaves under
    conditions, as it was: an object a key names under two routes is one object at that slot, whose routes
    say when it is there, not two occurrences of it.
  - *Exactness.* Written out (`writtenOut`: one leaf per route, `tags` that route merged with the leaf's,
    `routes = 0`), a key's leaves are the leaves it held before, up to `internRoutes`' normalisation (two
    routes that differ only in one choice's arms are one route over both, a route another implies is
    dropped): the same objects under the same conditions.
  - *Readers.* `Eval.expand` gives the leaves **written out**, so every reader that reads `tags` alone gets
    what it got before: correct, not yet cheaper. `Eval.expandRouted` gives them with their sets, for a
    reader that reads them: the read-off (it reads no tags), `AtomSets` (atoms by identity), and the
    distinct check, whose entry from such a leaf is the leaf without its set, under the set as its routes
    (`Entries.Ent.routes`); where the parent entry has routes too, the leaf is written out under the
    parent's. A reader switches by calling `expandRouted` and reading `Leaf.routes` (`Coexist.setsMeet`
    of `tags` and `routes`), or by writing out where it needs lists (writing out is the old cost again).
    The holder lane's readers (`Holders`, `Sweep`, `Later`, a `Hold`'s routes) switch on their side.
