  - *As built (#1714, 2026-11-03), the values lane's side.* The walk is `RouteWalk.zig` (L8, split from
    `Routed`, which keeps the write targets and `writtenOut` at L9). A descent item is `(value, ⟲'s index,
    place, origin, below)`; an `alt`'s arms below a `⟲` add no tag, as `projectLevels`' do. Where no
    literal route is read (`Eval.no_routes`) the walk takes a built value's steps itself, so arrivals merge
    below it too; a value with no arm or part is `project`'s alone. `arrivalLeaves` reaches the walk through
    `Eval.routed` (`RouteWalk.paramLeaves`, set by an evaluation: `Relation` is below it). The distinct
    check's expansion, the read-off and `AtomSets` call `expandRouted`; the relation's own expansions
    (`overlap`, `heldBy`, `apartOf`) keep the written-out `expand`. An item is charged once: a merge when it
    arrives, a walked item when it is read, an emitted one by `project`. Measured (Debug), the fold
    certificate through a shared DAG (`d_N`, `incAll (same x_N)`): 2 762 / 8 236 records at N = 4 / 8 are
    2 295 / 5 723 (28 742 at 16). The part outside the holder lane's judgement is 2 032 / 3 708 / 8 423
    (×1.8, ×2.3 a doubling). Its demands are 263 / 2 015 / 20 319, because `Holders.Walker.open` reads the
    key written out: N³/6 routes of about N tags, each one built again. **The test passes when the holder
    readers read the sets.** The ledger (2 196 roots) moves no verdict and no summary, and no limit line. No
    account grows worse (48 better). Totals: 281 up, 7 810 down. Every row of the cost table is down, with
    the same growth.

### 2.4 The state of a frame

*Amended 2026-11-02 (#1685).* In the slot domain a frame's state is its walk's tables (§3.3): the value of each
local and its binding point, the pending operands, the uses, the demands, the escapes as `(leaf, point)` and
the calls' instantiations. `contents` (the cell-slot relation of §2.13.7) is read through the cell words'
contracts (§2.13.6). An escape marks every leaf of the escaped value, deep; a target is escaped when it or a
leaf it is inside (a position's ancestor, the same atom) escaped at a compatible earlier point.

A frame is a declaration body or a lambda body (oc §7.3):

- `Σ`: the **binding log** `(local, NodeId, KappaId)`, append-only; a local is bound once and lexically scoped, so a `case`
  joins arm values but not SSA binding logs (§2.6); the log, `taken` and `pending` are popped to the mark
  taken at an arm's start. In-scope bindings at a point = the log segments of its enclosing regions (§2.5).
- `contents`: the versioned cell-slot relation `contents(handle-origin, ◆)` (§2.13.7). Fork its root at a
  branch, apply ordered slot effects in each arm, join possible contents at the continuation; unlike SSA
  binding logs this state MUST join. A loop/group propagates slot memberships and ordered effects to its
  settled post-fixpoint before writes/loans are judged.
- `Esc`: the monotone set of `(cell, point)` escapes (thesis §3.4). **Escape is deep and directional**: escaping a
  node marks every cell in `reach(n)` (once per node, memoised); a cell is *escaped at p* when it or any trie
  ancestor of it (a symbolic prefix or a refinement's parent; concrete containment needs no link because escaping a node marks its `reach` eagerly) escaped at a
  compatible point before `p`. A *deep* demand (send, `consumed`, focus) is also blocked by an escaped descendant;
  a storage write is not (a callback keeping a list stored inside the accumulator does not refuse writes to the
  accumulator, R-5.2.5 #749). O8.
- `taken` (§2.2), `pending` (operands evaluated whose consumer has not run), `uses`, `demands`, `supplies` (each
  call of a function parameter: the point and the nodes handed, §2.11).

### 2.5 Regions and points

A **point** is an instruction index. `Regions.zig` reads the region tree off the BIR once, using
subtree starts for a forward `let` body and retaining actual sibling-arm exclusions in virtual
`withDefault` regions (a virtual continuation does not make every later sibling compatible): a region per `case` arm,
`let` body and lambda body (a frame boundary), with `start`, `end`, `parent`, its case, and for an arm its *guard*
when the scrutinee is `i == e`, a `method_call` of `eq` `Dispatch` resolves to `Int`'s (§2.13.15). Two points are **compatible** when neither lies in an arm of a
case the other lies in a different arm of (oc §7.2). The region tree is series-parallel: a case's arms are parallel,
everything else is in sequence. `Regions` numbers a case's arms so that they tile the case's span after its
scrutinee, and gives each region `base₂`, its start in the **second order**, which lists every case's arms
(virtual `withDefault` arms included) in reverse. **Precondition: each case's arms are adjacent in the point
order**, so that they tile its span; `rank₂` is correct exactly where this holds. The pipeline form
`m |> Maybe.map f |> Maybe.withDefault d` lowers the `withDefault` reference between the map call and `d`; that
point lies between the arms, but it has no use and no demand, so no query asks about it and no compatibility
answer changes. A child region spans the same length in both orders, so a point
x directly in region r keeps its offset: `rank₂(x) = base₂(r) + (x − start(r))`. A series-parallel order has
dimension two, so for points p < u, **p and u are compatible exactly when `rank₂(p) < rank₂(u)`**. "After `p`,
compatible" is therefore one threshold on `rank₂`, never a list of ranges (§2.7). The binary-lifting ancestor
slots of §4.1 answer the same test for a pair of points and name the case and arms that separate them.
In the virtual `withDefault (map m f) d` region the inner `map` call belongs to the f arm, so the two arms tile
the span from the f arm's first point to d's last. The call writes only through `f`, on a payload that exists only
when `m` matches, which is the f arm's case; so a demand at the call never has a write that d's uses could
observe, and making the call incompatible with d loses nothing. Without this, the call would be compatible with
both arms while the arms are not compatible with each other, which no pair of orders can express. S2's
`compatible` must give the call this answer, and S4's `MaybeDefault` and `ResultDefault` pin it. The `withDefault (map m f) d` shape (R-4.2.3) is marked by the BIR
pre-pass (§2.12) as a two-arm region, so it has arms in this tree.

### 2.6 Transfer rules

*Amended 2026-11-02 (#1685).* `Transfer.eval` is now `Walk.Walker.eval`, one case per BIR tag over the values of
§2.3.3; its value table, not a shape, is what each case returns. The table's rules stand with these changes:
`local`, projections and patterns give positions (§2.3.2); `lambda` and `let_def` with parameters are codes
(§2.11.4); `call` and `method_call` instantiate a contract (§2.11.2), or apply a label (§2.11.3);
`record_update`, `try`, `markup`, `type_dispatch` and the schema references are §2.11.5's. No tag is "not
built": every instruction has a rule, and an unknown callee has the pessimistic contract.

`Transfer.eval(frame, inst) → Value{node: NodeId, kappa: KappaId}`, one case per BIR tag, recording uses at the consumer (R-4.1.1) and demands
where §2.8 says:

| BIR tag | `A(inst)` | Uses | Demands |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local x` | `Σ(x)`; in a lambda, for an enclosing frame's local: the capture leaf `env x·ε` and `(x, ε)` added to the lambda's capture list | at the consumer | — |
| `field_access`, `tuple_index` | `proj(A(e), s)`; a lambda's capture is `(x, .f)`: per path (R-5.4.6) | at the consumer, kind `field` | — |
| `top`/`ext_value` (a value) | its summary's `res` with `shared M.v·q` for its own cells (§2.10); transferred `site`s under §2.13.11 | — | — |
| `top`/`ext_value` (function), `ctor`/`ext_ctor` (as a value) | a `closure` leaf `{site ι}` carrying the declaration's summary or the constructor's class (§2.13.1) | — | — |
| `int`, `float`, `char`, `string`, `chunk`, `interp`, `unit` | crossing (`∅`) | interpolated parts | — |
| `error` | `⊤`, operands escape | — | — |
| `list` (a literal) | `node(place, {site ι}, [*] ↦ join(items))`; κ per §2.9 | items at ι | — |
| a **spread chain** (§2.13.2; one BIR fact from `Lower`) | prepend or construction | items at ι | the construction (R-2.3) |
| `tuple`, `record`, constructor application | `node(place, cells, children)`; a record's cells `{site ι}` (R-4.8.1), a tuple's and constructor's `∅` | parts at ι | — |
| `record_update { r \| F = … }` | `delta(A(r), F ↦ values)`: the same object, written (oc §31.3) | `r` at every field but `F`, kind `field`; values at ι | `update` on `A(r)@ε` with `F`; nested updates are two (R-4.8.4) |
| `call` | §2.11; a call of a *function parameter* πⱼ at instruction ι: the result leaf `{cb j@ι·ε}` with the callee's class slot, each argument recorded as a supply `(j, label, k, node, κ, point)` and used at ε, kind `call` | per the class `use`, kind `call` | call-site demands, edges |
| `method_call` | the dispatch table's callee as `call`; a nullary method is a call (R-5.1.7); a field of function type is a call of the field's value reading only that field (R-5.5.7); unresolved → unknown (R-5.5.4) | as `call` | as `call` |
| `type_dispatch` | `⊤`; every operand's cells join Esc (as a wordless `foreign`, O1) | operands | — |
| `lambda` (also `f a _`, which `Lower` makes a lambda, `Lower.zig:2725-2733`) | a `closure` node: cells `{site ι}`, child `◇ ↦ env node` whose children are the captured `(x, q)`'s nodes at creation; the body walked now as its own frame → the lambda's class (§2.10). **Captures**: a *field* capture `(x, .f…)` is a **read at creation**, kind `field` (hoistable: a closure created after a write of that field reads the old value through the hoist, R-3.2; created before, it holds the field's value, not the record, and is no use of the record, R-5.4.6); a *whole* capture `(x, ε)` is a holder, used wherever the closure is consumed (R-5.4.1). A body writing a capture makes the closure **once** (R-2.8): its creation is a demand on each written capture | field captures at ι; whole captures at consumption | once demands |
| `let`, `let_def`, `let_pattern`, `let_stmt` | the body; a `let_def` with parameters is a local function (a frame in the block's local group, §2.12); `let_pattern` a one-arm case; `let_stmt` consumes its expression | the value at the binding | — |
| `case`, `branch` | per arm: the pattern's locals bound to projections/materialisations of `A(scrutinee)` (§2.13.3); the arms' values joined | the scrutinee, kind `whole` | — |
| `try` (`e?`) | the resolved success payload projected; the `failure`-marked payload (§2.13.6) joins the result of the definition `?` returns from (R-5.1.6) | `e` | — |
| `markup` | a call of the markup row (§2.13.8) | its values | — |
| `schema_*` references | a schema member or constructor: the pessimistic contract (§2.11.5, amended 2026-11-02) | — | — |

Arguments are consumed at the call, items before the base is written (R-4.1.3); every forwarded result is a use
at that point (R-4.1.4).

### 2.7 Uses and liveness

*Amended 2026-11-02 (#1685).* A `call` use names its callee's **footprint** for that argument (§2.10
`reads`) instead of a use shape: `Facts.Use.use_node` is the footprint's index in the walk's footprint runs.
A footprint entry `(s, deep)` is read at the argument's path extended by `s`; a deep entry reads every path
below it, and an arrival of the result reads its slot (the rule of *A part a callee answers*). A path that no
entry reaches is not read: `rkids r = r.kids` reads `π1.kids` and leaves `π1.v` free (R-4.8.2's untouched
fields). The exits on a cycle (*A read that leaves its path on a cycle*) are the footprint entries' `Up`
closures, as before.

*Amended 2026-11-02 (#1714):* whether a footprint reaches a path is two binary searches over the callee's
effects, which a contract stores sorted by parameter and canonical key (§2.10): one for an entry at or below the
path, one per proper prefix for a deep entry above it. Each costs ⌈log₂(E + 1)⌉ + 1 records, reserved before
its work. Before this, every use group scanned the whole effect list, uncharged.

*Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714):* a footprint is the callee's, not the call's. Calls of one callee (one code, or one
fixed contract) and one arity read an argument through one footprint, since an evaluation gives them one
contract, so their uses at one path are one **group** of the index and the filter judges the group once. Before,
each call had its own footprint and its uses were a group each: `len r` called after each of N writes of `r.fᵢ`
was N groups at `r`, and every write's query judged all of them (N = 64 → 256: 122 532 → 1 842 568 records).
A subtree query (*the table below*, a use under `q`) splits its range: the uses at `q` itself are filtered by
group, and the uses strictly below `q` are one `firstAfter`, because a footprint read at a path below the hold
always reaches the hold. That holds only where `q`'s place is not on a cycle; on a cycle a path below `q` can
fold back onto it, and the query filters the whole range by group, as before.

A **use** is `(atom, local, PathId, point, kind, callee-use-node?)`, where `atom` is the use occurrence: unique in
its declaration and deterministic, not the operand instruction, so one instruction reading a local twice has two
uses and the transfer rules of §2.6 need no change. Kinds: `field` (this frame's own field chain,
record pattern or field capture — **hoistable**), `whole` (a scrutinee, a comparison at the root, a store, a
return, a send, a whole capture at consumption), `call` (an argument: the callee reads it at the paths its class
`use` names — recorded once as `(local, p, use-node U)` and answered lazily by projecting `U` along the queried
remainder, a node marked `D` on the way answering for every remainder below it (§2.10); **never hoistable**,
since the read happens inside the callee: R-4.8.2 bullet 4, R-4.8.7). Uses are
keyed by **path**, never by place (two fields of one record type share a place).

**The index** (`Liveness.zig`, §3.4a): per `(local, PathId)` the uses sorted by point; each use is stored once at its own path.
Paths are ordered lexicographically by their steps, so a path's subtree is one contiguous range and no use is
copied to an ancestor. Construction gives every canonical path node that an indexed path passes through its rank
in that order and its subtree's rank interval, once, so a query navigates by one-word comparisons of ranks and
never rereads a path's steps. Per-local last-use and range-index nodes use the one-key lanes of §4.1. A query
descends the range index explicitly; every node and candidate it visits is a retained query task, classified
before work into §4.1's direct-demand query lane or growth.

**Compatibility is a threshold.** Each index entry carries its use's `rank₂` (§2.5), and each merge-sort node keeps
a max tree over the `rank₂` of its pairs. "The first use of this range after p and compatible with p" is then one
descent: a binary search past p by point, and a max-tree search for the first `rank₂` above `rank₂(p)`. Every
candidate it returns is compatible, so a nested `case` produces no region intervals and no rejected incompatible
candidate. The binary-lifting ancestry query (§4.1) decides the same relation for a pair in hand: a holder's use in
`Demands`, a keep edge.

**One query per prefix.** A demand reads its path once. For the direct holder (the base's own local at the written
path q = s₁…s_d), the query for prefix q_i = s₁…s_i is one rank lookup (q_i is q's trie ancestor, so no step is
compared) and one exact-run descent, both on step s_i's own direct-demand lane (§4.1). The subtree query at q, or at
q·f for each written field f ∈ F, is one rank-interval descent on the last step's lane or on f's; a `call`
candidate's use node is tested at q·f on f's lane too. **Per demand,
the direct holder costs d + |F| direct-demand kernels, each O(log² U) fixed-word work in its own baseline lane:
no growth, whatever d and the case nesting depth.** Up to two further holders per
demand are baseline as well: in `let items = model.items in { model | items = List.push items x }`, `model` also
holds the written cell. Each runs the same prefix queries over the path at which it holds the cell, on the lanes
of §4.1's *holder and callee path words*. Separately reserved: a `call` candidate the kind filter rejects (its
use node empty at the remainder of q), holders beyond those two, a joined or deep cell set's further cells, and
inferred alternatives. These are §4.1's demand×use and demand×holder products.
Queries at a demand point `p` for holder `(h, q)` of cell `c`:

| Query | Lists | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| a use of `h` at an ancestor of `q` or at `q`, after `p`, compatible | `(h, q')` for each prefix `q'` of `q` | a whole use (`later-use`/`alias`); a `call` use counts the same when its node `U` is non-empty at the remainder of `q`, or (record demand) at `q·f` for some `f ∈ F`, or when `U` has a node marked `D` or `A` at a prefix of that remainder (§2.10: every demand at or below a deep read's path sees it; *A part a callee answers*, below); a use whose *exit* (below) is a prefix of `q` counts as one at `q`; a `call` use non-empty only at untouched fields is no use |
| a use under a written field `f ∈ F` (record demand) | subtree of `(h, q.f)` | kind `field` → a **hoist**; kind `call`/`whole` → a whole use, refused |
| a use under `q` (list demand) | subtree of `(h, q)` | a use |
| an untouched field's use | never read | — |

Query cost is the bound of *One query per prefix* for the direct holder; other holders and rejected `call`
candidates pay their own reserved tasks (§4.1). No bound solely by returned uses is asserted. `R-4.8.2`'s untouched
fields cost nothing.

**A read that leaves its path on a cycle** [M 2026-10-30, #1345]. The cover is by prefix: a use at `q` counts
for a hold at or below `q`. That is not enough where `q`'s place is on a cycle of the place graph. `extend`
folds a re-entry into the `⟲` of the deepest place on the path that the step re-enters (§2.1), and that place
can be *above* `q`. For `type Tree = Tree { v : List Int, kids : List Tree }` and `r` the record of a `Tree`,
every tree below `r` is reached through `r.kids[*]`, but its canonical path is `r⟲`, and `r.kids` is not a
prefix of `r⟲.v`. So `Debug.toString r.kids` after a push of a list that a tree below holds was accepted, and
v1 refuses it. A use therefore counts for the subtrees of its **exits** as well: the paths outside the subtree
being read at which `extend` puts what the use reads.

- **A deep read exits at `Up(p)`.** A read of every path below `p` — a `whole` or `field` use at `p = q`, a
  `call` use with no node, and a `call` use whose node `U` at the caller path `p` is a leaf with marks or is
  marked `D` (§2.10) — exits at `Up(p)`: the paths that `extend` reaches from `p`, step by step along `p`'s
  place's cycle, and that are not below `p`. Each is a fold target, `a⟲` for a prefix `a` of `p`, or `a`
  when it is a `⟲` already. The closure goes on from each target, because the levels below `a⟲` re-enter
  places further up. The cover below such an exit is free, as below a leaf.
  *Amended 2026-10-30 (#1253):* a fold target is now `a⟲` for `a` a first return (§2.1), which may be below `p`
  or above it, so `hits` tells what is below a path by prefix; and a sealed first return folds nothing
  outside itself, so `hits` does not walk its steps.
- **A `call` use's node is replayed in the caller's place graph**, as the graft replays it (§2.10, *Read-off*;
  `Walk.Graft`): from `q`, a step that `extend` folds out of the path being built, and a callee `⟲` at `p`,
  which lands at `levels(p)`, are exits with the callee node they lead to, and the cursor reads on from there. The
  levels of a sealed first return `a` (§2.1) are `a` and `a⟲`, taken whole, and the graft's levels are
  `Place.levelsOf`'s (#1253).
  `grand ts = case ts of [ Tree a ] → case a.kids of [ Tree b ] → List.length b.v` reads
  `π1⟲[*]#Tree.0.v`, which at the caller's `r.kids` is `r⟲.v`.

A hold at `f` is covered when `f` is a prefix of `q` or of an exit, or when `f` is below `q` or an exit and the
cursor from there accepts the rest of `f`. `⟲` names levels, not routes: `a⟲` holds what every route from `a`
re-enters. So the deep read of `r.kids` also covers a tree that a sibling field of `r` leads to, as if it were
below `r.kids`. That is the fold's abstraction (§2.1). It costs precision only where two fields of one record
reach one cycle; it costs no soundness.

**What it costs.** `Up(p)` is computed once per path in `Place.Table` and memoised. `hits(x)` is the fold
targets of `x`'s plain subtree on its cycle that are not below `x`, made from its plain children's, so each
canonical path of a cycle is visited once (on an explicit stack); `Up(p)` closes `hits(p)` over each target's
`hits`. Each request is one charged record, and a miss charges its steps and targets. A use's exits are made
once per `(path, use node)` in the holder index, by one walk of the use node, charged per node; a node whose
subtree has no place on a cycle has none. The descent of §2.8 step 3 does not follow exits: the cover of a
group that has one falls back to listing the holds (`hold listings`), as a folded step does. Fixtures:
`ownership/DeepReadCycle`, `ownership/DeepReadCycleImported` (v1's refusals: inline, through a helper, of
mutually recursive types, two levels below the cycle's entry, a whole use, a callee's `⟲` read; and a hold at
the root's own field, outside the read, accepted), `ownership/DeepReadCycleMutual` (a callee's read on a cycle of
two or three types, through `Maybe` and under a tuple, called at the root: an exit below `q` is kept, since a
callee on a mutual cycle keeps the route the caller folds into `t⟲`).

**A part a callee answers** [M 2026-10-31, #1370]. A `call` use reads its argument where the callee's `use`
names it, and the frame records no use for what it does with the call's result: the result is a temporary or
a new local, and neither is the argument's local. But the result holds every object the callee answers. So
the call is the last use of the argument's local, and the reads of the result that come after it must count
there. **A node of `U` marked `A` therefore reads every path below it, for the caller's liveness, as a
node marked `D` does.** That is the rule of a store or a binding (`x = k` is a whole use of `k`), applied at
the answered path. A path that the callee does not answer is not covered: `rkids r = r.kids` answers
`π1.kids`, and a hold at `π1.v` stays free. Before, `Debug.toString (idl k)` with a monomorphic
`idl : List (List Int) → List (List Int)` was accepted after a push of a list that `k[*]` holds, and so was
`case idl k of [ y ] → List.length y`, which reads the pushed list itself. v1 refuses both. A polymorphic `idl`
was refused only because its `π1` has a type variable's place, where the cursor finds no step and is free.

The rule is the liveness readers' only: the holder index's cursor (`Holders.stepCursor`) and the exits
(`Exits.deep`, so an answered path on a cycle exits at `Up(p)` too). Read-off composes the callee's `use` as
it is, and a parameter part that the result holds is read where the result is consumed, by `readsOf` (#1352),
so no class changes. The precision lost is that of the binding: `List.length (idl k)` reads `k` deeply
after the push, as `x = k; List.length x` does. Fixtures: `ownership/AnsweredRead`,
`ownership/AnsweredReadImported` (v1's refusals: read deeply, through a constructor's record and a field,
bound first, in a construction, through `▷`, by a deep-reading callee, through a pattern, and on a cycle; a
hold at a path the callee does not answer, accepted).

### 2.8 Demands and the check

A **demand** is `(point, kind, base NodeId, F, operands, pending, deep?)`; kinds: `writer` (R-2.1, R-2.4, R-2.12),
`construction` (R-2.3), `append` (R-2.2: one demand per `++` chain with the leftmost base), `update` (R-2.5),
`callsite` (R-2.6), `send` (R-2.9, deep), `once` (R-2.8), `entry` (R-2.10), `consumed` (R-2.11, deep), `focus`
(R-2.12), and `transfer` (§2.13.18, deep over backing identities only; 2026-11-02).

**Resolution on slots** (*replaced 2026-11-02, #1685*; the holder index of #1214 over cells, its pairs, its
sweep and its cross-check went with the shape domain). A demand is resolved offline, after the walk, when
every use, holder and pending operand of the frame is known. Its **targets** are leaves (§2.3.4): for a
storage write, the base's own storage at the written position (`at_position`); for a deep demand (`consumed`,
`send`, `focus`), every leaf of the base. In cause-precedence order (R-4.3.6):

1. **Known.** No target is `⊤` (`unknown`), and none is a loan (§2.13.7).
2. **Unescaped.** No target was escaped at a compatible point before the demand (§2.4; for a deep demand, nor
   anything below it); no target is `shared` (`top-level`), nor the model of `view`/`subscriptions`
   (`read-only`).
3. **Not captured.** No target is a capture written outside its `once` closure's frame (`captured-edit`).
4. **Disjoint.** No other operand of the instruction overlaps a target (§2.9.2): another argument, another
   path of the written argument that the callee reads, a field value of an update. `may` refuses
   `disjoint`; `under` is relied on.
5. **Dead.** No pending operand overlaps a target at a path its consumer touches (`held-operand`); no local
   bound before the demand and used after it, compatibly (§2.5), overlaps a target at an overlapping path
   (`later-use` for the base's own local, `alias` for another, `captured` for a closure holding it). A
   holder's overlap is found by the relation of its value's leaves with the targets; the path at which it
   holds a target is the holder's own path to that leaf (through what it built, then the leaf's position and
   the meeting slot), and the liveness index (§2.7) answers whether it is used there or above after the
   demand. Holders are indexed by root: a target of root `R` is compared with the leaves of `R` only, and a
   call's leaves are expanded into the roots they come from first.
6. **Exclusive.** What the overlaps relied on (§2.9.4): a selection of the frame's parameters is accepted
   `param` and added to `req`; anything else that is not given is refused `exclusive`.

**Base keys** (#1714, 2026-11-02). A leaf's *base keys* are what it comes from: a parameter for a parameter's
`ref`, the atom for a `site`, `fresh` or `shared` leaf, *unknown* for `⊤`, an answer or a callback's root, and
for a call's or a supply's leaf the union of the base keys of its expansion (§2.9.2 step 4). They are part of
the leaf's representation, two columns by leaf id made after the walk by a post-order (Tarjan) pass over the
expansions, strongly connected leaves sharing one entry, so each leaf is expanded once a column. The **facts**
are one word: whether the leaf reaches unknown objects, whether it reaches a parameter's, and the least shared
value it reaches by `(module, declaration)`, the one a `top-level` refusal names. Step 1 and the ground read
the facts, made for every target. The **run** of keys (sorted, once each) is made only for a target that meets
a live holder, a holder a demand meets live, and an escape's leaf: a value that comes from k atoms has k keys,
and a chain `x_k = step x_(k-1) [ k ]` would cost Σk to key every leaf. None of the readers expands a call
again. A run is copied from its kids' runs only while it has at most `flat_max` (32) keys and no kid's
keys are shared; past that a leaf's keys are a **shared set** (`KeySets.zig`, #1714, 2026-11-03): a hash-consed
big-endian Patricia tree over the keys' dense ids, the union of its own keys and its kids' sets, so a kid's set
is never copied and a set and its subset unite into the set itself. A set is listed (its keys sorted) only when
a reader asks for it, once a set. A chain of n leaves, each over the one below plus one key, costs a path a
level and not Σk items: #1146's chain of knots through calls and #1130's 400-call chain read at its end are
linear (`build_test.zig`). Charged: a node made or found is one `set`, a pair of nodes a union meets one
`inspection`, a key listed one `edge`.

**The holder index and its sweep** (#1714, 2026-11-02; #1214's live chains, restated on slots). Step 5 asks
only the holders that are *live at the demand*: bound before its point and used after it (`Liveness.lastUse`).
Each local is indexed under the base keys of its value's leaves; a local whose value reaches an unknown leaf
is indexed under the unknown key, which every target meets. Resolution judges its demands in point order (each line
keeps the walk's order, and the callback judgments of §2.11.3 are judged in the same sweep at their call's
point): a holder joins the **unkeyed list** when the sweep passes its binding point and leaves its lists when the
sweep reaches its last use. The first demand that meets live holders keys each unkeyed one, linking it into
its keys' **live lists**. The lists are doubly linked in flat arrays, the holders' and the `(key, holder)`
entries', so a join and a leave are O(1), and a holder no demand meets live is never keyed. The two orders
the sweep reads, by binding point and by last use, are counting sorts over the holders' own span of points. A demand's candidates are the live lists of its targets' keys, every parameter's
for a parameter's target (a parameter's object may be held through another parameter), and the unknown list:
O(the live holders it meets), never every holder its root ever had. In the push chain above, each demand meets
no holder at all: `a(i-1)` was last used by the push being judged. The holder index and the escape index are
built only for a frame that has something to judge (a demand or a label's supplied part): a tower of literals
with no write pays for neither (`Rose [ r ]` at n = 160: 59 279 records, 7 115 without them).

**Holder entries judged by base leaves** (#1714, specified and built 2026-11-03). The sweep still visits every
live candidate once per demand: k holders `oᵢ = Js.array [ Js.from (List.push zs i) ]` are candidates of each of
k pushes on `xs` (a parameter's object may be held through another parameter), `[ p1 … pn ]` bound from one list
and each pushed meets the n − i later `p`s, and `pᵢ = List.push r.fᵢ` meets every earlier `p`. Each pair costs a
`holds` walk and a liveness query, and answers the same `under`. The design that removes the product:

1. *Entries.* A holder's **entries** `(l, q)` are its value's leaves with the path at which it holds each, made
   once, when the holder is keyed, by one walk of the value (the leaf sets of §2.3.4 give the leaves; the walk
   gives the paths). `holds` stops walking the value per target.
2. *The factorisation.* For a target `t` that is a parameter's untagged `ref` leaf (not a cell's `◆`), and an
   entry whose leaf is not a `ref` of `t`'s own root (so §2.9.2 never refines its path by `t`'s slots),
   `overlap(l, t)` is the join over `l`'s **base leaves** (its expansion closed, as `Keys` closes it) of
   `overlap(b, t)`, since `t` is never expanded. A base leaf of another parameter answers `under H(b) ∪ T(t)`,
   `H(b)` the apart selection of `b`'s slots and `T(t)` the selection of `t`'s; an atom answers `no`; `⊤`, an
   answer or a label's root are judged as now. Neither selection is ever `no`.
3. *What is aggregated.* Such an entry never refuses (`may` needs a base leaf of `t`'s own root or `t`'s atom), so
   it only adds `H(l) = ∪ H(b)`, and `T(t)`, when it is live at the demand. The verdict needs none of it: only
   the frame's `req` does, over its *accepted* demands (§2.9.4). So step 5 visits per demand only the entries
   that can answer `may` or need a refined path: those of `t`'s own root, found by position ancestry and slot (as
   §2.9.3's index), those of `t`'s atoms, and the unknown bucket. The rest are judged per entry, not per demand:
   an entry's `H(l)` joins `req` when the first accepted demand inside its live range meets it live (one
   liveness query, the sweep's order), and `T(t)` joins when the demand meets any such entry live, which a
   per-key count of live entries answers.
4. *Ties.* The witness of a refusal is found among the visited entries only, by the order of *Verdicts*; no
   aggregated entry can be one.

*As built* (`Sweep.zig`, 2026-11-03). A holder's **holds** are listed once, when it is keyed: one walk of its
value (a node met again at the same path and tags is walked once), each hold a leaf, its path and whether the
path is refined by the target's slots; per demand a hold is judged against a target by the relation and the
refinement only (`Sweep.holdsAt`). A parameter's base key carries its base leaf's **position** (the escape index
folds it back to the parameter), and each parameter key's bucket is registered at its position and, below each
ancestor, under the class of the step that leads to it (a record a step, once a bucket; §2.3.2, *one relation
for the pairs and the indices*). A parameter's untagged
target (not a `◆`) at position `P` visits the unknown bucket and the buckets at positions related to `P`
(§2.3.2): at `P` or below it, at an ancestor, or below a list step of an ancestor that may name what `P`'s
step does. Every other live holder is an **aggregated** one for that target: each of its holds whose keys are
parameters' only answers `no` or `under` `H(l) ∪ T(t)`. The aggregated holders are on two lists, *pending*
and *done*. At a demand that is accepted, each pending holder not visited for the target has its pending holds
judged with liveness; a hold all of whose `under` paths are used after the point is done, and a holder all of
whose holds are done moves to the done list. When no pending hold was used after the point, the first done
holder that is adds its condition (`T(t)` with its own `H(l)`, which `req` holds already). So `req` is the
same union of selections as one judgement of every live pair, and an aggregated holder costs its pending visits
and, once done, nothing a demand that a pending one answers. A label's supplied part (§2.11.3) is judged with
no aggregation: its condition is its label's, not `req`.

*Use order* (2026-11-03). Step 4's witness is the hold used first (*Verdicts*), so a demand that is refused needs
only the holders that can be used before its witness. Each bucket is a heap of its live holders keyed by their
**next use** (a bound below every hold's use after the point: a holder's uses' points, sorted once, with a cursor
the sweep moves). A demand reads its buckets' heaps without changing them, by a frontier of heap slots in key
order: a slot's children enter when it leaves; a slot whose stored key is at or before the point enters again at
its holder's next use. Holders come in order of next use, each once, and the visit stops when the next one's key
is past the witness found so far: in `a_i = [ …v, ys ]`, `v`'s next spread is the witness and the earlier
`a_j`, used only at the end, are never visited. A sift is charged one record and one a swap, the frontier the
same. An accepted demand visits every holder of its buckets, as before. Measured (Debug, demands' records,
n = 25 → 100): `sites` 9 624 → 143 772 before, 1 871 → 7 968 now; `fields` 16 338 → 234 113, now 4 150 → 16 725;
`opaque` (`--core`) 78 097 → 1 228 389, now 6 121 → 25 787 (with the worded table of §4.1).

*Operands* (2026-11-03). Step 4 reads a call's other arguments the same way. A call's arguments' leaves are listed
once a resolution with their base keys (`Holders.Operands`); a leaf whose keys are parameters' only is aggregated.
A write of argument `j` at a parameter's untagged target judges one by one only the other arguments' leaves that
are not aggregated and those of its target's parameter at related positions (by binary search over the call's
`(parameter, position)` keys); `T(t)` joins when one aggregated leaf answers `under`, and at the end of the
resolution each aggregated leaf adds its own selection once, through a write of another argument of its call that
was accepted. A recursive call of `rot a1 … an k` handed `rot a2 … an a1 (k − 1)` made n writes of n − 1 operands
a round for n + 2 rounds: `GroupRotate` at n = 16 / 32 / 64 cost 110 353 / limit / limit, now 28 921 / 106 762 /
411 591 (growth 56 748 of 65 536: the rounds remain, each linear in n). An aggregated holder is also asked first
whether its local has any use after the point compatible with it, one range query, before a liveness query per
hold: in the `then` arm, the parameters the `else` arm's call reads are live by the sweep and never used.

*Targets as paths* (#1714, 2026-11-03, owed test (c)). A demand's target and a holder's hold are a parameter's
path, a node of the trie, never re-derived from a position by its steps: (1) a hold of a leaf held at the leaf's
own position's slot (the holder is the parameter, bound at its root) holds a target of the same root at the
target's own path when no `⟲` is on that path's way: a prefix test by jumps, never `relBelow` and a replay;
(2) a liveness query (§2.7) asks the prefixes of the hold's path only as deep as the holder's deepest use
(`Liveness.Index.deepest`, a column of the index), reached by the path's jumps, and a subtree query of a path
deeper than every use of the holder answers none at once; (3) a use group's filter (a call use's footprint) is
asked only of a group that has a use after the point, earlier than the best found. Each answer is the one the
step-by-step reading gave. In `( deepN r, r )`, the later-use judgement of `deepN`'s write at its 256-step target
cost 2 883 records (`relOf`, `relBelow`, a replay and 514 prefix queries); it is now 317, constant in the path's
length but one `relOf` of the target for the apart rest (#1742's), once per account.

*Holds read by their tags* (2026-11-03). A hold whose tags conflict with the target’s is never the target’s
holder (the relation’s first test answers `no`), so step 4 visits only the others. A holder’s holds are read, once
it has more than eight, as the tree of their tag lists by shared tail (`TagTree.zig`), made the first time it is
asked: a target meets its own list’s subtree and its ancestors’ holds whole, and below an ancestor only the kids
that do not part from its own path (§2.9.3’s parting), each hold there tested exactly. A node whose siblings all
part from it and whose parent holds none is passed by one pointer. The holds met are read in their order, so the
witness is the same. A hold’s liveness does not depend on the target, so a judgement asks it once per holder,
path and point. In `( incAll v, count v )` over an `else if` chain of D arms, each of about 4D targets met about
4D holds: D = 8 / 16 / 32 cost 5 587 / 27 275 / 169 231 demands’ records, now 1 074 / 2 034 / 3 974.

*The best-hold descent* (2026-11-03, step 3 on slots). A holder whose value is a DAG (a `(value, tags)` met at two
paths) lists its holds once a node, at the node's least path, by a second walk that visits kids in order
(`Sweep.holdsOfValue`); every other holder is listed as before, path by path. A target meets such a holder through a
descent from its root (`Descent.zig`): a node's met holds are judged at the descent's path, and each kid in order.
A kid at path `c` **answers for its subtree** when no place below `c` is on a cycle, no use of the holder after the
point is at `c` or below it, and every use at a proper prefix of `c` reads all of `c`'s subtree or none of it (a
whole or field use all; a call use by its callee's footprint at `c`: a deep read or a write at `c` or above all,
an effect only below `c` some, none none). Then every path below `c` has `c`'s later uses, so liveness is asked
once at `c`: none prunes the subtree, and otherwise each hold below it is met once a use, at its least path from
`c` (once more at an exact path after one below a `[*]`). A kid that does not answer for its subtree is descended
path by path, as on a cycle (`hold listings`). The holds are met in path order, a node before its kids, so the
witness at one use of one holder is the least path, an exact one before one at or below a `[*]` or a `⟲`
(*Verdicts*). An aggregated holder reads its pending holds by the same descent. The doubling DAG
`tₖ = ( tₖ₋₁, tₖ₋₁ )` over `xs`, `xs` pushed while `t_d` is read, cost d = 8: 40 478 demands' records and a limit
at 10; now d = 8 / 10 / 12: 249 / 281 / 313, the witness `t_d.0.0…0`, as v1 names it.
*Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714): a hold under its route set.* A holder DAG's nodes are its **values** (a value met
again under other tags is the node it is already), each holding its leaves under no tags (a deep set's element
once, with its route set, `RouteWalk.leavesOf`), and an `alt`'s edge carries its arm's tag. The descent first lists
its items in the order it meets them: a `(node, path)`, or, below a kid that answers for its subtree, a
`(node, use)` (and whether a `[*]` or a `⟲` is on the way) at the path it is met at first; each once. Then each item
is reached under one route set (`DagRoutes.zig`): items in decreasing value id, so every arrival is in before an
item is read (a kid's value is made before its parent's, as in `RouteWalk`), the arrivals united, and an edge's arm
tag put in front of every route (a route it conflicts with dropped; an item no route reaches is not read). Last,
each item's met holds are judged in that order, each hold's leaf under the item's routes: one route merged into its
tags, or the set as its `routes` (`Value.Leaf.routes`, §2.3.5), which the relation reads (`Coexist.setsMeet`); a
leaf with a set of its own takes the item's routes written out. Each item stands for the holds the walk by
`(value, tags)` listed at that path, so the judgements are the same, and the order of first meetings, so every
witness, is that walk's. A key's kids are read under their sets (`Holders`, `Eval.expandRouted`): a key is no
route, so the fold certificate through a shared DAG no longer expands each written-out route.
*Open (#1714): the shared-link knot chain.* Which holders are DAGs is unchanged: a `(value, tags)` met at a second
path. `x_k = if c then T [ x_{k-1} ] else x_{k-1}` meets each `x_j` under one tag list per subset of the choices
above it, every one at a single path, so it is no DAG and its holds are listed once a tag list (2ⁿ; 45 225 records
at n = 10, the limit at 16). Making it a DAG (a value met under a second tag list) costs 1 888 / 13 921 / 57 937
records at n = 8 / 64 / 256, but every `else if` chain whose arms share one value becomes a DAG too, and a target
then meets that value's one tagless hold through every arm's node: the chain read after the call of `chainDump`'s
build test goes from about linear to 16 342 / 61 730 / 244 642 records at D = 8 / 16 / 32. A plain holder's tag
tree (`TagTree`) finds the arm a target's tags name without visiting the others; the descent needs the same index
over its edges' arm tags before the classification can move. Searching a routed target once under its set, not once
a route, loses the same index (3 035 / 9 775 / 34 891 there), so `Resolve` still writes a target's routes out.
*Amended 2026-11-03 (#1742):* a hold that meets a target of its own root at some of its slots (`HoldAt.holdsAt`)
holds it there, and its other objects are the target's only where the root is not separated: the rest of the
holder is asked **apart** from the target (§2.9.2 step 3, under the selection of both), never related. The rest
is the holder's slots less the target's, and a slot set that holds a whole subtree as a symbol (`↓ε`, §2.3.1) keeps
an excluded subtree in it (an exclusion is read against explicit slots only), so the rest still met a deep
target, and the hold at the holder's own path answered **may**. A record-update base `model`, read at the update
at its other fields, refused `grow at model.root`'s deep writes (`browser/tea/ValuePath` 81:30, once `List.map`
had a contract) although the top write was accepted. The relation is now under the selection, and the
caller's `req` gains the deep occurrences (`ownership/HolderRestApart`).

*Pending operands* (2026-11-03). The walk no longer copies its operand stack at every call: each operand on the
stack is one entry, made once (its values, a record update's base by the fields its consumer keeps), with the
walk's clock at its push and at its removal (the clock ticks at a removal); a call, a label's call and a demand
record only the clock. An operand is pending at clock `T` when its push is at or before `T` and its removal after
it, and it is compatible with the point by §2.5 (it comes before the point, so exactly when its `rank₂` is below
the point's). Resolution lists every pending leaf once, with its base keys (`Stack.zig`), in lists sorted by push:
every leaf, the leaves that reach unknown objects, the leaves with a parameter's key, and one list a parameter key's
position, registered at its position and below each ancestor as the holder buckets are. Each list has two trees,
the latest removal and the least `rank₂` over each range, so a demand reads a list's pending, compatible leaves in
push order by a descent into the subtrees that can hold one (a record a node), and stops at the first that may meet
a target: no later operand can be the witness (*Verdicts*, a pending operand by its start). A parameter's untagged
target judged with aggregation reads the unknown list and its related positions' lists; every other pending leaf
with a parameter's key answers `no` or `under` its own selection and the target's, so the target's joins through
the first of them that answers `under`, and each one's own joins `req` once, through the first accepted demand it
was pending at, compatible with, not read one by one for, and answers `under` for (a tree of the writes' greatest
`rank₂` finds it). A label's supplied part reads the list of every leaf. In `[ List.push p1 1 … List.push pn 1 ]`
each push met every earlier push as a pending operand: sib n = 10 / 80 cost 1 990 / 73 040 demands' records, now
1 526 / 13 803.

**The escape index** (#1714, 2026-11-02). Step 2 reads the escapes through an index, never by a scan of
every escape per target. Escapes are bucketed by their leaves' base keys, each bucket sorted by point, with a
tree of the least `rank₂` over each range of it. For an escape `x` before `p`, `x` is compatible with `p`
exactly when `rank₂(x) < rank₂(p)` (§2.5). So a target's query takes, in each bucket its keys can meet (its
atoms', every parameter's when it comes from a parameter, the unknown bucket always), the prefix of escapes
before `p` by one binary search, then the escapes of that prefix whose `rank₂` is below `rank₂(p)` by
descending the tree only into subtrees whose least `rank₂` is: O((1 + k) log e) for the k escapes found, each
of which the relation judges as before. The search costs ⌈log₂(e + 1)⌉ + 1 records and every node it visits
one more, reserved before the work. Before this, each target asked every escape and nothing was charged:
`e × w` tests at growth 0 (the mixed term of the escapes × writes family was 0; master's v2 charged 144).

The verdict's ground is `fresh` when every target is an atom this frame allocated (a `site` or a call's
`fresh`), `call` when a target comes through a callee's contract only, and `param` when the write relies on
the frame's parameters (its `req`). A callback's write (§2.11.3) is `callback-param`. The holder named in a
refusal is the one used first, ties to the earlier binding (R-6.3).

**Verdicts** (R-0.3): `accepted` {`fresh`, `call`, `param`, `callback-param`, `once`, `entry`}; `pending detail`
(§2.11); `refused cause` per R-6.3, exact/approximate/position by the pairs it rested on; among failing holders
the first in one canonical total order (the owner's decision, 2026-10-29, #1214): an exact refusal before an
approximate one; then the earliest use (a pending operand by its start); then the earlier binding; then the hold
path, compared step by step from the root by step word, a prefix before its extensions; then the holder's source
order (its index among the frame's holders); then the use's atom. The last two make the order total: the positions
of one pattern are bound at one point, and one holder can be used twice at one point (`( r, r )`). Discovery order
(a radix walk's or a stack's) never breaks a tie, so a message never names a witness by registration order. A
refusal on several base cells is always approximate (the owner's decision, 2026-10-30, #1214): its verdict is
certain either way, and only its exactness would have needed the cells' join. That rule decides `(approx)` alone;
the cause word stays condition 5's (the manager's decision, 2026-10-30, #1214), so a hold that is exact for one
of the cells is `alias … (approx)`, never `element`. The result of every writer, construction, append and update **is
its base's object** (R-0.1, R-4.10.1): a `delta` or the base's node, so the next holder is the new version.

**Twin demands** (#1714, specified and built 2026-11-03). Two demands of one evaluation that one call makes
for one argument, equal in every field but the path their text names (the targets and the operands by their
leaves and values, the point, the kind, the base, the pending operands, the flags), are **twins**: the later is
not judged, and its line is the first's verdict with its own text. Every field the judgement reads is equal, so
the verdict is the one a second judgement would give, and `req` gains nothing from it. Twins come from a
callee's writes through a folding `⟲`: in `type B = B (List B) …` with k list fields, `incList` writes
`[*]#B.j⟲` for each field j, and each projects onto the same k canonical slots of the caller's `x[*]⟲#B.i`
(§2.1), so the call made k demands with one set of targets, each judged against k slots. A demand of a call
that makes only one for its argument costs nothing more; the others pay one record a target for the lookup,
and a hit pays for the comparison.

**Record lowering boundary (S5).** A write authorization is tied to a settled demand, the receiver's
value version, written fields and phase. A hoist names the old value version, field/constructor path and
placement dominating the read but after its binding. Branch/loop compatibility and pending operands are
part of that proof, not reconstructed by the emitter from source names. `Hoists` publishes an immutable,
versioned channel only for a clean checked module; a refused, pending or exhausted module publishes no
write authorization. Test mutation through a stale field holder after a join, closure capture before the
write, and hoists across constructor projections. `--ownership-records-lost` changes record facts only and
must not leak into list acceptance or a cache built without that mode.

### 2.9 Conditions: the selection and the one relation

*Replaced 2026-11-02 (#1685), with §2.3. Until then this section specified κ snapshots, their tries and
links, the path-multiset primitive, fold-first propagation (`propagate`), fold certificates and the order
check. The selection below is now the only condition; nothing else in the checker says that two objects are
apart.*

#### 2.9.1 The selection

A **selection** is a set of **occurrences** `(j, s)`, a parameter of the frame and one of its object slots
(relative steps, §2.3.1). A **deep occurrence** `(j, s)*` [#1706] is every object slot at and below `s`: the
selection of a symbol `↓s` (§2.3.1), instantiated at a call by a deep projection (§2.11.2). It asks every
occurrence of `j` at a slot whose steps continue `s`'s; a stored selection leaves those out, and `within`
reads them as asked, so a join that adds one changes nothing (§2.12). `Sep(sel)` says: every object at a selected occurrence occurs at most once among all
the selected occurrences. It is the inductive predicate of a region (Astra's second review, §2): a family
slot's objects are pairwise distinct, and distinct from every other selected occurrence's.

**Deep occurrences** [#1710, #1711, 2026-11-02]. An occurrence at a slot no step below can name — a type
variable's or an opaque place — is marked *deep*, printed `s*`: it selects every object at and below the slot in
the value it is instantiated on (§2.11.2 item 3 projects it deep). Such a slot stands for whatever the caller
passes, so the plain occurrence asked only the outer object to be once: `idd x = x` handed `( xs, xs )`, and a
cast (`Js.to (Js.from [ xs, xs ])`, an identity at an opaque slot, §2.13.9), answered two parts the caller took
for apart. The mark is bit 62 of the occurrence and bit 30 of its parameter word in a block (§3.6).
*Amended 2026-11-05 (#1956):* a function's slot is such a slot too. A function value holds its captures, which no
step below its slot names, and its code reads them. So an occurrence there is deep, written out deep (`Canon`), and
instantiated on a closure it takes the closure's captures (§2.10, #1772). Before this, `( h, ys ) = t` then
`( List.push ys 1, h ⊤ )` relied on `sel π1{.0~,.1}`, which a tuple `( λ⊤ → List.length xs, xs )` met (the closure
and the list are two objects), and `h` read the edited list (OnceOtherHolder's `tuple`: copying `2 1`, in place
`2 2`). Fixtures: `run/SanitiserClosureSlotHolder` (a captured tuple and a passed one, refused) and
`run/SanitiserClosureSlotHolderApart` (the function reads another list: accepted).

**One spelling of a subtree** [#1714, 2026-11-03]. `(j, p)*` asks every slot of `below(p)`, and so do the
occurrences at those slots written out (deep where no step below can be named): one set, two words. A round
that read the set the other way moved the contract although nothing changed (`Dict.descend`: round 0 read
`right`'s slots one by one, round 1 instantiated `π2ε*` over `Step key value right rest`, deep at `right`,
whose `below` is `↓#0.4` since a cycle holds an object, §2.3.1; two more rounds, 38 195 records). So a
contract's selections (`res_cond`, `req`, a supply's condition) are read off in one spelling (`Canon.zig`,
at the read-off, §2.10): a deep occurrence `(j, p)*` whose `below(p)` written out has at most `below_min`
slots is those slots, with its apartness; past the bound, at a type variable's or an opaque place, or at steps
that name no single path, it stays. Past the bound is decided first off the place graph: each place keeps a
lower bound on the object slots below a path at it (`Place.slotsAtLeast`, made with its component: each object
place of the component once, and what is below each step out of it), so a type of many places is read in one
lookup, not a walk of its places a selection (#1714: `Schema.described*` 254 → 244 growth records). Equality of contracts is then equality of the normal form, so a round
that only respells a subtree changes nothing (§2.12): `Dict.descend` is 3 rounds and 25 773 records, with
`below`'s cycle rule kept for the walk's slot sets. The other direction (written-out slots past the bound to
the symbol) is not taken: nothing reads a subtree past `below_min` slot by slot into a selection but a
constructor's and a worded declaration's occurrences (§2.3.1 *Written out where a contract names each slot*),
which are not rounds' contracts. *Measured, rejected:* spelling a subtree whose `below` is a symbol as the
deep occurrence (the other normal form): an instantiated `(j, p)*` projects deep at the caller's path, whose
`below` under a folded `⟲` name holds more than the callee's slots did, so `req` grew in later rounds (the
k-list-fields family went from 5 rounds to 7, 1.15 M to 1.5 M records at k = 16), and two deep spellings of
one set met in one selection and read as one object twice (`FoldSymbolicCall`'s `probeDistinct` refused).

A **condition** is `no` (unprovable) or a selection. Conjunction is the union of the selections: linear,
never a table of pairs. `yes` is the empty selection. A condition `a` is **weaker** than `b` (asks no more)
when `a`'s selection is a subset of `b`'s, or `b` is `no`. A selection is printed and encoded in a canonical
order: by parameter, then by the slot's relative steps, never by intern order.

A frame's parameters are its **assumptions**: a selection on them is what the frame asks of its callers. A
call's separation is the callee's `res_cond` instantiated on its arguments (§2.11.2).

**Apart occurrences** [#1685, as built]. An occurrence may be marked *apart*, printed `s~`: its objects must
be apart from the objects of every plain occurrence of the selection, but may repeat among themselves and
meet another apart occurrence's. A
holder beside a write needs no more: the written object is none of the holder's, whatever the holder repeats
inside it. So the relation (§2.9.2 steps 3 and 5) asks the holder's slots apart and the target's plain. The
distinct check never compares two entries of apart occurrences, and a family entry of one does not ask its
own root's separation. A plain occurrence asks more than the apart one of the same slot, so a selection that
has both keeps the plain one only. Without the mark, a write beside a list of records asked every record's
field to be distinct from every other's, and `List.unzipHelp`'s builder writes and `collect rest []` over a
list that repeats an element were refused `disjoint` where nothing aliases the written list.

The same holds below a deep apart occurrence [#1714, as built]: `π1{ε*~,[*]#0.0}` asks every object below
`ε` apart except the ones at `[*]#0.0`, which it asks plain, exactly as the same selection written out
(`π1{ε~,[*]#0.0,[*]#0.1~,…}`) does. A call's instantiation (§2.9.3's routed rule) reads such a parameter
part by part: the deep projection of a literal gives each part's own objects at the part's own route, so a
route names one place in the argument. An object a plain occurrence reaches at a route is then taken from the
apart ones at that route, once for each time a plain one reaches it there, never by leaf alone: one object
at a plain slot and at another slot below the apart one is two entries, and the check still refuses it. A
reference's slots lose the plain ones' at its route by `Subtree.without`. Without this, a `↓p` symbol
(§2.3.1) read a family more coarsely than its slots written out: the deep projection gave the object at
`[*]#0.0` apart and the plain one gave it again, and the check refused `incLabels [ Rose [] [], Rose [] [] ]`.

#### 2.9.2 The one relation

`overlap(x, t)` of a holder's leaf `x` (deep) and a target leaf `t` answers **no**, **under** a condition, or
**may**:

1. Tags that give one choice two arms: **no**.
2. `⊤` on either side: **may**.
3. **One root, two `ref` leaves.** When their positions are related (§2.3.2) and their slot sets meet: **may**;
   except that a shallow target at its own position (`at_position`) never meets what lies strictly inside it
   (no value holds itself). Otherwise the two are at distinct places, and the answer is: for a parameter,
   **under** the selection of both leaves' slots of that parameter; for a call, **under** its instantiated
   `res_cond`, or, when that is `no`, the relation of what the two parts come from (each side expanded, step 4).
4. **A call leaf and a leaf of another root.** The later root is **expanded** first: a call's leaf becomes the
   leaves the callee's contract says arrive at its slots, projected onto the call's arguments (§2.11.2), and
   the relation is the join of the relations of the parts (no < under < may; two unders conjoin).
   *Amended 2026-11-02 (#1714):* an atom made after the call (a literal's site, or a later call's `fresh`) is
   none of the call's objects: **no**, without expanding, by comparing the two points. An object that does not
   exist yet when a call returns cannot arrive in its result. `mayRecons` already reads a base this way
   (`PrependFresh`). Without it, the literal `[ k ]` handed to the kth call of a chain
   `x_k = step x_(k-1) [ k ]` was compared with every earlier call's result: the chain's demands cost n².
5. **Two parameters**: **under** the selection of both leaves' occurrences (one selection: their objects are
   pairwise distinct).
6. **Two atoms** (`site`, `fresh`, `shared`): **may** when they are the same atom, else **no**. An atom and a
   parameter's leaf: **no** (an object this frame allocated is no parameter's; a parameter that holds a shared
   value is the caller's to refuse, where the actual is seen).
7. **A label's answer** (§2.11.3). As the target: **may** (unknown code may answer anything it reaches). As the
   holder, when the label has a direct call in this frame: the join of each leaf that call supplied against the
   target, and of what the label's function slot `(j, s)` may hold: **no** for an object this activation built
   (`site`, `fresh`), **under** `(j, s)~` and the selection of the target for another parameter's leaf, a call's
   leaf expanded, otherwise **may**. A label the frame only passes on answers **may**. *Amended 2026-11-02
   (#1685):* before, every answer was **may**, so a callback's answer pending in a list literal kept every later
   supply of the same label (`[ f x, …mapL rest f ]`, `[ f x, f y ]`), and a writing callback was refused although
   the label's own condition (its supplies' elements distinct, its function apart from them) already keeps
   them apart.

The relation is a row per pair of leaves per walk, solved as §2.9.2 says, and reserved before work.

**The fixed point of the pairs** [#2146]. The steps above are one equation per pair, and the pairs a pair reaches
can reach it back: a fold's supply and its answer are `S → [ init, A ]`, `A → [ S, q ]`. The relation is the
**least fixed point** of those equations (§2.11.3), so a depth-first read that cuts a pair met again has a partial
value everywhere below the cut. At `(A, t)` with `t = q`, the read of `(S, t)` reaches `(A, t)` again, and that
`no` is `S`'s value only until `A` is done. Kept, it answered the next read of `(S, t)`, whose true value holds
`q`, so which pair was asked first decided the verdict: `w = ( r.0, r.1 )` over a fold's two-field accumulator
wrote in place under a live reader, and the same program with `w = ( r.1, r.0 )` was refused.

The relation is solved by one depth-first walk that finds the equations' strongly connected components as it goes
(`Pairs.zig`, Tarjan's algorithm). Rows are numbered in the order they are entered. Each row keeps the value it has
so far; a row read while it is open, or closed but unsolved, gives that value and passes on the lowest number it read.
A row that read no number below its own is its component's head, and it walks the component again until no value of
it moves. The number is not the row's depth: a closed member's low is a depth a later sibling can stand at, and by depth
that sibling passes for a head, with a value made under a cut (`H → [ A, C, t ]`, `A → [ H, B ]`, `B → [ A ]`,
`C → [ B ]`: `run/SanitiserPairCrossEdge*`). `may` is the top: a head that reaches it stops at once and forgets its
members, which saw less.

- **Where the equations are joins** (every step above but `keeping`'s), they are monotone, each value only joins
  upward over a finite lattice, and the walk ends in the least fixed point, whichever pair it met first.
- **Where they are not.** `AnswerKeep.kept` turns a `may` into `under` the function's `fresh`, so a larger value can
  map to a smaller one: its equations are not monotone and have no least fixed point. The walk **accumulates** there,
  joining each pass into the row, and it stops at a post-fixed point: no equation asks more than its row holds. Which
  post-fixed point can depend on the order the pairs are met. That is precision, not soundness. A model of 15 000
  random systems with `kept` edges, 12 orders each, has 51 order splits, and of the 1 807 980 equations it checked none
  asks more than its row. Its order sensitivity is tracked with #2160.
- **A value under another cut.** A pair's equation may read a call's separation (`apartIn`), and `instCond` reads `no`
  on a cycle of its own and keeps what it made. A solved row can rest on that, so a row is free of the relation's cuts,
  not of that one: sound, since each reader of `no` has its own route, and order-sensitive as #2160 says.
- **What is kept.** `Pairs.solved` is a retained table: computed answers, kept across queries for an evaluation and
  dropped at the next outer query after a key grows (§2.12), since a key that grew changed what a leaf expands to. A row of a walk is not kept in
  any form: a value enters `solved` when its head has solved its component. **It is kept by the owner's decision
  (2026-11-06), an exception for this table only**: the rule that caches go stands for every other.
- **Why it is kept.** Two measurements of the alternatives. With no rows, cutting only the pairs on the path is correct
  and exponential: `x_k = pick (id1 x_(k-1)) (id2 x_(k-1))` passes its account at n = 20. With rows per query, each demand
  walks again what the last solved, so `y_k = pick c y_(k-1) (List.push z k)` is n²: continuation 69 564 at n = 200 and
  760 296 at n = 800, against 29 369 and 119 501 here, and the flat-cost test fails. Removing it needs a design that
  holds no state between demands and is still flat on that chain; none is known.
- **A query.** A read made while another runs (a call's separation inside a pair's equation, a delivery) has a walk
  of its own: it reads no open row of the other.
- **Cost.** Each pair once, a component once more per pass that moved a value. Core's heads settle in two passes, the
  second only to confirm what the first found.

#### 2.9.3 Non-duplication: the distinct check

`Sep(v)`, the separation of a value built by this frame, says that `v`'s objects each occur once. It is the
**distinct check** over `v`'s leaves, each **entry** a leaf with its **route** (the literal kid path that
reached it, so one value placed twice is two entries):

*Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714): a `many` leaf has two routes.* A value's leaf set holds a leaf two coexisting
kids reach once, marked `many` (§2.3.4), and a read of the set gives it twice. A projection that reads a
set whole (a deep occurrence at a built value or a choice, a value's own storage, a step a literal cannot
follow) gave both copies the one route it was at, and the check took the second for the first: `idd`'s
`π1{ε*}` projected over `P t t` asked `t` once, and `firstOnly (P t t)` wrote `a` while `b` was the same
tree (the program printed `3 2` where its copy semantics print `3 3`). The second copy now takes a route of
its own (`Relation.Eval.readAt`), so it is a second entry, as the kids it came from are.

- An entry that is a family (`ref` not `at_position`) asks its root's own separation on its slots; `⊤` and
  `shared` entries make the check `no`.
- Entries are **grouped by root**. Within a group, a conflict is two entries at related positions whose slots
  meet. It is found through position ancestry: each entry is indexed at `(position, slot)` for each of its
  slots, and an entry is checked against the index at its own position and each ancestor, never against every
  other entry. *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714):* list steps too. Two list steps of one parent may name one element
  (a `front` and a `back`, a `front` and a `slice` from its index or before, two `slice`s) where two `front`s,
  two `back`s or two plain steps never do; so each entry is also indexed below every ancestor at
  `(ancestor, kind of the list step that leads to it, slot)`, and checked, below each list step of its own path,
  against the kinds that may name what that step names. Before, a group with list steps compared its pairs:
  `[ p1 … pn ]` pushed inside one literal was n²/2 pairs (*live sibling positions*: 371 986 records at n = 80,
  now 136 538). A group of at most eight still compares its pairs. A conflict makes the check `no`.
- A group of two entries or more asks its root's separation on the union of their slots (a parameter's
  selection; a call's instantiated `res_cond`). Two parameters' groups ask the selection of both. *Amended
  2026-11-02 (#1711):* so does a group of **one entry that names more than one object** — two slots or more,
  or a slot of a type variable's or an opaque place: `wrapDup x = dup x` answers `dup`'s call whole, one leaf
  over `.0` and `.1`, and claimed `nondup yes` while `dup` is `no`. A call that does not vouch for such an entry
  at a type variable's or opaque slot is `no` outright: the arrivals there are one set, so `xs` twice inside a
  cast is one leaf and expansion cannot count it.
- *Amended 2026-11-02 (#1711):* **a callback's answer** (a `cb` leaf, or a passed-on label's answer) is the
  unknown code's: any object its caller reaches — what the label was supplied, the code's captures, the caller's
  other arguments, another answer of the same code. It is apart from no other entry but an alternative to it or
  one of its own block. Before this, two answers were two roots and so apart: `callTwice f = ( f ⊤, f ⊤ )`
  claimed `nondup yes`, and `callTwice λ⊤ → xs` answered `xs` twice. A caller with the code to hand still reads
  both answers precisely, through the call's expansion (the call vouches for nothing).
- Two entries of one atom that coexist make the check `no`; an atom's single entry is distinct from every
  other root's. *Amended 2026-11-02 (#1714):* the entries of one atom are read as a tree of their tag lists
  by shared tail (§2.3.5); two entries whose lists part at two pairs of one choice with no arm in common
  conflict and are not merged, so an atom an `else if` chain reaches through D arms costs D, never D².
- When a call's group meets another root's, the latest call is expanded into its arguments' entries (one
  level), which form one **block** the call has vouched for, and the check runs again.
- A call's group of two entries or more whose instantiated `res_cond` is `no` is expanded the same way, but
  as no block: the call has vouched for nothing, so its parts are compared through what they come from, each
  on its own (as §2.9.2 step 3 does for one pair). Refusing there refused a write of one field of a record a
  callee answers whole beside another field (`AnsweredHolder`), where the parts come from distinct
  parameters.
- The conditions met are gathered as occurrences, each once, and made one selection at the end: a merge per
  entry or per group costs their product (the *Fields* family went 1.94×, 2.15×, 2.37× per doubling before).
- *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1713):* **candidates of one object.** A callee's occurrence that is neither deep nor
  apart, at a path of fields, tuple indices and constructor arguments only, names one object of one
  invocation (an entry whose slot no step below can name, or a whole subtree, is not such an entry). Every
  entry the check makes from it, projected or expanded, is a **candidate** of that object: where the object
  may come from. Two candidates of one object are never compared, in a group or in an atom's, and an
  answer is not compared with a candidate of its own object either. A candidate met again with its leaf
  and block, or an apart entry met again with its leaf, block and occurrence, is not made twice. Before
  this, a fold's accumulator was read as two objects: its supply is the first value or the label's answer
  handed back, and that answer holds the accumulator, so expanding it reached the first value again, as a
  second entry of its atom, and every fold whose step reads two parts of its accumulator (`π2{.0,.1~}`) was
  refused `disjoint`.
  *Why this is sound.* At one invocation the occurrence's place holds one object. Each entry made from it
  says that object may be this leaf's, at one route; two of them are two answers to where one object comes
  from, never two places that hold it, so they cannot make it occur twice. Their comparisons with every
  other entry are kept: the candidates of `.0` and `.1` come from two occurrences, so a first value
  `( t, t )`, or an answer `( p, p )` handed back, still meets itself and is refused. A repeated candidate,
  or apart entry, has the same comparisons as the first (the same leaf, block and occurrence; its route is
  new, so the routed rule never spares it), and leaving it out is what ends the expansion of
  accumulator → answer → accumulator. Measured: 8 positions refused before are accepted (`FoldKeepsInner`
  ×3, `FoldKeepsInnerRefused` ×3, which v1 also accepts, `FoldFeedbackCondition`, and
  `SanitiserNestedCallbackWrite`'s tuple fold), and `groupOrder` no longer reaches its limit; the negative
  controls (`run/SanitiserFoldAlternativesShared`) trap when all the parts are read as candidates of one
  object.
- **The routed rule.** When a callee's condition is instantiated (§2.11.2), two distinct occurrences of the
  callee that land in one value of this frame by one literal route and position are two distinct positions of
  it: they ask that value's own separation, never a refusal. Two parameters handed one value are that value
  twice: routes are per parameter.

The cost is linear in the entries and their ancestors' index hits; payload fields add entries, never pairs
(the experiment's *Fields* family: relation facts 819, 835, 1 421, 2 904 at 1, 2, 4 and 8 fields). A check
that needs a dense relation reserves each pair as growth.

*The rounds' state* (#1714, 2026-11-03; `Entries.zig`). A round expands one root, so a literal of n calls takes
n rounds; each round regrouped every entry and re-ran every group's check, n × n. The check now keeps its working
state across its rounds: every entry is made once, with the entry it was expanded from and its place in that
expansion (the inline order the rounds read: an expansion takes the place of the entry it expands); groups by root
and by atom stay built, each with its within-group index and the count of its members whose pairs and
occurrences were asked. A round places only the entries the last expansion made, re-checks only the groups they
changed (a parameter's group for its new members' pairs and occurrences; a call's, a supply's and an atom's whole,
as before), and asks the answer rule only for pairs with a new entry; a second parameter's group makes every
parameter group ask its occurrences, as before. A new member is compared with the earlier ones, pairwise up to
eight and then by the index, which files each entry's slots by §2.3.2's protocol of position indices (at its
position, and at each step's parent under the step's class) so that a new entry meets the earlier ones at, above
and below it and those apart only at a step that may meet its own (§2.3.2, *one relation for the pairs and the
indices*, #1963); an earlier entry that several of its slots meet is asked once. The root to expand is the greatest of a heap of the expandable roots,
or of the groups that ask to be expanded (`must`), a stale one skipped. A vouched block keeps the first of two
equal leaves in the inline order (its members compared by the expansions they came from, below their common
ancestor: each entry keeps a skew-binary jump pointer, whose depth is a function of its own depth alone, so the
comparison takes O(log depth) steps, not the depth of the chain of expansions). An expansion's leaf
that is the leaf of the entry it expands or of one that entry was expanded from is not made an entry: around a
cycle of expansions (a fold's supply and its step's answer, #1714) it names that ancestor's objects, which the
chain reads already, so a chain's leaves are distinct and the rounds end; a second chain still meets the cycle's
exits (`FoldSupplyCycle`). That test is one lookup for a leaf no entry has (the chain is walked only for one
that some entry has), never a walk a new entry: a chain of n calls walked it at every expansion, n², and
`x_k = step x_{k-1} [ k ]` cost 143 / 443 records a call at 10 / 40 calls (#1714). *A chain of calls handing one
object on* (#1714, 2026-11-03): where the expansion takes one entry of its root and gives one leaf, a call's
leaf of one object slot (no family's, no type variable's) whose call has one leaf there is read on to its end
(`Relation.Eval.endOf`, by `(leaf, keys' growth)`): each call on the way would be a group of one entry of one
object, which asks nothing of its own, so the check reads the same leaves without a round a call. `step` is then
113 / 104 records a call at 10 / 40 calls, `shared` 120 / 112; every summary and verdict is unchanged. Each
round charges a
record and one per new entry (each changes one group at most; the changed groups are listed as they change,
never found by a scan), besides the work of its checks. Every outcome is the one the
regrouping check gave: a group's check reads its members only, and the conditions gathered are a set. This is
the fixpoint's own working state, never a table of earlier answers. *Live sibling positions* at n = 10 / 20 / 40
/ 80: 4 090 / 11 883 / 38 608 / 136 538 records, now 3 134 / 6 370 / 12 923 / 26 191 (with the pending operands
of §2.8): flat per position.

*A call's atoms* (#1714, 2026-11-03; `AtomSets.zig`). A leaf of a call's result whose expansion ends, through
calls only, at atoms names exactly those atoms. It keeps them as a set: a hash-consed Patricia set of atom keys
(`KeySets`, the resolve lane's base-key sets), made with the leaf's first reading as the union of its expansion's
sets and sharing their nodes, so `y_k = List.push y_{k-1} [ k ]` makes a path a level, never a copy of the k atoms
below. A leaf that reaches a parameter, a label, a supply, `⊤`, a cycle, or a slot no step below names (one leaf
there may be one object several times, #1710) has no set. A set is made once a leaf while no key grows, as
`endOf`'s answers are; it is the leaf's description, never an answer of the check. Once a check, at its first round
after an expansion that would expand a root no group asks to, it asks whether it is decided already: every live
entry is an atom, a parameter's object (never an atom of this frame) or a call's leaf with a set; every call's group
has vouched for its own objects (its callee's `res_cond`, asked by the group's check and not `no`, or its members
all apart occurrences, or one member of one object, an expansion's family excepted); and no atom is named twice.
The last is a membership query, not a listing: the largest set is kept whole, every other atom is looked up in it
(a step a level) and among the others. Then every expansion would make atoms that meet nothing and ask nothing, and
the check ends with what it has gathered. Before, `x_k = merge x_{k-1} y_k` with `y_k` grown by a push expanded
`y_k`'s chain to its k atoms at every call: 328 / 534 records a call at 10 / 40 calls, now 297 / 319 (`indep`, two
chains merged, 397 / 601, now 366 / 387). Every summary and verdict is unchanged.

#### 2.9.4 What a write relies on

A demand (§2.8) is resolved against the relation. Every **under** it meets is added to the condition the write
relies on. When the condition is about the frame's own parameters, it becomes the frame's `req` (§2.10): the
callers must establish it, and the demand is accepted `param`. A condition on a call's result that the
callee's `res_cond` does not give is `no`, and the demand is refused `exclusive` (cause precedence of §2.8
step 6). A demand whose target is fresh and that meets no holder is accepted `fresh`; one whose target comes
through a call's contract only is accepted `call`.

*Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714):* the conditions are **gathered**, never conjoined one by one. Each condition a
demand meets appends its occurrences to the demand's list (a record each), and the list is made one selection,
sorted once, when the demand is accepted. The frame's `req`, a label's supply condition and a passed-on
