label's are gathered the same way over their accepted judgements. A conjunction per condition merged the whole
selection so far each time, so n demands that each add a slot cost n² for `req` alone.

#### 2.9.5 Why this is sound

`Sep` of a parameter selection is an assumption that every caller checks at its call (§2.11.2): a call
instantiates the callee's `req` on its arguments, by the distinct check over the projected leaves, and a `no`
refuses the call's write demand. `res_cond` is computed by the distinct check over the leaves the body
returns, under the candidates of its group (§2.12), and validated by a separate walk. Positions name the
source's own projections, so two distinct positions are two places in one structure, and their objects are
distinct exactly when the root's separation says so. Leaves never forget a provenance: unknown provenance is
`⊤`, never an empty set, and a call's leaf is expanded to its arrivals whenever it meets another root.
*Amended 2026-11-06 (#2143):* this paragraph is the argument's outline. §2.14 is the argument, and §2.14.3 says what an empty set may claim.

### 2.10 Contracts

*Replaced 2026-11-02 (#1685). Until then a declaration's behaviour was a class: shapes over its parameters'
places labelled `R`/`A`/`E`/`W`, a `res` shape, κ, `xreq`, `fun(j)`, a class table, `slots`, `effects`, `refs`
and `once`. The contract below says the same things over slots.*

A **contract** describes one **code**: a top-level declaration, a lambda, a local function, a constructor, a
worded row (§2.13.6) or a schema member. Its parameters `π1…πn` are the code's own, then its captures
(§2.11.4). Every slot below is relative steps from a parameter's or the result's root (§2.3.1).

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `returns` | whether some activation returns: `false` is ⊥, a recursive candidate's start (§2.12) |
| `cross` | the result holds no object |
| `res` | per object slot `q` of the result, its **arrivals**: `π_j·s` (the objects at the parameter's slot `s`), `fresh` (allocated by the activation), `shared d`, `cb L` (the answer of callback label `L`), `⊤`. Sorted by `q`, then by arrival |
| `res_cond` | `Sep(result) ⇐` a condition: the result's objects are each once, under a selection of the parameters, or `no` |
| `reads` | the **footprint**: `(j, s, deep)`, the parameter slots the body reads, a deep read reading `below(s)`. An arrival is a read of its slot where the result is consumed (§2.7 *A part a callee answers*) |
| `writes` | `(j, s, deep)`: the parameter slots the body writes, shallow (a storage write, `F` fields for a record) or deep (`consumed`, §2.8) |
| `req` | the condition the writes rely on |
| `escapes` | `(j, s)`: the parameter slots whose objects escape (stored behind a cell's barrier, sent, handed to unknown code, §2.4): the caller marks them escaped at the call (deep, §2.4) |
| `stores` | `(j, s) ⇐ c`, one per cell: a value is stored in the `◆` at the parameter slot, and what that cell holds escapes at a call where `c` does not hold (§2.13.7, *the contents relation*) |
| `labels` | per callback label `L` (§2.11.3): the function slot `(j, s)` it calls, its **origin** (the instruction of the call, as `module·declaration·offset`), `calls` ∈ {0, ≤1, many}, and per argument `k` the **supply**: arrivals per object slot of the argument (as `res`), the slots the code **keeps** (a live holder after the call or another operand at it), and the condition under which the supplied objects of distinct invocations are distinct |
| `once` | the code writes one of its captures (R-2.8): a caller may call it at most once |

The fields are flat runs in the module's contract table (§3.5): a contract is a record of ranges.

**Lattice.** Arrivals, `reads`, `writes`, `escapes`, `labels` and supplies are sets ordered by inclusion (`stores` too, its conditions strengthening as `req`'s);
`res_cond` and a supply's condition weaken (a larger selection, then `no`); `req` strengthens the same way;
`returns` and `once` are bits. A **join** is pointwise, and it never drops a result slot: a slot one side
does not have keeps the other side's arrivals (the experiment's first requirement: a loop over an empty list
skipped the append). `within(got, claim)`: every arrival, read, write, escape, label and supply of `got` is in
`claim`, `got`'s `res_cond` is no weaker than `claim`'s unless `claim`'s is `no`, `got`'s `req` asks no more
than `claim`'s, and `got` does not return where `claim` does not.

**Read-off.** After a walk, the contract is read off the frame:

- `res`: the result value is described along the result's place. A `built` part extends the result slot by
  its step; a `ref` leaf at result slot `q` of a parameter's position at slot `p` gives, for each object slot
  `p·r` in its set, the arrival `π_j·(p·r)` at `q·r`; an atom gives `fresh` or `shared d`; a `cb` leaf gives
  `cb L`; a call's leaf gives the callee's arrivals at its slots, projected onto the call's arguments and then
  described again (a recursive group's calls are delivered instead, §2.12). An `alt` describes each arm.
  *Amended 2026-11-02 (#1716, #1740):* an **open** arrival (one that holds by structure at every slot below its own,
  `Relation.open_bit`) whose leaves are another call's or a supply's result stands for that result's whole subtree:
  it is widened to every slot below its own (`Relation.widen`) and described through the call's own key below each
  of its slots (`describeCallWide`), never as its top slot alone. A fold's open answer is such an arrival:
  `Dict.partition`'s `foldlTree` answers `step`'s tuple of `Dict.insert` results, and with the top slot alone the
  partition's result said its values were `shared` and nothing more, so an edit in place of a list the argument held
  was accepted while a half of the partition still held it (`run/SanitiserPartitionHolds`); a fold with a known
  lambda whose answer is a constructor holds no object at its top slot, and `Dict.filter`'s result said nothing of
  the argument's lists (`run/SanitiserFoldAnswerWide`). An atom (fresh, `⊤`, a shared value) that a wide entry
  at or above the result slot already holds is said there for every slot below it, so it is not described again
  (`Held.zig`; one lookup in the draft, one record, as an arrival's; a committed tree joined in is not read). Without
  that, `Schema.shapeOf` describes the same fresh objects at every slot of its recursive result and passes its
  allowance. *A call's subtree of atoms* (#1714, 2026-11-03; `AtomGraft.zig`): where a settled callee (no live
  draft) says only atoms at and below a call's slot and open above it, and the slot's place is the result slot's,
  the read-off grafts the callee's node there and says the open atoms above it wide, instead of reading a key below
  the slot item by item. Each node of a result tree keeps whether every arrival at and below it is an atom, made
  with the node, so the test at a call's root reads no node; a deeper slot is walked from the root, a record a
  node. The graft names the slots below the result slot by the callee's own steps, so it is taken only where no
  place on the result slot's path above it is reachable from its place (no cycle spans it, and `Place.extend`
  then folds every return below it as the callee does). Every summary is the slot-by-slot read's; `shapesOf`'s
  growth goes from 5 622 to 3 119.
  *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1225, #1714): a parameter's path grafted.* When a call's argument `j` is one of the
  caller's parameters `j'` whole, at its root and at the place of the callee's parameter `j`, the callee's slots
  of `π_j` are the caller's slots of `π_j'` step for step: the same relative steps. So a call slot whose
  arrivals (`Forest.atSlot` of the callee's settled `res`) are all atoms or such a parameter's at the slot itself
  (deep only at a type variable's slot) is read off as those arrivals, `π_j·s` renamed `π_j'·s`, and never
  projected onto the argument and described again (`CallGraft.slotArrivals`). A label's arrival, an arrival open
  above the slot, another argument, a member being solved or a slot whose key is made already takes the
  projection. The arrivals are the ones the projection names, so nothing else changes; the work at the call is
  constant in the length of `s`. Before, `callN r = deepN r` with `deepN r = List.push r.a…a 1` (N steps)
  replayed the callee's path at each of its result slots, a place extend a step: `call256` 5 293 records, growth
  1 195 (now 1 649, growth 0).
  *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714, owed test (c)): an arrival keeps its path.* A parameter's arrival the read-off
  makes from a slot it holds also keeps that slot's **path**, the module's node the relative steps name from the
  parameter's root (`Trees.Arrival.path`; part of the arrival's content in the module's trees, never in a block,
  so a decoded arrival has none). An expansion of the call's leaf (§2.9.2 step 4) whose argument is a `ref` at
  that path's root, with no `⟲` on its way and no steps below the arrival's, is the leaf at that path itself
  (`canon` of it, `below` of it when deep): the leaf the projection names, made without replaying the steps. The
  distinct check of `( deepN r, r )` expanded the call's leaf onto `r` at its two result slots, four records a
  step (1 565 at N = 256); it is now constant in N.
  *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1756):* **a key reads the objects at its own slot.** A call's or a supply's key at caller
  slot `s` (`instAt`, and `feed` while a group is solved) reads each arrival of the callee's tree that it meets.
  An **open** arrival is the parameter's subtree by structure, so it gives the parameter's object at the
  matching place only (`Subtree.readAt`); it is read deep only where `s` is a type variable's or an opaque place,
  where no step below can name the objects. A **plain** arrival is read as it is: a deep one (`aliased`'s
  `everySlot` row, a slot the result cannot name) says that any object of the parameter's subtree may be at `s`.
  Before this, an open deep arrival was read deep at every slot, so a key at `s` also held every object below
  `s`. Through a label, `grow g = { g | kids = List.push g.kids "new" }` asks `π1{ε~,.kids}`: the record's own
  object apart from the written list. The supply's key at `ε` gave the record and both of its lists, so the
  apart entry met the plain `.kids` entry, and the write was refused through any label (`apply1 f x = f x`,
  `List.update`, a fold), while the tuple form, which has no `ε~`, was accepted. A known code's answer that an
  arrival reads deep (`arrivalLeaves`' `cb` arm) is now its subtree's slots: before, it was its top slot, and
  only the deep key read made it hold what is below.
  *Why this is sound.* Every leaf names the places it stands for in its slot set: a deep projection writes
  out `below(p)` or holds `↓p` (§2.3.1). So a reader that wants what is below a slot reads each slot below
  through its own key, as the read-off and the deliveries already do. An open arrival holds by structure: the
  result's object at `q·r` is the parameter's at `p·r`. At a type variable's place, parametric code cannot
  answer a part of its argument for the whole, and a cast that can (§2.13.9) reaches the caller through an
  opaque slot, which stays deep, or through a step its value cannot follow, which reads every object of it.
  Measured: 14 positions refused before are accepted (the #1756 rows `ElementEdits` 20:19, `NestedFor` 42:28
  and 48:21, `Differential` 92:16, `BesideRecordHelper` 24:5, and folds and recursions whose keys read too much,
  `PolyRecBranch` 61:31 among them); 3 refusals move from the callee to the caller, where the fixture wants them
  (`ElementEdits.repeated`, `Differential.t57Repeated`, `t57RepeatedRows`: v1 refuses them too);
  `SubscriptionTapFold`'s `build` grows 53 715 records, not 65 512. The negative controls
  (`run/SanitiserRecordCallbackShared`) trap when the apart occurrence is dropped.
- `res_cond`: the distinct check of §2.9.3 over the result's leaves.
- `reads`, `writes`, `escapes`: the frame's uses of its parameters' positions, its demands' targets that are
  parameter leaves (whatever their verdicts), and its escapes, each as `(j, slot)`. A call contributes its
  callee's footprint projected onto the arguments: a call use reads what the callee's `reads` name below the
  argument, not all of it (`CallFieldStep`'s `rxa2` reads `π1.x.a`).
- `req`: the conjunction of what the frame's accepted `param` demands rely on (§2.9.4).
- `labels`: each callback call of the frame (§2.11.3) and each label of a callee whose function slot is one
  of the frame's parameters.

**Determinism.** The fields are sorted by their words (relative steps compare by their canonical words, not
by intern order), so the contract read off a body does not depend on declaration order or on the order the
walk met things. The experiment checked declaration reversal; the determinism test checks job counts (rule 5).

**A worded code** (§2.13.6) has the contract its words say, read against the call site's own places
(§2.13.6's table, *as contracts*); it is never walked. **A constructor's** contract: the result is a `built`
constructor at the type's place with `C#i ← πᵢ` at each argument slot, `res_cond` the selection of every
argument (a constructor duplicates nothing), no write. **A code with no contract** (a `foreign` without
words, an imported declaration whose module published none, a declaration past its limit) has the
pessimistic contract: every argument read and escaped deep, the result `⊤`, `res_cond no`.

*Amended 2026-11-03 (#1735, #1744, the manager's decision): host objects.* A `foreign`'s unknown result is not
unknown code's. **The rule:** the objects of a `foreign`'s result that its words do not name (a result with no
word, `unknown` or `escaped`; a `foreign` with no words at all) are **host objects**: objects JavaScript made,
or beni objects that escaped before the call returned. Such a result arrives `host`, an arrival and a leaf of
its own (§2.3.4), and never `⊤`. An imported `foreign` is read this way too: its module publishes nothing an
importer applies, so the importer reads its words, or their absence, itself. A parameterless `foreign`
(`Js.null`) is a `host` value. `lent` and `lentoptional` results, and every other source of `⊤` (unknown
code's answer, a worded declaration that is not a `foreign`, a declaration past its limit, an imported one
with no contract), stay `⊤`, except a called value's (§2.11.1, #2132).
- **Why it holds.** A `foreign` body is JavaScript. It reaches a beni object in three ways only: through an
  argument, through what an earlier `foreign` call kept, and through what a beni callback that it calls
  answers. An argument with no word, or `escaped`, escapes deep at the call (§2.4, boundary rule 6); a
  `borrowed` one is "not kept, not in the result", an `unused` one is not read, and an `aliased`,
  `returned` or `stored` one is named by its own arrival (§2.13.6). What an earlier call kept escaped at
  that call. A callback handed to a `foreign` escapes deep with its captures, so what it answers is either
  escaped or made by that call of it, and nothing else in beni holds the latter. A cell's contents written
  through `Js.ref`/`Js.write` are `escaped` arguments. So every beni object that a host leaf names escaped
  at an earlier point, in the frame that made it or in a frame that was handed it.
- **Escapes reach every frame that can name the object.** A frame names an object through a parameter, a
  call's result, a label's answer or supply, or its own site. An escape of a parameter's object is the
  contract's `escapes` (§2.10), applied at the call. **An escape of any other object the result or a
  supply holds** is said by the arrival `host` beside its own arrival: the read-off (§2.10 *Read-off*) says
  a call's or a supply's subtree by the leaves its key holds, and each of the frame's own objects it says
  there (a site, a callee's fresh objects, a label's answer or result) that one of the frame's escapes of
  its own objects holds, read through the calls' keys, gets `host` at that slot too. An escape that holds
  a label's answer may hold what the label was handed, so then each object is asked of each escape by the
  one relation (§2.9.2). The check is by the escape's objects, not its point (an escape in another arm
  also adds it), so it may say more than happened, never less. An escape the read-off is told of after an
  object was said (a group's delivery, §2.12) adds `host` where the object was said, or, said inside a
  subtree described once per place, at every slot of its list.
  Before this, `g ⊤ = y = [ 1, 2 ]; keep y; y` said `res ε fresh`, its caller edited `g ⊤` in place, and
  JavaScript read the edit (`run/SanitiserEscapedResult`; also through a callee's fresh list and a
  callback's answer). Master's v1 says `res esc1` for the same body.
- **What a `host` leaf is.** A write of a target that holds one is refused `escaped`. A holder's `host`
  leaf holds no target that is still writable, so it is in no bucket of the holder index (§2.8) and in no
  bucket of the escape index. In the one relation (§2.9.2) a `host` leaf may be the same object as another
  `host` leaf or a `⊤` one, and is apart from every other leaf, with no condition. That is sound because
  the relation is only read to accept a write: a target that a host leaf may name is refused itself, and a
  target that no host leaf names is, by the two points above, an object no host leaf holds. A `host`
  arrival is an atom: the same at every slot, held wide as `fresh`, `⊤` and a shared value are.
- **What it buys.** `Task.scope`'s `openScope` builds its handle with `Js.from`, stores its finaliser with
  `Js.set` (so the record escapes) and holds `Js.construct`'s `Set`: its result is `ε host`, not
  `ε fresh ⊤`, and the scope label's supply is apart from the lists the callback edits (`Control` 17:5,
  #1735). A spawned fiber's or a finaliser's hold on those lists is still refused at the edit (`escaped`).
- **Text and block.** It prints `host`. The block's arrival kind 5 is `host` (block version 18 on its lineage; 19 once joined with the write trees, 2026-11-03).
- **As built (2026-11-03).** `Host.zig` keeps the frame's escapes of its own objects and what the read-off
  said; `Rows`/`Groups` give a `foreign` the `host` result; `Distinct.overlapRaw`, `Holders` and
  `Resolve.judge` read the leaf. Ledger over every root: one position moves accepted → refused,
  `BallMachine` `Main` 36:5, where `Control.run`'s edit of `m.world◆.balls` is now accepted at 17:5 and
  relies on its caller to separate the balls (the program was refused at 17:5 before); eleven move refused →
  accepted (`Task` 1198:28, five in browser-tea's `Tea`, `Record.copy`'s callers in Sternhalma and
  bike-wars, `Control` 17:5). The cost table's growth does not move; `Schema.shapeOf` costs 283 388 records
  (272 813 before) and `shapesOf`'s growth is 6 744 (5 622): the escaped objects its result now says.
  *Amended 2026-11-03 (the join with #1714's read-off shortcuts):* a call read off by its callee's arrivals
  renamed (`CallGraft.slotArrivals`, *a parameter's path grafted*) or by its callee's node grafted
  (`AtomGraft`) never expands its leaf, so the read-off asks `hosted` of the call's fresh objects itself:
  where an escape of the frame reaches them, `host` is said beside the arrivals. Without it `core/Schema`'s
  compiled run answered its issues `fresh` only, and so did `read`, `decode` and every caller (17 summaries).

*Specified 2026-11-02 (#1714), not built: a contract is a tree of shared subtrees.* A contract names one entry
per result slot and one effect per parameter slot, and a reader walks every entry. So a type whose two parts
are one type doubles its slots at each level: `w₁ x = ( x, x )`, `wₖ x = wₖ₋₁ (wₖ₋₁ x)` has 2^(2^(k-1))
result slots (`w₅`: 6.1 million records, master's v2: 968), a write below a doubling record reads 2ᵏ slots,
and `wrap r = [ r ]` names every slot of `r`'s type at `[*]`, so a call costs its argument's width (#1714's
report, F4). Master's v2 printed a shared subtree as `.1 = .0`. The contract becomes:

- **Result trees.** `res` and a supply's `res` are one node of a tree over the result's relative steps: a node
  is its `open` bit, its arrivals (a sorted run) and its kids, `(step, node)` pairs sorted by the step's
  words. Nodes are hash-consed in the module's contract table by that content, so equal subtrees are one node
  and `wₖ`'s result is k nodes. An arrival names a parameter's slot from the parameter's root, which does not
  depend on where the node sits, so sharing is exact. The flat entries of §3.5 are the tree's paths. A reader
  that asks one slot walks its steps from the root; a reader that needs every slot walks each node once.
- **Effects as trees.** `reads`, `writes`, `escapes` and a supply's `kept` are, per parameter, a tree of the
  same kind: a node is what it says at its own slot (nothing, shallow, deep; for a write also `fields`) and its
  kids. **Covering effects fold:** a node whose own slot and every object slot below it are read, or escape,
  is that one deep effect, and its kids are dropped. A shallow write of every slot below is not folded: a deep
  write is `consumed` (§2.8), which says more. Nothing else changes: a fold names the same slots.
- **Arrivals by structure.** An `open` node with an arrival `π_j·s` reads, at its slot `q·r`, the objects at
  `π_j·(s·r)` for every `r` its place takes (the `q… π_j·s*` entry of a type variable's slot today). The
  read-off writes a parameter's subtree read by structure as that one node, never one entry per slot below
  (§2.3.1's *written out* rule is withdrawn for it). A caller reads such a node **lazily**: an asked slot `q·r`
  is the argument projected at `s·r`, made when it is asked and kept in the call's instantiation (below).
  **Owner's decision when it is measured:** #1706 measured an eager by-structure form at `Schema.shapeOf`
  540 000 records against the 215 000 of slots written out. The lazy reader must keep a call's cost flat in
  its argument's width (tests 151, 155, 171) without moving `Schema.shapeOf`'s row past today's. If it
  cannot do both, the choice is the owner's.
- **The read-off describes a value once per place.** `describe` (§2.10 *Read-off*) gives a node per
  `(value, result place)`, not per result path: a value read at a place is described by the place's steps,
  so a value of a doubling type is k descriptions. A call's leaf is described by the callee's result tree
  instantiated (below); a join of arms is the union of their nodes.
- **A call's instantiation is a tree** (§2.11.2): per callee node, once per call site, the caller's node for
  it. An arrival `π_j·s` becomes the description of argument `j` projected at `s`; `fresh`, `shared`, `cb`
  and `⊤` are what they are today. It is the call's representation, built with the call in the frame's call
  columns and read by every reader of the call, never a table of earlier answers.
- **Join and `within`** (§2.10 *Lattice*) are pointwise over two trees: a union of nodes is a node of the
  arrivals' union and the kids' unions, hash-consed. A join still never drops a result slot.
- **Text.** A kid equal to an earlier sibling prints as `.1 = .0`; a folded effect prints as today's deep
  effect (`π1ε*`).
- **Determinism** is unchanged: kids sort by their steps' canonical words, arrivals as today, so a tree does
  not depend on intern order.
- **Done means:** `w₃ / w₄ / w₅` within master's v2 (287 / 514 / 968) and linear in k; the doubling family
  (149, 231, 257, 154, 157, 168, 169, 147, check_test's tuple DAG, `EvidenceDagBuildDepth32` without its
  limit line) and the width family (151, 155, 171) pass; the ledger moves no verdict from accepted to
  refused, and no summary says less.

*As built (#1714), in part.* **Result trees** are built (§3.5): drafts hold arrivals and whole subtrees, a
commit unites them into one hash-consed tree, and every reader walks it; no flat result entry is kept.
**Reads** are one tree a parameter, a deep read covering what is below it (`Forest.foldDeep`); a call use
of a parameter's subtree of more than 16 objects takes the callee's read tree whole. A parameter's whole
subtree of more than 16 objects, read at its own acyclic place, is **one open arrival**, and a caller
describes the argument's value there; by-structure continuation is exact only where no cycle is below the
place (with `⟲` the result's level paths fold otherwise than the parameter's), so a slot with a cycle below
it is still written out. *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1715):* a parameter's subtree that the result returns **at its own path** (`same t =
t`, the result's slot and the parameter's slot one path) folds below it exactly as the result's slot does, so it
is one open arrival there too, cycles below or not, once written out it would name more than
`Subtree.written_max` (256) slots. Over five mutually recursive types with a list and a `Maybe` of each other
(`K0 … K4`), `same : K0 → K0` named so many that it passed `ownership_summary_size` at any allowance; it is now
`res ε… π1ε`, and a caller reads each slot of it as of any open arrival. Until the next amendment, below that size
the slots were written out: their readers cost less than the open node's (`Dict.descend` 37 191 records written
out, 66 105 open). *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714, the manager's decision):* the size gate is withdrawn.
A subtree returned at its own path is the one open arrival at any size: that node, `ε… π_j·ε` at a result's
root, is the **identity tree**, recognised at a call by its structure (§2.11.2, *the identity control*). The
open node is made cheap to read instead: a below key reads an open `π_j·s` at each slot below as argument `j`
projected there, never through a key of its own per slot; a parameter's whole subtree at the slot's own place is
that one open item, which the read-off says as it says a parameter's subtree (open where its paths fold as the
slot's, slot by slot otherwise); and a commit drops an arrival `π_j·(s·r)` at `p·r` that an open, non-deep
`π_j·s` at `p` says by structure (`Normal.zig`), so the two spellings are one tree. `Dict.descend` costs 24 895
records (26 448 written out); `Dict.removeMin` 25 704 (23 589), all at growth 0. Not in a callback's supply: there the open node read back at a caller's argument
names its top slot only, which says less than the slots written out (`Codec.Decode.decodeString`). Where nothing the frame reads grows and no place below the slot is on a cycle, the
read-off **describes a value once per (value, place)** and a call once per (callee node, place). The text
prints a kid equal to an earlier sibling as `.1 = .0`, for reads too (`π1#1.2 = π1#1.0`). A defect of the
slot domain's base went with the trees: a result kept the draft's label numbers while the labels were
sorted, so a `cb` arrival could name another callback's answer, and a write onto it was accepted that the
sanitiser catches (#1737, `run/SanitiserCallbackLabels`); the result is put with the sorted numbers, as the
supplies were. **Not built:** `writes`, `escapes` and `kept` are still flat lists and the covering fold is
not applied to them; a call's instantiation is not yet per callee node. *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714):* a call's
paths into one argument are projected by **one walk** of it (`Paths.zig`): the occurrences of the callee's
`req` on one parameter, and the writes of one argument whose targets are a projection of it. An arm or a step
two paths share is read once, its tags made once; a path alone, at its end, or at a value read by its kind
is projected on by `project` from there, so each path's projections and their order are unchanged. Before,
each path walked the argument again, and an `else if` chain of D arms made each arm's tags once a path:
`chainCallCold` (`Lib.incAll v`, three writes and three occurrences, the call's records less the plain
chain's and its demands) cost 626 / 1 042 / 1 833 at D = 8 / 16 / 32, now 246 / 278 / 301. Measured (Debug): `w₃ / w₅ / w₈ /
w₁₀` 1 081 / 287 / 1 575 / 5 991, linear in the result's depth; `EvidenceDagBuildDepth32` has no limit line;
`Schema.shapeOf` 256 826 (256 618 before); ledger: no verdict moves, 11 limit lines fewer, none new.
*Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714):* the read-off names the result slot of a callee's slot **once per `(from, q,
slot)`** (`ReadOff.destsOf`): the steps from a key's prefix (or a position's slot) down to an item's slot,
replayed below the result slot `q`, are the same for every item at that slot, so the one result slot they reach
is kept with the read-off, as a key's caller slot is once per entry (`Relation.Eval.feedBelow`). Before, each
item of a key below a prefix walked up from its slot and replayed the steps again (one record a step, twice):
`bench/corpus`'s `Codec.Decode.oneOfHelp`, whose recursive `Result Error a` reads 519 items at a few dozen
slots a round, spent 69 000 of its 251 712 growth records there and now needs 182 461 (`path` 156 606 → 91 484).
A slot the steps reach several of (a `⟲` that stands for several levels) is replayed each time. Every summary is
the same; no account grows (`Dict.descend` 24 180 → 21 138, `Fields16` 149 250 → 137 922). Where `from` is
`q` itself (a call's result read at its own root, a cast's), a slot whose canonical steps extend `q`'s is that
slot (§2.1, *one position, one name*: its steps replayed are its name; checked over the ledger's roots and core,
no slot differs), so it is read off its name, two records, and never replayed. `Schema.shapesOf`'s growth 2 581
→ 0, `boxOf` 6 384 → 1 708, `asVariant` 5 837 → 1 810, `variantList` 5 041 → 183, `fieldList` 3 645 → 0,
`describedOf` 1 622 → 0; `Schema.shapeOf` 263 634 → 258 000, `Dict.descend` → 19 896, `oneOfHelp` → 179 864.
*Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714):* those result slots are no longer remembered per `(from, q, slot)`. A read — a value
below `from` described at result slot `q`, or a call root's callee entries read at the root's path (`feedBelow`, which
remembered one caller slot per `(root path, entry)`) — has **a column** (`Dests.zig`): an entry per slot the read
meets, kept in the slots' order. A leaf's named slots, a key's items and the slots below a call's slot are entered
as one batch, in that order, before they are read; an item delivered later is entered when it arrives. Each entry
is made once, from its nearest ancestor in the column: that ancestor's result slots (`q`, or the root's path, for
none) the remaining steps on, one record a step, as `Slots.replay` takes them; below `q = from` a slot named by
`q`'s steps and its own is itself, one record. A slot whose canonical name is not its parent's and one more step
(a fold, `relBelow`'s walk) is replayed from `q`. A column covers only what its read meets: filled up front over
`belowAll(from)`, `Schema.shapeOf` and `shapesOf` pass the limit. Every summary is the same; growth is worse
nowhere and better in 31 accounts, totals 8 431 down. `Schema.shapeOf` 258 000 → 220 738, `shapesOf` 24 348 → 22 195,
`describedHost` 6 927 → 4 956, `Fields16` 136 119 → 132 529, `Dict.descend` 19 896 → 19 500; `variantList`'s growth
183 → 0, `boxOf` 1 708 → 1 356, `asVariant` 1 810 → 937.
*Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714):* a draft's join is pointwise (*Lattice*), as it was specified. `Forest.unite` had a
second mode for a contract joined into a draft: at a node where the joined side brought an open arrival, every
plain arrival of the node moved into the open run, so a plain `fresh` at a slot also stood at every slot below it.
That made a draft that a round had read plain say more than the round did: `Codec.Decode.oneOfHelp`'s validation
round read its own candidate's `π3[*]*` at every slot below `[*]`, 23 `cb` arrivals where the inference round had
read one, and took a fifth round (an inference defect). The mode is gone. 22 roots' summaries change, each an
arrival that the join had made open and that is now plain where it was said (`RecordTree.deepest`
`#0.0.kids[*]#0.0.kids… fresh` → `#0.0.kids[*]#0.0.kids fresh`, `SplitArmsJoin.update` `ε… π2ε fresh` → `ε fresh,
ε… π2ε`); no verdict moves and no limit line changes. Where a slot below loses `fresh` (11 summaries: `Conduit`'s
and `BikeWars`' `update`, `ListPersistence.walk`), the parameter's arrival at it stays, so a caller decides the
same; sanitised probes of the shape through callers that edit the result's lists in place, the argument live and
dead, accept and refuse as before and run the same.

### 2.11 Calls

*Replaced 2026-11-02 (#1685). Until then a call grafted its callee's class onto the arguments lazily, as a
view read one step at a time, and κ crossed the call through `inst` atoms. A call is now instantiated once.*

#### 2.11.1 The callee

A call's callee is, in this order: a member of the frame's recursive group (its candidate, §2.12); a
declaration of the module checked before (its contract); a worded declaration (its words, §2.13.6); an
imported declaration (its published contract, §3.6, or the pessimistic one); a constructor; a derived or
user `eq`/`compare` that `Dispatch` names (§2.13.13); a function **value** (§2.11.3–4). A call whose result
and arguments all cross is harmless: no contract is read.

*Amended 2026-11-06 (#2132): a published contract is a call's only at the call's arity.* A declaration with no
parameters, called with arguments, is a function value, and what it publishes is what its body answers: `res ε fresh`
for `mk = Pt`, arity 0, which says nothing of what a call does. Read as the contract of `Lib.mk [] k`, it let `k` go
free while the result held it, and the sanitised run trapped. The one reading of a block for a call is
`Callees.publishedCall`, and these go through it: a call and a pipe, a method call, a function reference used as a
value (§2.11.4), and a dispatch site's evidence. Each reads the chain's end and then each name of the alias chain
(R-5.5.6), since a private end publishes nothing and its alias publishes its contract. A contract is read only at the
call's arity. What it answers then, for a value:
- **What its body is**, when that is a lambda or a constructor, or a choice, `case` or `let` whose every arm is one of
  these, a declaration, or a local function, none with captures: the called contract at `ε` (§2.11.3, *A value's
  lambda*), of the same arity, the join of the arms'. In its own module, that code, or that join.
- **Else the pessimistic contract**, its result `host`. So `mk = build ⊤`, `mk = r.f` and a let around a lambda with
  captures escape every argument and answer `host`, imported or in their own module. This is a refusal for want of a
  contract, not a finding about the program: `x = (Lib.mk [] k).a; s = show x; List.push k 2` over `mk = build ⊤`
  runs correctly, and it is refused because a block says nothing of what the call does. A value of the same form may
  keep what it is handed in a fiber, and the caller is the same text (`run/SanitiserValueKept`, accepted before and wrong). So
  the caller cannot be accepted on today's block. #2152 holds the precision.
- **Why `host` holds and `⊤` was too much.** A value's function is made when its module starts, so no frame's
  object is in its closure. It reaches a frame's object only through an argument, which escapes deep at the call, or
  as something that escaped at an earlier point. So §2.10's argument for a `foreign` holds as it stands: an object
  that no host leaf names is an object it does not hold, and one it may name is refused `escaped`. A value's closure
  holds what its module made for it, or a shared value. A shared value's cell is written (`Queue.offer` writes a
  top-level `q`), but what goes in has escaped at that call, and what comes out of such a call is `host`, refused as a
  target: `run/SanitiserValueCallQueue`. `⊤` said
  more: a later `List.push k 2` of a list the call never saw was refused, as held by the call's result. A function
  **parameter** stays unknown code: its closure holds its caller's objects, escaped or not.
A worded declaration and a `foreign` keep their words, stated over the scheme. An alias of a declaration with
parameters keeps that declaration's contract, whose arity is the call's. `(x.m) a` is two calls: the method at its
own instruction, and a call of what it answers, a function value (§2.11.3), never the method again. Evidence is read
at the declaration's own arity: its reader looks for writes, and a value's own contract has none, since a writer held
in a top-level value is refused where it is made (`once`, §2.11.4).
Pinned: `run/SanitiserValueCallImported` and its `…Apart`.

#### 2.11.2 Instantiation, once per call site

A call `k` of a code with contract `C` and argument values `a1…an`:

1. **Uses.** Each argument `x.p` is used at `(x, p)`, kind `call`, with the callee's footprint for that
   parameter (§2.7): the caller's liveness reads the argument where `C.reads` names it.
2. **The result** is the value `ref(call k, root position)` when `C.returns`, else `bot`; `scalar` when
   `C.cross`. Its leaves are **expanded** on demand (§2.9.2 step 4) by the call's **instantiation**: per
   result slot of the caller's result place, the leaves of `C.res`'s arrivals projected onto the arguments.
   `π_j·s` projects `a_j` by the steps of `s` (a `⟲` is projected into a literal exactly, as the values one
   or more levels below at the same place, and into a reference by its descendant paths, never its own
   storage); `fresh` is the atom `fresh k`; `cb L` the call's label instantiation (§2.11.3); `⊤` is `⊤`. The
   instantiation is built once per call per candidate generation (§2.12) and never re-read lazily. The walk
   of a `⟲` into a literal meets each (value, place, literal route) once, not once per path (#1714): two
   arrivals by one literal route are one position, and they give the same projections. Its leaves carry no
   route, so it meets each (value, place) once. `xᵢ = if n == i then Node xᵢ₋₁ [] Leaf else xᵢ₋₁` names
   `xᵢ₋₁` twice, 2ⁱ paths but i + 1 literal routes.
   *The identity control* (#1714, 2026-11-03, the manager's decision): where the callee is settled when the
   caller is walked (a contract from an earlier group, an import, words; never a member of the caller's own
   group), its `res` is the identity tree on parameter `j` (`ε… π_j·ε` and nothing else, `Trees.identity`),
   it writes nothing of `π_j`, and `a_j` is at the call's own place, the call's result **is** `a_j`: the walk
   gives the call the argument's value, with no per-slot instantiation. A called code's closing call (`pick c = if c then idf else idf`) has
   parameters for arguments and no argument expression, so no place to compare: it takes the ordinary path (#2076). The call is still a call: its uses,
   writes, `req`, escapes and labels are read from `C` as above. It is recognised by the contract's structure,
   never a name or an annotation, at any size, and it is exact: the result's objects at every slot are the
   argument's there, so its separation is the argument's own. A generic identity (`idt : a → a`,
   `ε… π1ε*`) no longer lumps every object of the argument at the result's top slot, so a write through it
   targets only what it writes (`GenericResultHeldImported.nested` no longer writes `π1ε`). `wrap (ident r)`
   costs 1 611 records at 10 calls and 6 313 at 40, against 1 571 / 6 153 for `wrap r` (was 2 585 / 10 197).
3. **The separation** of the call's result is `C.res_cond` instantiated on the arguments: the distinct check
   over the projections of its selected occurrences, under the routed rule (§2.9.3). It is computed once per
   call, on first need; a cycle through the call's own condition reads it as `no`. *Amended 2026-11-03
   (#1225, #1714):* where every selected occurrence's parameter is handed a caller's parameter whole at its own
   place (§2.10 *a parameter's path grafted*), and no two parameters one, the instantiation is the selection
   with each parameter renamed (`CallGraft.sel`): the projections it replaces are those parameters' own slots,
   so the distinct check finds exactly the callee's pairs. `nondup ⇐ sel π1{.a…, .a…[*]*}` of a 256-step path
   cost 2 112 records an instantiation, a walk of the argument a step.
   *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714, owed test (c)):* an expansion of the call's result reads a parameter's arrival
   at its path (§2.10 *an arrival keeps its path*).
4. **Writes.** Each `(j, s, deep)` of `C.writes` is a demand at the call (`writer`, or `consumed` when deep,
   §2.8) whose targets are `a_j` projected by `s` (a shallow write's target is the position's own storage);
   the other operands are the other arguments and the other paths of `a_j` that `C.reads` names; it relies
   on `C.req` instantiated on the arguments. A demand's text names its written path by the base's root and the
   steps of `s` (`Walk.Demand.write_rel`), replayed only when its line is printed, on an account of its own
   (#1225, 2026-11-03): naming it at the call cost four records a step. *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714):* that instantiation is the call's, not
   the demand's: it is made once a call and every write of the call relies on the one result, which the frame's
   `req` gathers once (§2.9.4). A demand's own judgement adds to it apart. Before, each of n writes of one call
   instantiated `C.req` (n occurrences) again and added it again: `caller w = wall w` with 256 written fields
   reached the growth limit, and `fresh` cost 42 653 → 167 333 records at 64 → 128 fields (now 3 037 → 6 309).
5. **Escapes.** The objects at `C.escapes`' projections are escaped at the call (§2.4), deep.
6. **Labels.** Each of `C.labels` is instantiated (§2.11.3).

*Specified 2026-11-03 (#1714): a projection carries a route set.* A projection (items 2–4) walks the
argument's value, and an `alt` sends the walk down each arm under that arm's tag. A value two arms both
reach (`xᵢ = if … then xᵢ₋₁ else if … then b else xᵢ₋₁`, or the arms `Rose [ sN, Rose aᵢ ]` that share
`sN`) was walked once per arm, and each walk made its own entries: a chain of n such choices gave 2ⁿ
entries of one leaf, and the distinct check compared them (`reads two positions of one image through a chain
of n choices`: 6 706 / 86 834 records at n = 2 / 4, past the limit at 8).

- **The walk.** The selection's walk (`Routed.zig`, the occurrences of one parameter projected together) reads
  the argument's values in decreasing value id. A value's kids are made before it, so every arrival at a
  value is known before the value is read. Two arrivals at one value with the same remaining paths and the
  same literal route (§2.9.3: built steps only, an arm adds none) are one item, whose **routes** are the
  union of theirs (a route set of §2.3.5, `Routes.Set`). An arm's tag is put in front of every route of the
  set as one node (`pre`) when its choice comes before every choice the set names, which is the order an
  enclosing `case` gives its arms; otherwise the routes are written out with the tag merged in. An output
  is `(leaf, route, routes)`: the leaf is reached under each route of the set, merged with the leaf's own
  tags (set 0 is the one unconditional route). A route set's routes never hold together: two arrivals at
  one value by one literal route parted at an `alt`, by two arms of one choice. So one item names its object
  at most once, as the arrivals did, each alone.
- **The distinct check reads route sets** (§2.9.3). An entry carries its projection's routes. Wherever the
  check asks whether two entries hold together (a pair of a group, an atom's entries, a callback's answer),
  it asks whether a route of one and a route of the other merge (`Routes.Table.setsMeet`): the sets are
  walked from their latest choices together, each node's tags merged into a running tag list, which drops
  every choice later than both remaining sets name, so the walk is asked once per pair of nodes and running
  list. An entry's expansion (a call's parts) keeps its routes; a vouched block keeps one entry per leaf
  and route set. Equal route sets under equal tags hold together when the set is not empty.
- **Other readers** of a projection (write targets, §2.11.2 item 4; holders, §2.8) keep the walk by arms,
  each output one tag list, as before.
- **Exactness.** A set is the union of the routes the per-arm walk gave, and each question the check asks of
  two entries is asked of every pair of their routes at once: every verdict and condition is the one the
  per-arm entries gave. Only the number of entries changes.
- *As built (#1714, 2026-11-03).* `Routed.zig` (L8) replaces `Paths.zig`: one walk for the selection's
  occurrences, a call's writes of one argument, a callee's reads at a use and a choice read deep at a use. An
  item keeps one tag list while one arrival reaches it and takes a route set only when a second does (the sets
  of all its arrivals united once, when it is read), so a walk with no shared value costs what the walk by
  arms did. A set of one route is that route's list. `Coexist.zig` (L2, split from `Routes`) holds the meet
  of two sets: lists written out (a `flat` set or a `join` of them) go into the tree of tails that
  `anyPair` reads, one block a set, and any other set is read by the walk above. Write targets carry their
  set in the leaf (`Value.Leaf.routes`); the operands' deep read (`Routed.leavesOf`) gives each element
  once under its set; the live holders, read by their tags (§2.8), meet a target route by route, as before.
  Measured (Debug): `reads two positions of one image through a chain of n choices`, `f` 6 706 / 86 834 at
  n = 2 / 4 and past the limit at 8, is 3 909 / 6 236 / 10 967 at n = 8 / 16 / 32, and the test passes;
  `chainCallCold` 246 / 278 / 301 → 280 / 336 / 407; test 21's `read32` 11 034 → 10 530 records. The
  ledger moves no verdict and no summary; every growth on the cost table stays 0, totals +0.3 % to +5 %
  (the sets an arm's arrivals unite). **Not done:** `call over a choice whose arms share a subtree` (six more
  arms 2 602 / 5 178 records at N = 8 / 32, ×2.0, bar ×1.5). Its growth is now the walk's alone: an `alt`'s
  leaf set (`Leaves.arms`) merges the shared tower's N elements once per arm, N × D (`join2`), since the
  tower sits in each arm's set under that arm's tag and no node of it is shared.
- *As built (#1714, 2026-11-03), the shared subtree.* A leaf set has a **route wrap** node (`Leaves.zig`):
  a set whose elements are all unconditional (no route, no wrap below it), under a route set. Where an
  `alt`'s join meets one such node on both sides, under any tag wraps and at most one route wrap each, it
  makes one route wrap over it whose routes are the two sides' united (`Routes.unite`), in one step. A
  join that looks inside opens the wrap one level, as it does a tag wrap. The iterator gives an element
  below the wrap the wrap's routes. `alike` and `minus` read two wraps over one node as not alike, without
  walking it. The elements and their routes are those the join key by key gave. Measured (Debug):
  `call over a choice whose arms share a subtree`: six more arms 2 602 / 5 178 records at N = 8 / 32
  (×2.0) are now 1 778 / 1 812 (×1.0), and the test passes. The ledger moves no verdict and no summary. The
  cost table moves by −0.6 % (`removeMinF`) or less, and every growth is still 0.

*Specified 2026-11-03 (#1714): a write onto a caller's parameter stops at the parameter.* Item 4 projects
each write of `C.writes` onto its argument, and a callee whose writes double (`t₁ ( a, b ) = touch a + touch
b`, `tₖ ( a, b ) = tₖ₋₁ a + tₖ₋₁ b`) has 2ᵏ writes and a `req` of 2ᵏ occurrences: `caller w = tₖ w` made 2ᵏ
demands and instantiated 2ᵏ occurrences (1 591 / 25 966 records at k = 4 / 8), and `f` handing `tₖ` a
doubling literal over one list projected 2ᵏ paths onto the same list.

- **Writes and `req` are trees** (§2.10 *Effects as trees*, extended): `writes` per parameter a hash-consed
  tree whose node says what it writes at its own slot (nothing, shallow, deep) and its kids; `req` per
  parameter a tree of the same kind whose node says which occurrence it holds at its slot (none, plain,
  apart; deep or not). A doubling callee's writes and `req` are then k nodes.
- **The stop.** A write node whose argument projects, by an exact prefix (no `[*]`, no `⟲`, no `alt`), onto
  an exact leaf of one of the caller's parameters at slot `c` is not projected on. Its target is that leaf
  with the callee's node **grafted** below `c`. Its demands are one per **state**: the node walked
  together with the trie `T(c)` of the caller's slots at and below `c` that something else in the frame names
  (a holder live at the call, another argument of the call, an escape, a later use of a holder). A route
  that leaves `T(c)` never comes back, so the routes that leave it at one trie node, by steps to one place,
  and reach one write node are one state, and the frame cannot tell them apart. The demand names its least
  route in canonical order. Each route of a state has the verdict its least route has (the argument of the
  removed `TransferGroups` design, #1412, with "use node" read as "write node"). `caller w = tₖ w` is one
  demand (one state). A K-wide `T` whose root's list and K children's lists are written is two: the
  children's lists leave the root by K steps to one place, `T`'s, and the root's list by its own.
- **The caller's contract** takes the grafted node: its `writes` at `c` are the callee's node, and its
  `req` the callee's `req` node grafted at `c` (an instantiation onto one exact parameter leaf is the
  occurrence tree moved to `c`; the routed rule and the distinct check of §2.9.3 find no pair in it that
  the callee's own selection did not have).
- **A literal argument** is projected once per (tree node, value): `f` hands `tₖ` the value `xₖ = ( xₖ₋₁,
  xₖ₋₁ )` and the walk meets `(nodeᵢ, xᵢ)` by two routes. The second route reaching a pair whose subtree
  selects a plain occurrence at an object is that object twice: the instantiated `req` is `no` there and
  then, and the write's targets are the pair's leaves once.
- *As built (#1714, 2026-11-03).* `writes` are one tree a parameter, kept as the reads are (`Table.writesOf`,
  §2.10 *Effects as trees*): a plain mark writes its slot, an open one its slot and everything below. The
  summary prints them written out, an entry a slot, as the flat runs did; a block encodes them as the reads
  (version 18; 19 once joined with `host` arrivals and `fed` occurrences, 2026-11-03). A reader that takes a write a slot at a time (a closure's captures, `once`, a write that
  does not stop) writes the tree out (`Table.writesFlat`). `Graft.zig` (L8) holds the stop. Its demands are
  judged on **every** object of their routes, not on the least route alone: a subtree that writes every object
  below its slot (the test of *Stored selections fold exactly*, made on the write tree) is one target, the deep
  projection there (`↓s`, §2.3.1); elsewhere each written slot is its own target, as before. So the verdict
  and every condition a demand gathers are the per-route ones, and `T(c)` decides only how the targets are
  grouped into demands: `T(c)` is read as the frame's positions below `c` along the tree's steps (a holder
  bound by a pattern, an operand named by a projection). A slot `T(c)` names is read step by step, past it a
  whole subtree; the demand of a state is named by its least route. The stop holds only where the canonical
  names are the steps joined (no `[*]`, `⟲` or `◆` in the tree, no place on a cycle above `c`). The
  caller's `req` from such a call is the callee's moved to the arguments' slots (`Graft.movedReq`) when
  every parameter it asks is handed an exact slot of a parameter of the frame and no two of those slots
  are one at or below the other; otherwise it is instantiated as before. A literal (a tuple, a constructor
  or a record, a tree of plain steps) is walked once per `(node, value)`, a demand a written slot there,
  named by the first route: two routes to one value are one demand. Read part by part (a parameter asked
  deep apart and plain), a literal's selection asks its plain occurrences on the whole values first, and a
  value they name twice makes it `no` before the walk by routes (`Graft.plainsOnLiteral`); those plain
  occurrences are projected as the walk by routes projects them, one walk a parameter (#1714: `f` over the
  doubling literal 365 / 826 records at depth 4 / 8, was 365 / 1 229 with a projection an occurrence). The fold is
  made on `req` at the read-off (`Graft.fold`); a full slot with nothing asked below it is kept as it is
  (it names the same objects). Measured (Debug): `caller w = tₖ w` 1 609 / 26 226 at k = 4 / 8 and past
  the limit at 10 is 240 / 298 / 364 at k = 8 / 10 / 12, one demand; the K-wide caller 850 / 2 078 / 5 878
  at K = 8 / 16 / 32 (K + 1 demands) is 441 / 793 / 1 497, two demands; `f` over the doubling literal
  546 / 11 008 at depth 4 / 8 (one demand a path) is 231 / 464, one demand. The ledger moves no verdict;
  72 summaries differ, each asking at least what it asked (a deep occurrence moved where the instantiation
  wrote its parts out, `s*~` for `s~, s[*]*~`). Lines merge where routes share a state or a value
  (`ParamLeafByNode`'s `alone` and `deep`, `CallOtherPathsKeys`, `LevelPlacesCall`); the merged line names every
  route it covers: a state's further targets by their least routes, a second route into a literal's `(node,
  value)` by its own steps (n + 1 routes for a doubling literal of depth n). **Not built:** `req`
  as a tree (the fold keeps it linear here).
- *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1714, owed test (c)): the walk carries its path.* The stop's walk of the callee's tree
  extends the argument's path a step a kid, as it extends the place, so each node knows its path; a target is
  the parameter's objects at that path (`canon`, or `below` when the subtree is written whole), exactly the
  projection of the walk's steps onto the argument, never replayed from the argument's root. `call256`'s write
  graft cost 1 543 records (a replay of the 256 steps, its canonical name, the walk); it is now the walk and the
  group's text (1 029, half a record a step each for the kid, its extension, `fullAt` and the least route).

*Specified 2026-11-03 (#1714): stored selections fold exactly.* A stored selection (a contract's `req`, a
`res_cond`, a supply's condition) names each object slot it asks. A slot every object slot of whose subtree
is asked plain, the slot's own included, is stored as one deep occurrence `s*` (§2.9.1), its occurrences
below dropped. The test is exact and made on the occurrence tree with the place: a node is **full** when its
own slot is asked plain or is no object, and every step its place takes to a slot that is or holds an object
leads to a full kid. A place with a cycle below the slot is never full (its subtree names infinitely many
slots, not stored as a list). The count of objects below a slot (`Place.objectsBelow`, F7) saturates at 16
and is not this test. A deep occurrence asks the same objects the folded occurrences asked, so nothing reads
less: `tₖ`'s `req`, `{.0…0, …, .1…1~}`, is `{.0*, .1.0*, …, .1…1.0*, .1…1~}`, k + 1 occurrences.

#### 2.11.3 Callbacks

A call whose callee is a value reached from a parameter — `f x` with `f` a parameter, `r.on x` with a field of
function type, an element of a list of functions — is a **callback call**. Its label `L` is the parameter's
function slot `(j, s)` and the call's instruction (its origin). In the frame:

- the result is `ref(cb L, root)`, a root of its own whose objects are the label's answer;
- each argument `k` is a **supply**: its leaves are recorded with the label, and after the walk, the slots of
  it that are held by a live holder after the call or by another operand at the call are its **kept** slots;
  the supplied objects of distinct invocations are distinct under the condition the distinct check gives
  over the supply's leaves as a family;
- the arguments are used whole at the call (the callee's footprint is not known).

A label of a callee whose function slot is projected from one of the caller's parameters becomes a label of
the caller, its supplies projected onto the caller's arguments, its origin kept: so a callback handed through
`List.map` to `mapHelp` and back to itself is one label, and a recursive group's labels are finite (one per
callback call instruction reachable, per function slot).
*Amended 2026-11-02 (#1721):* the label's `calls` adds up its sources in the frame: each direct call is one,
each callee label it is passed on to counts that label's `calls`, and two sources that each call it are many.
So `myMap xs f = case xs of … [ x, …rest ] → [ f x, …myMap rest f ]` calls `f` many times: the direct call
and the recursive call's label (once, on the first round) are two. Before, the sources were joined (`once ⊔
once = once`), so `mapHelp`'s label, and with it `List.map`'s, `List.initialize`'s and every recursive walker's,
was once, and a closure that writes a capture was accepted there.
*Amended 2026-11-03 (#1721, through a lambda):* a label passed on **inside a known code that an outer label runs**
— `mp rs f = List.map rs λv → f v`, `f` passed on at the lambda's virtual call — takes the outer labels too,
at every level outward (§2.11.4, #1758). Its `calls` is many where any of them is many: the lambda runs once per
element, so `f` does. Its supplies' condition adds each outer label's supply condition at that label's call, and
a slot an outer label keeps is kept, as the part that arrives from it. Before this, only the lambda's one call
was counted: `mp`'s label was `once`, its supply `sep yes`, nothing kept, and `mp [ k, k ] λv → List.push v 5`
pushed `k` twice in place, through `List.map` and through a hand-written map (`run/SanitiserForwardedLabel`; the
sanitised runs trapped). Sound because the lambda's supply is the outer label's, so each invocation of the passed
label is an invocation of the outer one. Two apart lists through a hand-written map are still accepted
(`run/SanitiserForwardedLabelApart`). A fold's `fed` occurrence, asked of the forwarding lambda (`List.foldl xs
start λx acc → step x acc`), is decided as §2.11.3 *a label's answer handed back* says, with one more arrival: an
answer at the root that is the answer of a label the code passes on to the frame's label `F`, which it hands its
parameter `k` whole as `F`'s argument `k′`, is `fed F k′`. Sound because under that occurrence `F`'s answer is
what it was handed as `k′`, which is the code's `k`, or fresh. Without it, `ownership/CapturedParam`'s `sumBy` is
refused at its caller.
Projected by structure: each part of the caller's argument arrives at its own slot below the supply slot, at
the call's function type, as a direct label's argument does. A callee supply slot of a type variable's place
(`apply : (a → b), a → b`) takes the whole argument, so one arrival there for `{ f0 = a, f1 = b }` would leave
a write of `.f0` with nothing to read. Each part is also judged at the call as a direct label's argument is: a
part held after the call or reached by another part or operand is kept, at its own slot, and the distinct check
over the parts joins the supply's condition (`wrap f a b = ( apply f { f0 = a, f1 = b }, b )` refuses
`wrap g xs xs`). *Amended 2026-11-02 (#1712):* a part that comes partly from unknown code — a callback's answer,
as a fold's accumulator is after the first step, or `choose c x (g ⊤)` — cannot be judged whole (it is
`unknown`), but its known objects can: each is judged on its own, and one held after the call keeps the part's
slot. Before this, the unknown half hid the known one, and `keepFold acc g = ( fold xs acc λ_ a → g a, acc )`
supplied `acc` to `g` unkept.
*Amended 2026-11-03 (#1713):* **a label's answer handed back to it.** A recursive walker that hands its label's
answer back to the label as its argument `k` — a fold's accumulator, `fold rest (f x acc) f` — asked the
supplies' condition of the next invocation of that answer. The answer is unknown code's, so the condition was
`no`, and every write of a fold's accumulator was refused `disjoint (approx)` at the caller, however fresh the
initial value was. Now, at a call that passes the frame's label on, an argument that is the answer of a
direct call of the same function slot `(j, s)`, handed back as the label's argument `k` (the callee's
parameter arrives whole at the supply `k`), is read in that call's condition as what the direct call was
handed as `k`, deep; and the condition gains the occurrence `fed (j, s) k`. At the same call the part is
judged as that argument is: one held after the call (a pending operand, a live local, through the answer
that holds it) keeps the slot, as the answer would. A `fed` occurrence instantiated at a caller is the
caller's own `fed` where the callee's function slot is one of the caller's parameters (the label passes on);
where a known code `K` is applied there, it holds when every arrival of `K`'s result at a slot that holds an
object is `K`'s own parameter `k` or `fresh`; anywhere else it is `no`. Sound because under `fed`, an answer
holds only what it was handed as `k` and objects its invocation made: an invocation's argument `k` is the
initial value or a part of an earlier invocation's argument `k`, each judged at its own call, so the
condition read through the answer asks exactly what it would ask of those objects; a fresh object is
distinct from every object that existed before it. Measured (2026-11-03): v2 accepts `List.foldl xs []
λn acc → List.push acc n`, `List.foldr` and user-written folds alike; a code that answers another argument
(`λx acc → … x`), a capture, or anything else is refused as before; a walker that also holds the answer it
hands back (`a = f x acc` then `[ a, …keepFold rest a f ]`) is refused, where without the judging at the
pass the sanitiser traps. Text: `π3{ε!2}` (the function at `π3ε` answers its argument 2).

At a caller where the label's function value is **known** — a lambda, a local function, a declaration, a
constructor, or an `alt` of them — the label is applied: for each possible code `K`, `K`'s contract is
instantiated (§2.11.2) on the supplies (projected onto the caller) and `K`'s captures. The answer `cb L` is the
least fixed point of that instantiation over the caller's leaves (a fold's accumulator is fed its own
answer: `foldl f acc xs` supplies `cb L` back to `L`), a finite set of leaves; a read of it is solved to that
fixed point, and a value met under a cycle's cut is never an answer of the pair relation (§2.9.2, *The fixed point of the pairs*; *A value under another cut* is #2160). `K`'s writes become demands at
the call (`callsite`): refused `later-use` on a kept slot, relying on the supply's distinctness condition and
on `K.req`; accepted `callback-param` otherwise. `K`'s escapes escape the supplies. `K.once` with `calls`
many refuses `once`.

Where the function value is **unknown** (`⊤`, a call's result, a value stored in a cell), the answer is `⊤`,
every supply escapes, and a supplied object can no longer be written.

*Amended 2026-11-03 (#1773, #1775, #1776): a function value goes where a value goes.* A function value
carries its code's writes and its call count to every call that runs it, along every route a value takes: a
call's result, an argument a callee hands a code, a label's supply, a label's answer. Three routes lost them.
On each, a call ran a function value that no label named, so the writes its code made relying on its callers
(`param`) and how often it ran were judged by nobody, and the sanitised runs read a stale list:

- **A call's result.** `first v f = (g = pick f 0; g v)`, `case List.head fs of Just g → g v`, a callback that
  answers `f` (`answered v λ_ → f`): the call `g v` was unknown code, whose answer is `⊤` and whose arguments
  escape, and it labelled nothing (`run/SanitiserFunctionResult`).
- **A callee's supply.** `each v f = app1 f λg → g v`, `List.map fs λg → g v`: the lambda's label of `g`,
  applied at the callee's label, had the supply as its function value. The application read it as unknown: the
  supplies escaped, the function did not (`run/SanitiserSuppliedFunction`).
- **A callee's own writer.** `withPush use = use λv → List.push v 5`: a supply describes the objects a label is
  handed, never a code, so nothing at the caller said that the handed function writes its parameter, or that
  the callback runs it twice (`run/SanitiserHandedWriter`).

The rule has two halves.

1. **Followed where it can be.** A value that is, by every arrival and under any tags, one parameter function
   slot `(j, s)` of the frame is that slot (`FnRun.oneParam`). A call of it is a callback call of `(j, s)`, a
   label of the frame, as `f v` is. The walk reads the value through the contracts settled when the caller is
   walked (an earlier group's, an import's, words), as the identity control does (§2.11.2): `pick f 0`, `List.head
   fs` and `Just f` taken apart are followed; a lambda of the caller's own group is not. A callee's label
   applied to such a value passes on as that slot's label, with the outer labels' count and supply conditions
   (#1721), as when `f` itself is handed: `app1 f λg → g v` gives `each` the label `π2ε`, `List.map fs λg → g
   v` the label `π2[*]`, `many`.
2. **Escaped where it cannot.** Anywhere else (a choice of two codes, `⊤`, a label's answer, a lambda of the
   caller's own group), the code that runs the value is unknown, so the value escapes there, as an argument of
   unknown code does (§2.4). Only its **function objects** escape: each parameter function slot it arrives
   from, so the contract says `escapes π…` and at each caller the code handed there has escaped, and each
   closure of the frame it is. An escaped closure's parameter writes are `callsite` demands on `⊤`, refused
   `unknown`, and its capture writes are `once` (§2.11.4). Four things run a value as unknown code: a call whose
   callee value is not followed; a label applied to a value that is not; a label handed a closure of the frame,
   directly or as a label the frame passes on, since a supply names objects and never a code; and a callee that
   a known code answers its label to, since the answer goes back to code the frame does not see (§2.11.4,
   #1709, now a parameter's function slot as well as a closure). The value's other objects (a closure's
   captures) do not escape here: they are not run, and the closure's escape makes its capture writes `once`, but for what the
   closure's own code lets escape (#2041).
   A worded row's value (`use List.pop`) does not escape: it writes nothing in place (§2.11.5 *Evidence*). What
   a growing draft adds later is read the same way, through an `escape_fn` subscription (§2.12 *Deliveries*),
   so it too gives function objects only.

*Amended 2026-11-05 (#2059):* what a closure answers leaves with the closure, and so do its captures. A closure run by code the frame cannot
follow hands its answer to whoever runs it, so a capture among the arrivals of its result escapes, and so does what a capture function holds when the
answer is that function's, with every capture supplied to it, label by label (`ClosureAnswers`). A function capture itself stays unescaped unless the
answer's type can hold a function: it runs at its label. **Unless the runner is known and only reads:** a contract whose result, supplies, escapes
and stores name neither the parameter nor an answer of it (`AnswerRead`) keeps the answer inside the call, so `List.map [ (λ⊤ → y), … ] λq → List.length
(q ⊤)` leaves `y` free to edit, and what such a closure runs answers into the same read. A label that is a cell's callback stores its answer, so
it never only reads (`Ref.update r q`). The closure has still escaped for its writes (§2.11.4); only its answer stays. A value that holds a label's answer
and escapes (a closure spawned on it) marks the label `answer_left` (block version 24): a caller's closure there is not escaped for that, but what it answers has
escaped, and the run is not read-only. And what a closure hands a
function it is given, a capture too, is seen by nobody: it escapes whatever runs the closure (`λf → f y`). A closure that arrives in a result as a
`.site` leaf, back through a label's answer, has no structure to carry its captures, so read-off describes them at that slot, once per slot and list
(`ReadOff.describeLeaf`); and `Captures` finds every closure built at an arrival's steps, through each element of a list and each arm of a choice.
Refused that a perfect checker accepts: the bare-closure cases this now shares (`List.map [ c, d ] λq → q ⊤` with `c` a local writer of its own list,
as the amendment below says). Fixtures `run/SanitiserClosureResult`, `run/SanitiserClosureResultApart`.

*Amended 2026-11-05 (#2041):* a closure's own labels of its captures escape with it (`ClosureRuns.zig`). A captured function is not run by the
value's escape, but it is by the code the escape hands to unknown callers: `chain y g = List.map [ (λ⊤ → g y), (λ⊤ → []) ] λq → q ⊤` runs `g`
on `y` in a place no label names, and its write was judged by nobody. So each closure in `fn_escapes`, a captured closure among them, and
each closure an escape reaches (stored by a callee, spawned), which joins `fn_escapes` and so `Closures`' own writes, has the function slots
its contract's labels and `escapes` name escape in turn, a deep escape deep, and a writer handed to `chain` is refused `unknown`. A reading `g` is accepted (`run/SanitiserClosureList`,
`run/SanitiserClosureListApart`). Refused that a perfect checker accepts: a writer of a list the closure itself makes, `λ⊤ → g [ 1 ]`.
*Amended 2026-11-05 (#2050): **a later function.*** A row's footprint says nothing of its callback, so `( y = w zs; ( y, List.update l 0 f ) )`
read nothing of `f`, and a `w` that writes what `f` holds was asked nothing of it. A read of the function at the row would make it an operand at
every pass, which asks `π{[*]…}` plain and refuses rows that share a key the callback does not write (`run/SanitiserPassedTupleRowApart`). So
the supply of a label run at a point asks each function the frame passes on later apart, deep, its own too (`π1{ε*~}`), and no more
(`LaterFunctions.zig`): nothing about what that function is handed. Sound because the later function can reach only what it holds and
what it is handed, and the second is that pass's own supply, judged at it. Fixtures `run/SanitiserLaterFunction`, `run/SanitiserLaterFunctionApart`.

Sound because every call of a function value now runs a code that a label names, or a code that has escaped.
For a label, its writes become demands where the label is applied and its count adds up outward (§2.11.3).
For an escaped code, its writes are refused in the frame that made it. There is no third case. A call of a
value is a call of a closure (a code call), of a choice of them (each arm), of a followed slot (a label), or of
anything else (an escape). A label applied to a value meets a known code (a virtual call), a followed slot
(it passes on), or anything else (an escape). A supply and an answer carry objects, so a closure or a
parameter's function in one escapes. A parameter's escape is projected onto every caller's argument, so a
closure there escapes at that call, or the caller's own parameter escapes, outward. A function value stored
in a cell is read back as `⊤` (§2.13.7), and the closure escaped where it was stored.

Precision. The followed half makes some programs precise that were refused before: a reader reached through a
call's result no longer escapes the list it is handed (`g v` was unknown code and escaped `v`), so the caller
may edit that list in place afterwards (`run/SanitiserFunctionResultApart`, `run/SanitiserSuppliedFunctionApart`).
Refused that a perfect checker accepts: a writer handed through a list of two closures (as a pattern of the
parameter already was), through a lambda of the caller's own group, as a callback's answer, or by a callee to a
label, even on a list nothing else holds. A reader or a core writer handed the same way is accepted
(`run/SanitiserHandedWriterApart`).
*As built (2026-11-03).* `FnRun.zig` (L9). The walk asks `Context.settledParam`, which reads the value with
each walk call's settled contract filled in for that read only (`FnRun.settled`); an evaluation's label asks
`FnRun.oneParam`. A call the walk reads as unknown code keeps its callee in `Walk.runs`, and the evaluation
escapes its function objects; so does a label applied to a value it cannot follow, and every virtual call's answer
whose place holds a closure (an answer that cannot hold one is skipped before it is read). A closure is noted
where the read-off says it into a label's supply (`Put.handed`, from `hosted`), which already walks every leaf of
every supply, direct or passed on, so it costs no reading of its own. A closure's escape goes into
`fn_escapes`, which `Closures` reads after the frame's other escapes and its hand-backs, so a demand already
named by the call that hands a closure back keeps that name. Measured (Debug): the oracle's 1 332 probes, 31 of
them trapping before, 0 TRAP, 0 DIFF; the cost table unchanged in growth.

*Amended 2026-11-05 (#1955): a capture written across the callee's run.* A known code applied at a callee's label
runs inside the callee, while the callee holds what it was handed. Its supplies are judged at the callee (their kept
slots), but a capture the code writes is the caller's object, which the callee may hold too, out of the caller's
sight: a loan of a cell's contents (`v = Ref.get r`, then `f ⊤`, then `List.length v`), since a loan is a holder
behind the barrier the handle `r` does not show, and the answer of another label it holds (`v = g ⊤; f ⊤;
List.length v`, with `g` answering the list the code of `f` edits). Before this the write was judged against the
caller's holders only: `reenter r λ⊤ → Ref.update r λxs → List.push xs 1` was accepted, and the loan read the
edited list in place (copying `1 2`, in place `2 2`). So at every label outward of the virtual call (§2.11.3, the
chain), a capture write has as its **operands** the call's arguments but the one that hands the code (whole when
the label's function slot is the root of that argument, otherwise that argument too), and the answers of the call's
other labels applied to known codes (`Across.zig`). An operand reaches the contents of every cell it holds through
`◆`, because the operand rule (§2.8 step 4) is a relation of objects, not of holders behind a barrier. Sound because
everything a callee can hold of the caller's objects came to it as an argument (a closure callee's captures are
arguments of its call), as an object reached from one (a cell's contents among them), or as a label's answer; a
callee's own allocations are none of the caller's captures, an escaped object is refused already, and a top-level
value is never written. Coarser than a callee-side rule: a capture the callee does not hold across the run is still
refused when an argument reaches it (`reenter r f = (f ⊤; List.length (Ref.get r))` is refused; v1 refuses it too).
A capture of another cell than the arguments reach is accepted (`run/SanitiserCellReentryApart`). Fixture:
`run/SanitiserCellReentry` (direct, through a helper, passed on to another function, a loan answered by another
label, a list answered by another label; the sanitised runs printed the edited contents through the loan).

*Amended 2026-11-05 (#1975): **a taken supply.*** A callee's supply is **kept** or **taken**, and the word says who
may still read the object after the call. It is *kept* when a live holder of the callee, or another operand of the
callback call, reaches the supplied object: a write of it is refused `call` at every caller, whatever the caller
knows, because the callee reads it again (`filter`'s `x`, stored after the predicate answers). It is *taken* when
no such holder is left: the callee never reads the object again, so a write of it is the caller's to judge.

The one holder that does not count is the traversal's own container (§2.13.6, *the index obligation*). A call of a
`taken` row (`traverseAt`) answers one element of its argument 1, and the body reads that container only through
the traversal, once per index, for the rest of the frame. So the relation (§2.9.2) compares the taken result, read
whole, with a leaf of its container's root as two leaves of that root at distinct places (`Taken.zig`): under the
root's separation, the other leaf's slots apart and the element's plain, and never `may` by position. A holder of
the container holds the others. Before this, `mapHelp`'s pending `a` met the element at `π1[*]`, so every traversal's
supply was kept, and `List.map xs λl → List.push l 1` was refused `call` even over a fresh literal. A holder of the
*element* (the local `x`, the taken result stored) meets it as before: that is the same leaf, not the container's.

**What the caller's demand is.** The supply's arrival is the caller's own argument at `[*]`, so a known code's write
of a taken supply is a `callsite` demand on that argument, judged as any write of it. The element is the callback's
exactly when the caller's list is dead after the call or fresh: a live holder is refused `later-use` or `alias`, as a
direct write would be, and a parameter's list makes it the frame's own write of `π1[*]`, which its callers judge in
turn (an `entry` function's have none yet: *As built*, below). The write also relies on the supply's two conditions, which a kept supply never needed.

`sep` is what judging the supply relied on: what the callee's holders and operands keep apart from it. Each supply has
its own. For `List.map`, `indexedMap`, `filterMap` and `concatMap` it reads `sep ⇐ sel π1{ε,[*]*} π2{ε*~}`, and for `foldl`
and `foldr`'s element `π1{ε,[*]*} π2{ε*~} π3{ε*~,ε!2}`, while the accumulator's stays `π1{ε~,[*]*~} π2{ε*} π3{ε*~,ε!2}`, so a
fold that reads its own list writes its accumulator in place. `π1[*]*` plain, each object in an element once, so two
positions of one list and a part two rows share are refused; `π2ε*~`, what the function holds apart from them, so a
capture of the list or of an element is refused. A taken supply is not an owned one: if the condition fails the write is
refused, and nothing is copied. `List.map2` stays kept: it reads with `at`, an `elementof` row, which makes no split (C.7).

`below` (block version 21) is the callee's claim about the value it hands, and it is derived from that value, never assumed. At each direct
call of a label, read-off runs the distinct check over the argument (§2.9.3, `Distinct.sepOf`, `SupplyCond.zig`), family
positions included. So it is `no` for `wrap v f = f [ v, v ]`, a selection on the parameters where it depends on them
(`app v f = f v`: `below ⇐ sel π1{ε*}`), and `yes` only when shown. A capture-held family is the same check in the frame of
the code that makes the call: `g = λf → f [ a, a ]` publishes `no`. At a call that passes the label on, the callee's
`below` is instantiated on the arguments, and inside a known code each outer label's is added too, through the chain
(`opt m f = Maybe.map m λz → f z`: `sel π1{#0.0*}`). A pass inside a known code keeps the callee entry's open mark where no
structure was described at the call: `go v f = app v λz → f z` is `ε… π1ε*`, as `app` is. Closed, a write at `[*]` of `go`'s
supply landed on no entry, so inside another callback (`app [ s, s ] λr → go r λl → List.map l push1`) it never reached
the outer call, and no condition was asked of it. **Only a write below the supply's root asks `below`.** A write of the
root reaches one object, and an object holds no copy of itself, so `wrap v f = f [ v, v ]` with `λl → List.push l 1` and
