   callee's supply owned (R-5.9.5); a lambda sending a capture is once; taggers are callbacks with `need owned`
   (R-5.9.6). The alias form remains a temporary v2 input protocol below; the final API is nominal because `Unify.expand` (`Unify.zig:843–870`) expands a
   non-generalised alias that meets its expansion, so a `Send` passed through a helper annotated `msg → ⊤` would lose
   its class if ownership facts followed only erased types; v2 instead keeps value provenance during migration. At S10 the API changes (`Hosted.job`, `tap`, …, `Cmd.perform`,
   `Sub.on`, `Sub.map` need no row of their own, R-5.9.9).
   **Migration with v1 frozen (S2b/S7→S10).** v2 reads both the existing callable alias and the final nominal
   form; `src/own/` is never edited. Until switch-over, existing platforms/corpus keep `Send msg = msg → ⊤`
   and `send message`, so the whole-corpus v1 diff baseline is unchanged. A v2-only contextual type word
   marks the protocol source: `pub sender type alias Send msg = msg → ⊤` in core/platform packages. It is
   validated as a one-argument function alias returning ⊤. The frontend preserves `sender` type metadata and original alias-use terms before expansion
   (not a new tag in v1's row enum); S7 resolves the protocol role from those terms;
   type equivalence and emitted runtime code stay unchanged. S2b's compatibility test requires the old v1
   inputs/outputs byte-identical, with no adapter in `src/own/`.

   The S7 adapter reads unexpanded BIR alias references and interface alias terms before type erasure
   (#1056), then publishes a v2 callable-port role on its protocol row. If a frontend path cannot retain
   that provenance, add the role column there; never recover it from `msg → ⊤` or a type name. Cold/warm and
   cross-package tests must include wrappers annotated with the expanded function type.

   Entry/platform protocol rows use those marked ports to supply a known callable class with `S` on its sole
   argument, crossing result and no retained payload. The authority is the pinned runtime dispatch protocol,
   not the alias name or merely the expanded function type. The class travels as ordinary value provenance
   through wrappers, captures and erased aliases, including a helper annotated `msg → ⊤`; an unmarked function
   of that same type is not a send. If provenance is actually lost, apply the ordinary unknown/pending rule,
   never guess a send class from type shape. `sender` on a name supplies no class by itself at an arbitrary
   expression: only a protocol-produced value or an already tracked class has that capability. Foreign
   protocol producers and their checked interface ports are pinned under R-5.10.7.

   S7 tests both forms on paired v2-only fixtures while the existing full corpus and platform API stay in the
   alias form. S9's v1/v2 diff uses that unchanged corpus. S10 then migrates platform declarations, callers,
   documentation and skills to nominal Send/Send.to and runs the migrated corpus under v2, comparing it to
   the recorded pre-migration semantic results before deleting v1. No v1 golden is reblessed to accommodate
   nominal Send. R-5.9.9 and the rule above describe the final API; this temporary alias provenance is an
   implementation bridge inside v2, removed with the switch-over.
6. **Foreign words and rows as data** (R-5.10): `Rows.fromWords` builds a class from oc §24.2's words, defaults
   pessimistic (R-5.10.3). **The words and selectors below** express every row R-5.10.8 asserts beside its type
   and `Rows.zig` names no declaration: parameter `written` (`W` at `ε` only: a storage write, R-4.10.9);
   parameter `stored` (a value retained at the result's `[*]`, or a callback whose selected result is
   stored as specified below; both take part in §2.9's construction rule); `taken`, on a function parameter (the supply is a materialised element of the first container
   argument: `List.focus`, `Dict.focus`, `Dict.update`) **and on a result** (`foreign pure traverseAt : List a, Int →
   taken a`: the result is a materialised element of parameter 1, in force for the rest of the frame); result
   `lent` (a loan of parameter 1's `◆`: `Ref.get`). A `taken` element is owned iff the container is exclusive, owned, and
   has no holder of the *element* outside the call — a holder of the container holds `others`, not the taken
   element, while the split is in force (§2.2), so `mapHelp`'s pending `a` does not borrow it; and an owned item
   does not make an accumulator outliving the call owned (R-5.3.4).
   **The index obligation and pins [O 2026-10-26].** A body that reads a `taken` result reads that
   container only through the certified traversal, once per index in one direction. Pin the primitive,
   every body reading its result, and every forwarder of that result, across modules and packages. Find
   forwarders as a least fixpoint over result flow through calls, aliases, lets, lambdas/partial applications
   and case arms, including resolved dispatch. A caller of a completed fold does not owe a pin merely
   because the fold reads taken elements. The gate keys pins by package plus declaration, not `Module.name`.
   Pin the implementation that executes: codegen-inlined primitives include the `Operator` dispatch and
   `js/Lower` lowering regions, not only their unused sibling exports. Every row retains its pinning fixture
   and unsafe-direction flip report (R-5.10.7). Helpers on which an asserted body relies are followed across
   module/package boundaries to a separately justified pinned contract; an unworded beni helper is not a
   trust boundary. Foreign siblings and P-sync remain explicit trusted leaves. This closes Task/Deferred's
   helper gap (#1061) in S8 without editing v1. Derived eq/compare compose component classes (§2.13.13).
   Wordless `foreign` is pessimistic (R-5.10.1). Words erase only from runtime representation; checked metadata
   survives interfaces. `misplaced_ownership_word` validates the placement/companions below; the S3a signature
   adapter additionally rejects a resolved type that lacks the required kind, rather than silently treating
   an invalid asserted word as absent (#1056).
   **A word on a bare type variable applies at every depth** [M 2026-10-26, #1105]. A parameter whose
   declared type is a type variable (`borrowed a`, `returned a`, `stored a`, or an alias that expands to one,
   `type alias Id a = a`, expanded before deciding; not `List a`) can hold any
   structure at the call, and the callee — a `foreign`, `Js`, or evidence — may read anything inside it. So
   every word there is its deep form: `borrowed a` is `R` at `ε` and at every path below (a leaf of marks,
   §2.10), and so `A`, `E` and `W` for the words that give them. A caller of such a callee reads the leaf
   as `D` at the argument's path (§2.10, *A deep read across a call*), never as a leaf of its own.
   `Rows.fromWords` reads this from the
   callee's annotation (`Rows.Param.type_variable`), never from the call site's instantiated places, where
   `ε` would end at the instantiated type's root. A word on `List a` keeps its own depth (`List.length`
   reads only `ε`, R-4.3.5). Fixture: `ownership/core/HeldIntoTypeVariable.beni`.
   `Js.maySuspend f` gives `f` `unused`; Log's work is `once`; `Task.keepLogContext` is `returned`. Their
   v2 wording and Dict's rows land at S8 (#1053), with v1's input columns and verdicts unchanged.
   **Type metadata, published as data (S2b).** These are contextual ownership words, permitted only in core/
   platform declarations, parsed/lowered with `misplaced_ownership_word`, erased from runtime types but retained
   in typed interfaces, checked core and ownership blocks. `Rows`/`Place` switch on enum metadata, never a
   module/type/constructor spelling. User code cannot assert them. The exact forms are:

   ```text
   pub equatable sequence foreign type List a
   sequence foreign type Builder a
   pub opaque cell type Ref a = Ref Js.Value
   pub opaque cell type Deferred a = Deferred Js.Value
   pub type Result e a = Ok a | failure Err e
   ```

   `sequence` precedes `foreign type`, after `pub`/`equatable` if present, on a unary type only: storage kind
   list, one `[*]` child of its formal parameter, even when its runtime representation is opaque. `cell`
   precedes `type` after `pub opaque` (or precedes `foreign type`) on a unary type only: a stable handle cell,
   one barrier `◆` child typed by its formal parameter, independent of representation fields. An unworded
   opaque/foreign type does **not** acquire either contract. `failure` precedes one unary constructor of a
   two-constructor type; the other constructor is unary success. The type checker publishes the instantiated
   success/failure payload paths for `try`; ownership reads those resolved paths instead of looking up `Result`
   or `Err`. Incorrect arity, duplicate/conflicting words or placement outside core/platform is an error.
   A renamed test type/constructor with these words must behave identically. Every such type/constructor's
   representation and associated operations enter R-5.10.7's pinning/mutation gate.

   **Value words selecting those slots (S2b).** In addition to `written`, `stored`, `taken`, `lent`, add the
   following contextual parameter/result words. Numeric roles below are fixed by the word and verified against
   the signature; they are not special knowledge of the declaration's name. Unmentioned parameters still
   require explicit existing words (otherwise pessimistic). The spellings below are the source words.

   | Word / placement | Exact row semantics; declarations carrying it |
   |---|---|
   | result `elementof` | Parameter 1 is a sequence with element type equal to the result; result `π₁[*]`, π₁ `R` at ε and `A` at `[*]`. No split, no `taken`, no ownership transfer. `at`/`unsafeGet`: `borrowed List a, borrowed Int → elementof a`. The root `borrowed` does not suppress the word's element `A`. Additional parameters have explicit words. |
   | result `copyof` | Parameter 1 and result are sequences with the same element type. Result storage fresh, `[*] = π₁[*]`; π₁ `R`, `[*]` `A`. List-kind descendant κ is `lost`; record-kind descendant κ is the corresponding `excl π₁` path, not unconditional `yes`; crossing paths are `yes`. Copying storage removes only that root's loan tag. `copy`, `sliceOf`, pinned `sortWith` (its comparator additionally `many`, borrowed supplies). Companion π₁ `borrowed`; reject `fresh`, `exclusive`, `returned` or another result selector beside it. |
   | result `prepended` | Exactly two parameters: `stored a, returned List a → prepended List a`. Result storage is π₂'s storage (re-cons: a view over, or a header sharing, π₂'s base) or fresh (copy), π₂ `RA`, π₁ `RA`; contents are the positional collection of π₁ and π₂[*], not a branch union. At each path κ is `excl π₁ ∧ excl π₂[*] ∧ sep(π₁,π₂[*])`, with the construction's cross-path comparisons. No existing storage write is demanded: prepend allocates or reconstructs a view. Surface prepend's fresh-front refinement is §2.13.2, never a name test for `cons`. |
   | callback parameter `stored` | Store its **result**, not the closure. Without a cell selector, the answer is put back at the element position `[*]` of the written container, whatever its kind: a `sequence`'s `[*]` or a `dict`'s value position `[*]` (keys cross). **Row:** the callback is invoked at most once with the taken element; its stored answer replaces that element at the destination's `[*]`, the result's `[*]` is the join of the stored answer and the remainder, and κ there is derived as §2.9's construction rule derives it with the remainder (the taken position removed first). The answer is either the element type `a`, and then the whole answer is stored, or a resolved Maybe-like two-constructor carrier (one nullary, one unary whose payload is `a`, validated by shape as for `lentoptional`, no name test). For the carrier, the unary payload path (`Just`'s payload) is the selected result path that is stored, and the nullary alternative (`Nothing`) is a removal: it stores nothing, the taken position is gone, and the result's `[*]` is the remainder only; the result row joins the two alternatives. **Placement:** on the callback parameter. **Companions:** the callback is `once taken`; parameter 1 is the sole `written returned` destination, a `sequence` or a `dict` whose element type is `a`; the callback's argument is `a` or the same carrier over `a` (the taken element at its payload path; the nullary argument alternative takes nothing); the answer type must match the argument form. `List.focus` carries `once taken stored` with `a → a`; `Dict.focus` carries it with `Maybe v → Maybe v` over a `dict` destination, worded in S8 (#1021, #1053). With `cellupdate`, store result ε at π₁◆; with `cellmodify`, store only result .1 at π₁◆ and return .0 under the loan/disjointness rule below. These selectors require `stored sync` and imply once/taken/owned; reject duplicate/conflicting invocation or destination words. |
   | result `cellnew` | Result is a fresh `cell` handle, ◆ initially parameter 1; require parameter 1 `consumed`. `Ref.make : consumed a → cellnew Ref a`. Inspect the payload for loans **before** installing the barrier. |
   | result `cellempty` | Fresh `cell` handle with initially empty ◆, no payload; unit argument `unused`. `Deferred.make`. Empty is an initial state, not the result of later reads. *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1736):* the first parameter may be `escaped` instead: code the callee keeps fills the cell later, and what it puts there is reached only through that escape. `Task.spawn` (§2.13.7, *the fiber rows*). |
   | parameter `cellread` + result `lent` | First parameter must be `cell`; record its stable slot in `refs`, no write, return a loan of the current ◆ at the resolved result payload path. `Ref.get`, `Deferred.wait`; the latter may suspend and the loan is born at return. |
   | parameter `cellread` + result `lentoptional` | Same, but result is a resolved Maybe-like two-constructor carrier (one nullary, one unary matching contents); empty alternative or loan at its unary payload path. `Deferred.poll`. No name test; validate the shape and publish the path. |
   | parameter `cellread` + crossing result | Read only, no loan in the result; `Deferred.isDone`. |
   | parameter 1 `cellwrite`, parameter 2 `consumed cellstored` | Update parameter 1's ◆ with parameter 2; shallow write of handle is **not** this operation. `Ref.set`. The payload has a deep Known/no-loan demand before the barrier store, then ownership/holder checks. |
   | parameter 1 `cellwrite`, parameter 2 `cellupdate stored sync` | Second parameter is a→a, invoked once with taken owned contents under κ; while focused it must have no possibly-aliasing `refs`. Its `stored` effect puts the whole callback result back into the same slot, with a deep no-loan/consumed demand on that result. `Ref.update`. `cellupdate` implies once/taken/owned, cannot duplicate those words. |
   | parameter 1 `cellwrite`, parameter 2 `cellmodify stored sync` | Callback a→(b×a) is once/taken/owned; `stored` puts .1 back with the deep no-loan/consumed demand **only on .1**, and .0 is returned. Compare .0's reachable cells with the stored .1 and remaining slot contents: any overlapping or unknown component returns as a **loan of that slot**; only proved disjoint transferred/fresh components return ordinary origins. `Ref.modify`. Thus `(xs,xs)` cannot export unloaned contents. |
   | parameter 1 `cellcomplete`, parameter 2 `consumed cellstored` | Single-assignment cell: join already-completed/no-store and empty/store alternatives; first accepted payload stays the slot's contents. Bool result crosses. `Deferred.complete`; callbacks/resumptions get loans, not ownership of independent copies. |
   | result `builderdone` | Unary sequence storage in parameter 1 is returned as the result sequence with **the same cells, children and κ**; changes only nominal wrapper and logical length. `List.done`; not fresh exclusive. Parameter 1 is `written returned` (setting the logical length is a storage write at `ε`), length parameter crossing/borrowed. |
   | result `concatenated` | Two sequence parameters, result storage may be parameter 1 or fresh; contents are the union of both `[*]` shapes. List-kind descendant κ is lost, record-kind κ preserved only if both inputs are exclusive and mutually apart. `List.append`; no `List.append` name test. Both inputs get their read/use rows, with the existing write demand on the first storage argument at EVERY call, direct or through an alias/wrapper/method (R-2.2/R-2.7); the `written` companion is mandatory. Spread/`++` fusion lowers that same demand once per surface construction. |

   **Write-back is a summary effect, not a Boolean `need`.** Retain a flat effect record
   `(callback label/port, selected result path, destination parameter/path, mode)` with mode `element`
   (a `sequence`'s or a `dict`'s `[*]`) or `cell`; an `element` effect over a Maybe-like answer also records
   that its nullary alternative removes the taken position and stores nothing. `Calls` instantiates the callback once, projects that path with its κ, records retention at
   the destination and applies its store rule. Carry effects through forwarding, joins and blocks even
   when the enclosing result crosses. Ordinary `stored` preserves loan tags; a cell write-back first
   demands no loans and consumable ownership. `cellmodify` never demands ownership of the unrelated .0;
   `.0` aliasing `.1` is returned loan-tagged, not silently transferred. Element focus (sequence or dict) removes the taken
   position before comparing the replacement with the remainder; returning the taken value is permitted,
   returning another held element loses exclusivity. A callback `need` on its entire answer cannot encode
   these effects (#1052). `Rows.Signature` must expose the callback result place as well as its arguments. The no-call alternative
   (an out-of-range focus index) returns the original sequence unchanged; `once` means at most once.

   The new result selectors are mutually exclusive, result-only, and cannot be combined with `taken`,
   `lent`, `unknown`, `escaped` or other storage selectors. A source parameter cannot be `unused`/`escaped`.
   Validate element and callback-result types after solving, including through aliases; reject ambiguous
   destinations and `stored` on a list of callbacks. These selectors are new v2 syntax (#1052), not claims about S2b's parsed word set. Word metadata is versioned separately from v1; adding
   these v2 words moves all of that declaration's ownership words to the v2 column. Runtime code is unchanged.

   `cellstored` is a destination-specific store word: it means parameter 1's ◆, unlike `stored`, which means
   the result container's element position `[*]` (a sequence's or a dict's). `cellstored` creates a deep no-loan payload demand even when the result crosses.
   Ordinary `stored` grafts the payload shape and its path-indexed loan origins/lifetime into the result,
   including its deep has-loan condition; no no-loan demand is made merely for building a local collection.
   Later consumption/escape/suspension of that collection checks the retained tags. `cellnew`, `cellwrite`, `cellupdate`, `cellmodify`, `cellcomplete` and `cellread` use the
   versioned slot relation in §2.13.7. A row missing mandatory companion words/arity/types, or using both
   `fresh exclusive` and `builderdone`, is rejected during word validation. These are specified new syntax,
   not assertions that origin/master already parses it. The slice introducing each word updates parser, formatter, published type/row metadata, cache versions,
   diagnostic catalogue, `language.md` and `skills/beni/` together (S2b baseline, S3a #1052 completion).

   **Builder derivation.** `builder : unused Int → fresh exclusive Builder a` starts with empty `[*]`;
   `put : written returned Builder a, borrowed Int, stored a → Builder a` stores parameter 3 into `[*]`,
   computing κ by §2.9 at every store; `done`'s `builderdone` transfers that κ unchanged. The type's `sequence`
   metadata makes the contents visible without a name test. Hence mapHelp's recursive store/within calculation
   (§2.12) sees actual callback results: `List.map xs (λ_ → shared)` may produce a value but its inner write is
   refused (same shared object across calls); `List.map xs (λ_ → [1])` retains exclusive fresh elements; and
   `λl → List.push l 1` needs the input's κ. No Builder row asserts the final contents always exclusive.

7. *On slots* [#1685]: a `cellwrite` or `cellcomplete` word writes the parameter's `◆` slot. The demand's target is
   the contents position of each cell the argument names, whatever the contents' type, and the relation never
   meets it (a write replaces what the cell holds and changes no object anyone holds), so `Ref.set` is
   accepted beside every holder of the handle (`RefSetThenWrite`). What a callee keeps of the value its own
   write consumes (`Ref.set` storing `v`) is that write's own business: an escape made by the call itself does
   not refuse that call's demands. *Amended 2026-11-02 (#1727):* a cell operation of a closure on a captured `Ref`
   does not make the closure `once` (§2.11.4): rewriting the cell on each call stales no reader. Only an in-place
   write of a list keeps a closure `once`. A list taken out of the cell under `cellupdate`/`cellmodify` and edited
   in place is judged at that row's callback, by its own rules, and not by the closure's `once`.
   **`Ref` loans** (R-5.12.3, #981): `Ref a` is a `ref` place; **`◆` is a barrier**: a holder of a `Ref` is not a
   holder of its contents, `reach` and Esc stop at `◆` (a `Ref` captured by a handler, a spawned fiber or JavaScript
   does not escape its contents, since only the worded operations reach them: rule 6), and the only outside
   holders of the contents are loans. `Ref.make v`: fresh `site` with `◆ ↦ v`, `consumed` on `v`. `Ref.get`
   (`lent`): `loan(c·ι)` per `c ∈ cellsAt(r, ◆)`, a holder that may be read, passed to readers and used to build
   values. Implement `lent` as a lazy overlay tagging every reachable mutable storage path in the cell's
   contents, stopping at nested ◆ barriers; scalars/crossing descendants carry no tag. A backing handle cell (§2.13.18)
   is not crossing and **is tagged** (2026-11-02): before §2.13.18 a native handle crossed and carried no tag, but
   §2.13.18's loan rule for `backingof` and its Known condition both rely on the tag. A projection retains
   the overlay at the selected descendant. Loan origins carry the introducing region id (u32) and stable
   slot identity; summary substitution maps incoming region variables to the caller's original ids, never
   fresh regions. Thus a shallow copied outer list still has loan-tagged inner lists; a loan reaching Esc, a send, a model or a closure/return outliving its loan region is refused
   (`list_still_used`, with the depth-correct copy fix below). A callee returning an incoming loan
   through its `res` preserves the caller's original region; this is not itself escape. Thus `Dict.insert`,
   `List.push`, `filter` and forwarding helpers may return values carrying an incoming loan to its still-live
   caller. A locally introduced loan may not escape its introducing region except through an explicit
   trusted `lent` protocol. All loan-bearing descendant paths participate in later lifetime checks; a loan whose holder is live across an instruction whose effect rung may
   suspend (`Dispatch.effectAt`, `EffectPlan.zig`; `poly` counts as may-suspend) is refused. Call entry includes
   every argument, callback capture and callee environment until that call returns, even if the caller's last
   syntactic use is the call itself. Therefore `show (Ref.get r)` is refused when show may suspend; so are a
   passed closure capturing the loan and a suspending callee environment containing it. Existing pending
   operands are included. A loan returned by a suspending read is born **after** that suspension; it may be
   read synchronously, but cannot survive a later suspension. Indirect/unknown effects remain pessimistic. `Ref.set/update/modify`
   (the `cellwrite`/`cellstored`/`cellupdate`/`cellmodify` rows above): a `writer` demand on the `◆` cell; Dead requires every
   live loan of an aliasing contents cell dead; **re-entry**: the class field `refs` (§2.10) lists the `◆` cells a
   body or its callees operate on, by **stable handle/slot** identity, so a callback (or anything it calls) that operates on a `Ref`
   whose slot may alias the focused slot is refused at compile time (`p/RefOwnsContents`). **P-sync**, a trusted
   obligation of every platform, pinned: the runtime never enters beni code synchronously from inside a host call
   beni made (an event a host API raises synchronously is queued to the next dispatch), so within one fiber no
   beni code runs between two points that do not suspend. `Deferred` follows its explicit rows above. `Js.ref` is **worded**, but is not a `cell`-marked type:
   `ref : escaped a → fresh Ref a`, `read : borrowed Ref a → unknown a`, `write : borrowed Ref a, escaped a → ⊤`
   (`core/Js.beni:193–202`). Thus stored contents escape and reads are unknown, per R-5.12.4; a spawned fiber or queued body holds its captures as an escaped closure (R-5.12.1).
   *Amended 2026-11-02 (#1729), the loan rule at a cell callback, as v2 builds it:* the rule "Dead requires every live
   loan dead" is the rule of an **in-place edit of the contents**. Replacing the contents (`Ref.set`, the cell write of
   `Ref.update`/`Ref.modify`) stales no loan, because the loan still names the old contents, which nothing changes; that
   `writer` demand is behind the barrier. Before this amendment v2 checked no loan at all: the cell demand's targets are
   the `◆` position, which no holder meets, and a `cellupdate`/`cellmodify` callback was unknown code, so every edit it
   made in place was refused `unknown (approx)`, loan or not. Now:
   - **The callback is a label** of the row (§2.11.3), called `once`, whose one supply is `π1◆` slot for slot and kept
     by nothing (`Rows.fromWords`). It no longer escapes. Its in-place edit of what it is supplied is a `callsite`
     demand on what the cell holds, judged as any other. A loan of the contents (a `Ref.get` or `Ref.modify` result,
     or a value or closure built from one) that is live after the operation is a holder of them and refuses it:
     `alias: v holds it`, `captured: g, a closure holding it`. With no loan live, the edit is accepted
     `callback-param`. Loans are still `⊤` in v2 (`lent`), so a live loan of another cell refuses the edit too
     (no longer since #1977: a loan names its cell, below).
   - **The edit is deep at `π1◆`** at the caller (`writes π1◆*`), never a cell operation (§2.11.4,
     `Eval.cellWrite`), so a call of a function that makes it is judged against the caller's loans in the same way
     (`bump r` with `v = Ref.get r` live is refused at the call).
   - **The cell holds its contents behind the barrier.** A hold whose path steps through a `◆` is no holder of what
     the cell holds: the handle's later uses and a record holding the `Ref` do not refuse the edit
     (`Place.behindCell`). Only the worded operations reach the contents, and what they hand out is a holder of its
     own. A cell operation's target is the `◆` position also where the projection names the cell by a slot below it
     (`m.world◆` of a captured record), so an escape of the contents never refuses a cell operation.
   - **What the callback answers is stored back** (`Ref.update`'s answer, `Ref.modify`'s `.1`). At a slot where
     every object is one the callback was supplied or one it allocated, the contents stay the cell's own. At any other
     slot (a capture, a top-level value, the answer of a callback or of unknown code, a code still being solved, a
     callback the frame passes on), what the cell holds there may be held elsewhere: it escapes at the call
     (`Eval.cellAnswer`), so a later in-place edit of it is refused `escaped`. Without this, `Ref.update r λ_ → ys`
     followed by an edit in place would change `ys`, which v2 cannot see, as it keeps no slot state yet.
     *Amended 2026-11-05 (#1955):* the answer's objects at such a slot escape at the call too, not only what the cell
     held there. They are the cell's now, as `Ref.set`'s payload is (`Stored.zig`): `put = [ 7 ]; Ref.update r λ_ →
     put`, then `List.push put 1`, edited in place the list the cell holds (copying `21`, in place `22`; `Ref.modify`'s
     `.1` the same). The rule is applied at every label whose one supply is a cell's `◆` (`Cells.supply`; `Loans.supply` since #1977), worded or
     passed on, since a passed-on label keeps its supply: `upd r f = Ref.update r f` and `upd r f = Ref.update r λxs
     → f xs` store what `f` answers, and their callers see it only through that supply. Only a worded `cellmodify`
     label stores `.1` alone; elsewhere the whole answer is treated as stored, which is coarser and sound. Fixtures:
     `run/SanitiserCellStoredCapture` (refused) and `run/SanitiserCellStoredFresh` (a fresh answer, then an edit
     through the cell; a stored capture only read: accepted).
   Fixtures: `run/SanitiserCellLoan` (each loan refused; the sanitised run of an acceptance shows the stale read) and
   `run/SanitiserCellEdit` (the same edits with no loan live, accepted, the sanitised run prints the same).
   *Amended 2026-11-02 (#1734), loans across a suspension, as v2 builds it:* v2 does not build the rule above that
   refuses a loan whose holder is live across an instruction that may suspend. No program v2 accepts needs it, because
   each fiber's code is checked on its own and every way to start a fiber (`Task.spawn`, `spawnIn`, `start`, `par`,
   `par3`, `parOk`, `race`, `raceAll`, `raceOk`, `timeout`, a platform's handlers and frame callbacks) gives its work
   to JavaScript or to a label called many times. Two rules then keep a loan that one fiber holds across a suspension
   away from an in-place edit that another fiber makes:
   - **An escape reaches through `◆`.** In v2, Esc does not stop at a cell's barrier. What escapes with a closure (its
     captures, or `escapes π1ε*` of a helper that spawns it) includes the contents of each cell it reaches. So the
     frame that starts the fiber, and each caller of a function whose contract escapes the cell, cannot edit those
     contents in place afterwards: refused `escaped` (`run/SanitiserFiberReader`: a helper spawns a fiber that holds
     `Ref.get r` across a sleep, and the caller's `Ref.update r λxs → List.push xs 1` is refused). The barrier above
     ("reach and Esc stop at ◆") holds for holders (`Cells.behindCell`) and for cell operations, not for the reach of
     an escape. A cell operation beside such an escape is accepted (`Ref.set`, or an update whose answer is fresh):
     it changes no list that a loan names (`run/SanitiserFiberReplace`).
   - **An in-place edit of a captured cell's contents makes the closure `once`** (§2.11.4), refused where it escapes
     or where a label may call it many times. So the work of a fiber never edits contents that another fiber can hold
     a loan of (`run/SanitiserFiberBranch`: one branch of `Task.par` holds a loan across a sleep, and the other branch
     edits the contents in its body or through a callee. The edit is refused at `par`).
   Each rule alone refuses its fixture. If the escape stops at the contents that a cell callback is supplied,
   `SanitiserFiberReader` is accepted and its sanitised run reads the edited list. If the edit is exempt from `once`,
   as a cell operation is, `SanitiserFiberBranch` is accepted and reads the edited list, and so do #1734's probes of
   `par`, `parOk`, `race`, `raceOk`, `timeout` and `spawnIn`. So relax neither rule alone. Before an escape stops
   at `◆` (as the barrier text says), or before an in-place edit is exempt from `once`, build the suspension rule in
   this form: a loan live across a suspension point is a holder that each in-place edit of those contents by another
   fiber meets, and the writes of a closure given to a fiber starter are effects at the start, which the starter's
   holders see until the fiber is joined. Until then v2 is coarser than that rule. After a spawn, the frame does not
   edit in place what the spawned work reaches, joined or not. And because `Task.spawn`'s result is `⊤` in core's
   inferred contract, `Task.join` escapes `⊤`, so after a join the frame edits nothing in place at all, not even a
   list made after the join (#1734's probe `C13MakeAfterJoin`).
   *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1759), a work's answer in a `fresh` result:* `timeout : borrowed Duration, once aliased (⊤
   → a) → fresh Maybe a` answers `Just` of what the work answers, and that may be any object the work reaches.
   `fresh` names only what the row makes. Before this, a worded callback was only escaped, so the `Just`'s contents
   were read as fresh, and `List.push` on the work's captured list ran in place while the list was still read
   (`run/SanitiserTimeoutAnswer`; the sanitised run trapped). Now an `aliased` callback of a row is also a label
   (origin offset 2, no supply, `once` else many), and its answer arrives at every result slot beside `fresh`. At a
   caller, a known work's answer is read off its code: its capture is `escaped` with the closure, and a list it makes
   is fresh (`run/SanitiserTimeoutAnswerFresh`, accepted in place). Unknown code's answer is `⊤`. The escape stays:
   it refuses the code's own writes (§2.11.4) and keeps the fiber rule above. An `aliased` list of callbacks
   (`raceOk`) already reached the result through its parameter arrival. A worded row's label names no instruction,
   so §2.11.3's site type is never read from its origin.
   *Amended 2026-11-03 (#1736), the fiber rows:* `Fiber a` is a `cell foreign type`. Its `◆` is the fiber's
   `outcome`. Only `Task.complete` writes it, once: with `Done` of the work's answer itself (`finished`, the bottom
   of every fiber's stack), or with the shared `Cancelled` (`ended`), which `joined` never returns (it cancels the
   joiner). So:
   - `spawn` and `spawnDetached : escaped (⊤ → a) → cellempty Fiber a`, `spawnIn : escaped Scope, escaped (⊤ → a) →
     cellempty Fiber a`. `fork` makes a new record whose `outcome` is null, and only queues it (`enqueue`; a
     scheduler's `run` that calls the drain during the call is a defect, `drainS`), so the cell is empty at return.
     The fiber's stack keeps the work, and a scope given one keeps the fiber, so both escape. The escape through
     `◆` above still covers what the work's answer reaches.
   - `join : cellread Fiber a → lent a`, the row of `Deferred.wait`. Every join of one fiber answers the same
     object, so a join is a loan of the contents and not an answer of its own. With the work's answer as the
     join's own (`fresh`), two joins would look apart, and an edit in place of one would change the other:
     `run/SanitiserFiberJoins` is refused with `lent`, and its sanitised run traps with `fresh`.
   - `wait`, `poll` and `joinAll` keep their inferred rows, whose answers are `⊤`.

   With these rows, a frame that spawns and joins can edit in place what the work does not reach (#1734's
   probes `C8SpawnOtherRef`, `C9SpawnNothing`, `C12JoinOnly`, `C13MakeAfterJoin`). It is still coarse in one place:
   a loan of a list is `⊤` in v2, so while the answer of a `join` of a `Fiber (List a)` is live (as for
   `Deferred.wait`), each in-place edit of a list is refused, even of a list made after the join. *Amended
   2026-11-03 (#1739):* no longer: §2.9.2 step 4's *made after* (#1714) reads an atom made after the loan's
   call as none of its objects, so a literal or a copy made after it is edited in place
   (`run/SanitiserLoanFreshEdit`), and two joins of one fiber still refuse (`run/SanitiserFiberJoins`). The four bodies
   and every helper of `Task` they run are pinned in `word-bodies.txt`. `check_test`'s reach rule follows them
   from these four v2 rows. `Task`'s v1 rows keep v1's rule (their own body), as they did before `Task` had a
   v2 row.
   *Amended 2026-11-05 (#1977), loans per cell and the owning extraction, as v2 builds them (S8-ref's first
   step):* a loan names its cell, and `Ref.modify`'s `.0` is owned when the stored `.1` keeps none of it.
   - **A loan is a loan of one cell's contents.** A `lent` result (`Ref.get`, `Deferred.wait`, `Task.join`) is a
     `lent π1◆` arrival (`Rows.fromWords`): at a caller, one **loan** leaf (`Value.LeafKind.loan`) per object
     the frame names at the cell's `◆`, deep, each naming the leaf it lends. Held, a loan holds what it lends
     and nothing else (`Distinct.overlap`), so a live loan of one cell refuses an in-place edit of that cell's
     contents and no other (`SlotStateBranches`' disjoint-handles green). Written, consumed, stored by
     `Ref.set`/`Ref.make`, or handed to unknown code, a loan is unknown, as `⊤` was: refused `unknown`. An
     escaped loan escapes what it lends. Where the frame names nothing at the `◆` (a `Deferred` or a `Fiber`
     made empty, `cellempty`) the loan is `⊤`. The read-off publishes a loan as `⊤`, so a callee's loan
     reaches its caller as unknown, as before.
   - **What the frame's contents name, with no slot state.** v2 still keeps no versioned `contents` relation
     (*Slot state and loans* below): a cell's `◆` names what `Ref.make` stored, or a parameter's `◆`, for the
     whole frame. Every way to reach the contents (`Ref.get`, a callback's supply, `modify`'s `.0`) reads that
     one name. An object a cell holds later is a `Ref.set` payload (consumed and escaped, `cellstored`), a
     callback's allocation, or an answer at a slot that is not the callback's own (escaped at the call with what
     the cell held there, #1955, `Stored`). So two names of one object meet at the name, or the object has
     escaped, **with two exceptions the rules below close for a take**. A store may put an object at a slot the
     first contents never named (`Ref.make Nothing`, then `Just ys`): the escape projects nothing there. So a
     slot behind a `◆` where the frame names nothing is unknown (`Holders`), never empty. And a stored value may
     hold one object at two slots (`Ref.set r ( n, n )`), which the two names hide: #1984, closed by *the contents
     relation* below. A loan taken before a replacement still names the old object: it
     refuses edits it need not.
   - **`Ref.modify`'s `.0`.** The row's result is the callback's answer at `.0` (a `cb` arrival). At a
     caller that knows the code (`Loans.answer`), `.0` is the answer as read, **owned**, when the stored `.1`
     can share nothing `.0` holds (`Loans.lends`, over the code's contract): `.1` holds no object of unknown
     code (`⊤`, an unknown callback's answer, a loan), and `.0` and `.1` do not both hold the contents supplied
     (or what a capture reaches through a `◆`: a callback may re-enter its own cell, `( steal r, old )`),
     nor both objects the callback allocated (a contract does not tell two allocations apart). A label's answer at
     `.0` may be anything `.1` holds, so with anything at `.1` it is a loan. An answer that is no tuple of the
     callback's (a top-level pair) gives a loan. *(Until the contents relation below, 2026-11-05: withdrawn, and any contents may be taken; contents that hold one object twice have escaped, and an edit of the take is refused `escaped`.)* **The contents must be at most one object** at the cell's type (a
     type variable's slot may be any number), since with no slot state a value of several objects may hold one
     twice (#1984): `Ref (Maybe (List Int))` and `Ref (List Int)` are taken, `Ref (List (List Int))` and a pair
     are lent. A slot that holds no object is skipped. A capture or a top-level value at `.1` is the cell's after the call and
     escapes there (#1955), so whatever else names it, `.0` included, is refused an in-place edit. Otherwise
     every object of `.0` is a loan, and so is all the cell holds. Unknown code, a code of the group being
     solved, and a label passed on (whose whole answer is stored, #1955) give a loan. So `( old, Nothing )`
     and `( old, [] )` answer the old contents owned and leave the slot holding the second part;
     `( old, old )`, `( n, n )` and `( old, List.map old f )` answer a loan; `( [ 9 ], xs )` answers a
     fresh list.
   - **Why an owned `.0` is sound.** After the call the cell holds `.1` and only `.1`. Each object of `.0` is
     the old contents, an allocation of the callback, or a capture. The old contents are named as the cell's
     (above): a live loan of the cell meets them and refuses the edit (`v = Ref.get slot` before the take and
     read after the edit); another cell cannot hold them (a cell's payload is consumed or escapes); the
     handle is no holder (the barrier: only the worded operations reach the contents, and each reads them
     again and is judged where it is made). One object cannot alias itself, so the frame's one name is enough.
     An allocation answered at `.0` and not at `.1` has no other holder. A capture is the frame's own binding,
     judged as any holder is, and escapes if `.1` stores it too.
   - **An edit in place of the taken contents through a helper is deep at `π1◆`.** `grow r = List.push (take
     r) 9` publishes `writes π1◆*` (`ReadOff.paramEffects`: a write at a `◆` that is not a cell operation's,
     at its own position), as a callback's edit does (#1729). A shallow `π1◆` would read as a cell operation
     at the caller, and a live loan there would not be asked.
   - **A function whose answer escapes, escapes.** `put b f = Ref.update b λ_ → f ⊤` stores what `f` answers, and
     the callee's contract had no word for it, so a loan a caller's closure answered reached the other cell
     unseen. An escaped label answer now publishes `escapes` of the function (`ReadOff.paramEffects`): the
     closure's captures escape, through `◆`. A top-level value in a result is one atom at every slot (`res ε…
     shared`, `Put.arriveWide`): a pair of lists answered by a function read as fresh below its root.
   - **A cell callback's label is found by its supply below the `◆`** (`Loans.supply`). Contents that are no
     object (`Ref (Maybe (List Int))`) are supplied at their objects' slots (`◆#Just.0`), and before this
     amendment such a label was not recognised: neither #1955's stored-answer escape nor this item applied to it.
   Blocks carry the new arrival, since a worded row such as `Task.join` is published (block version 20).
   Fixtures: `run/RefTakeOwned` (inline, through a helper, and stored into another cell: accepted, the
   sanitised run prints the same); `run/RefTakeKeepsLoan` (`( old, old )` the same three ways, `( n, n )`, a
   named callback, half of a pair, re-entry: refused; with `.0` read as owned, every edit is accepted and the
   sanitised run traps); `run/RefTakeWhileHeld` (an owned take beside a live holder: each loan route, a stored
   capture, a passed-on callback, a fiber); `run/RefTakeUnseenHolder` (a holder the frame has no name for, from
   #1980's review); `run/SanitiserLoanPerCell` (SlotStateBranches' green,
   LoanModifyReturn's green, #1404's `direct` and `boxBuilt` twins with v1's verdicts).
   *Amended 2026-11-05 (#1991, #1984, #1986), the contents relation, as v2 builds it:* a frame keeps **one name per
   slot of a cell's `◆`**, for the whole frame. That is the relation `contents(handle-origin, ◆)` with one version:
   a store is a weak update of those names, so a name stands for every object the slot has held. It stays sound
   because of what a store leaves behind. **Every object a cell holds is, at each store, one of: named by the frame at
   its own slot; held by no one else (a consumed payload, a callback's allocation); at a slot the frame names nothing,
   which is unknown (`Holders`); or escaped.** Three of those four were built by #1729, #1955 and #1977. The one they
   left are that **two slots of a cell are two objects** and that **a slot's object is the one its name says**. The
   first bullet below keeps the first, *A move* the second.
   - **The rule.** A store that may put one object at two slots makes what the cell holds escape at the store, deep
     (`Contents.zig`). So a later edit in place of any of it is refused `escaped`, at the caller too: the frame's
     escape of `π1◆` is published as any other. `Ref.set r ( n, n )`, `Ref.update r λp → ( p.0, p.0 )`, `Ref.modify`'s
     `.1`, `{ p = s.p, q = s.p }` (#1986), `[ n, n ]`, `l ++ l`: reading such a cell is accepted; editing its contents is
     refused.
   - **What is asked.** A contract's store (`Ref.set`'s payload, `Deferred.complete`'s, a helper's) asks the separation
     of what is stored at the call. A cell callback's answer asks its code's `res_cond`, which must not be `no`. Its
     selections need no asking: a selection of what it was supplied holds by this rule, inductively, and a selection
     of a capture is at a slot `Stored` has escaped. `Ref.modify`'s `res_cond` covers `.0` too, so `( p, p )` over a cell
     of several objects escapes it, which is coarser than the rule needs and sound. A cell that holds at most one
     object at its type (`Cells.oneObject`) asks nothing.
   - **A store that hangs on a parameter is its caller's to judge.** `put r x = Ref.set r x` cannot know what `x` will
     be. When the store's condition asks only the frame's own parameters and the cell is one of them, the contract
     publishes `stores π1◆ ⇐ sel π2{ε*}`, one column of a contract (`Contract.Store`): at each call the cell's contents
     escape unless the condition holds there. So `put r [ 7 ]` over a `Ref (List Int)` and `put r ( [ 3 ], [ 4 ] )` stay
     editable. Elsewhere (a cell the frame made, a captured cell, whose store a call cannot see) an unsettled condition
     escapes at once. The worded rows state the column themselves: `cellstored` beside a cell write is
     `stores π1◆ ⇐ sel π2{ε*}`. Blocks carry the column (block version 22).
   - **What it replaces.** The rest of *Slot state and loans* below describes a relation with versions and strong
     updates. A strong update would only let a loan of old contents stop refusing an edit of new ones: precision, no
     soundness. The transforms' **order** is what the frame's points already give: an escape refuses the edits after
     it, and a helper's published escape refuses what follows its call, so `step r = edit r; Ref.set r ( n, n )` called
     twice refuses the second call. **Slot reads and writes** are the contract's `reads`, `writes π1◆`, `escapes` and
     `stores`. A re-entry test keys on the handle, never the payload, because a loan names the cell (#1977).
   - **Consumed.** A store's own `consumed` demand stays, and it is what keeps one object out of two cells: `Ref.set a
     n; Ref.set b n` is refused `later-use` at the first.
   - **A move is an edit of what it moves.** A callback may store what it was supplied at another slot: `( y, x )`,
     `( y, [] )`, `{ p = w.q, q = w.p }`. No object is held twice, so the rule above says nothing, but a loan taken before
     the move still names the old slot, while an edit or a take names the new one: with the frame's names, they
     look apart (from #2009's review: traps, and with the take over several objects, a regression). The names stay
     right for everything read **after** the move, because they all moved together. So only a holder from before
     matters: each supplied slot the answer stores elsewhere gets a deep write at the call (`Contents.moved`), judged as
     an in-place edit of it, published to callers as one. A loan of it live after the call refuses the move
     (`run/CellMovesSlots`); with none live the move is accepted and the slots stay editable. **A slot already escaped
     refuses the move** too, even if the cell is only read afterwards: an escape marks a name and does not follow its
     object, so a capture moved to an unescaped name would be edited. Only one escape is no refusal: the call's own
     that covers the whole cell, as a helper's passed-on callback publishes (`upd c f = Ref.update c f`). Every name
     stays escaped after it, so nothing is lost. An escape of one slot is not excused (`helperEscapesOneSlot`).
     Three refusals here are coarser than soundness needs, and a program can reach them: a loan held across a swap and
     only read; a move of escaped contents that are only read after; and a closure that swaps a captured cell's
     slots is `once`, because the move is an in-place edit.
   - **`.0` and `.1` read at the call.** `Loans.lends` asks whether a slot of the answer may hold an object. The code's
     own place may be generic, so `.0` is read at the call's result and `.1` at the cell's `◆` (`Loans.answer`). And a
     type variable that only scalars can instantiate holds no object: `[ 0 ]` is a `List number`, whose `[*]` is a
     crossing place (`Groups.Adapter.close`, `Kind.scalar`), so `( List.push (List.copy xs) 5, xs )` answers a list
     owned, Appendix B's `ModifyResultPaths` (`run/RefModifyIndependent`). The same fact took eight `disjoint` refusals
     of fold accumulators over numeric literals off the corpus; each had a real `escaped` refusal or none needed.
   - **A take of several objects.** With two slots of a cell two objects or escaped, `.0` no longer needs contents of
     one object: `( o, ( [], [] ) )` over a pair takes it (`run/RefTakeOwned`'s `pairTake`). After a store of one object
     twice the same take is refused `escaped`.
   - **P-sync, pinned per platform.** `tests/corpus/ownership/p-sync.txt` lists the bodies each platform's host enters
     beni through, and each is pinned in `word-bodies.txt` (R-5.10.7). A gate test fails on a platform not listed
     and on a listener (`addEventListener`, an emitter's `on` or `once`) added in a declaration not listed.
     | Platform | Bodies | Why no program code runs inside a host call |
     |---|---|---|
     | `node` | `Http.Server.startListen`, `receive`, `takeUpgrade`, `WebSocket.fromUpgrade`, `Io.run`, `ChildProcess.listen`, `collectFrom` | an emitter's listener resumes a fiber (`Task.resume`), which queues it; `Io.run`'s `beforeExit` only reports; a child's `data` listener keeps a chunk, or closes the pipes and signals the child, and Node emits nothing back inside those calls (`boundary.md` §9.14) |
     | `browser` | `Rt.turn`, `delegate`, `delegated`, `listen`, `watchEdits`, `crashScreen`, `Listen.on`, `on2`, `WebSocket.attach` | a message a handler sends is queued for the turn's flush; a `Listen` value is queued for a fiber. **One exception, #2006:** a DOM handler's own extractor runs at the dispatch, so under a `focus()` it runs inside that host call |
     | `browser-inline` | `Inline.on`, `onArm`, `listen`, `crashScreen`, `Listen.on`, `Browser.Navigation.listen`, `listenOne` | the same, and the same exception |
     | `browser-tea`, `html` | none | no host code of their own |
     | `cloudflare` | `Worker.listenForAbort` | the listener stops the scheduler; a request's handlers are the host's calls with nothing beneath them, and resume fibers |
     Core's own half, `Task.schedule`, `drain` and `fromHost`, was pinned with `Task`.
   Fixtures: `run/CellStoresTwice` (each store, each edit refused; each traps with the rule removed),
   `run/CellStoresApart` (the greens, and a store of one object twice that is only read).
   **Slot state and loans.** A versioned frame relation `contents(handle-origin, ◆)` supplies current stored
   origins/κ. `cellnew`/`cellempty` initialise it; set/update/modify write-back changes it after the callback,
   and complete joins the already-complete/no-op and empty/store alternatives. Strong update is allowed only
   for one definitely identified slot; possible aliases get a weak union. Branches/recursive feedback join and
   settle this relation like other shape facts. Summaries publish these slot reads/writes and ordered
   transformations, so a later get cannot read only the original make payload. A handle alias names the same
   slot; replacing contents never makes an operation on that handle distinct for re-entry. Unknown callable
   `refs=top` touches every slot: refuse it inside a focus, and refuse any live loan across a call that may
   replace its slot even when the call is synchronous. Cross-module facts preserve these effects.
   Read the **value being stored** for loans before installing ◆; ordinary reach of an already-owned handle
   still stops at its own barrier. This rejects `Ref.set r2 (Ref.get r1)` and `Ref.make (Ref.get r1)` even if
   neither loan local is read later. `Ref.modify r (λxs → (xs,xs))` returns a loan, not an ownership escape;
   a subsequent update while it is live is refused. A proved-disjoint fresh result can still leave modify.
   **Copy depth and diagnostics.** `List.copy` copies only list storage; `Record.copy` only the record and
   `Dict.copy` only dictionary storage. Remove the loan at that copied root, preserve tags on every shared
   descendant. A copy/filter/map with fresh outer storage is therefore sufficient for `List Int` (and for
   opaque crossing handles), not for borrowed inner lists. For `r : Ref (List (List Int))`, a fully independent
   snapshot is `List.map (Ref.get r) List.copy` when the inner elements cross; `List.copy (Ref.get r)` alone
   retains `[*]` loans. Further nesting requires copying/rebuilding each loan-bearing path that will escape
   or survive suspension. Diagnostics list those paths and suggest a type-correct reconstruction whose
   inferred result has no such tags; if no finite fix is known, give a manual “copy these borrowed paths”
   explanation without a bogus automatic JSON edit. Never claim a shallow outer copy discharges deep tags.

   **Backings.** Native backing identities reuse this item's stable slot identities, without contents (§2.13.18,
   2026-11-02). The owning extraction `Ref.modify slot λold → ( old, Nothing )` is what lets a payload taken from a
   cell be transferred there. The `Ref` part of this item is built in S8-ref, ahead of S5 (§8).

   **S8 boundary.** A callback's selected write-back and its returned projection are evaluated under
   one snapshot before slot mutation. Slot effects form an ordered graph of alternatives: sequential
   writes compose; branch joins union alternatives; they are not an unordered set of writes. `refs` is a
   may-touch set keyed by handle/slot, not current payload identity. Cell/loan overlays, original region
   variables, store destinations and that order survive forwarding and disk blocks. Re-entry and may-suspend
   tests consume effect/class facts from the same settled generation; no syntactic-last-use shortcut.
   `Deferred.complete`'s no-op branch does not transfer ownership anew or erase live loans.

8. **Markup** (R-1.6, R-5.8.9, R-5.8.12): a `markup` instruction is a call of a row synthesised from the lowering's
   slot kinds: render slots `R`; event slots `A` into the result's `⟨event⟩` slot as borrowed payloads (`payload
   (a)` on an `update` write reaching them); a `For` row callback's parameter supplied borrowed (`read-only`,
   R-5.8.6, `p/RecordForItem`); a handler capturing a scalar key holds nothing. The construction's result is
   `fresh` (`assumed`, R-6.3).
9. *On slots* [#1685]: a `returned` word whose parameter slot is opaque or a type variable's arrives deep at
   the result slot it lands on, which is open: a caller's slot below it takes its own steps on inside the
   parameter. A
   projection that an opaque or a type variable's place cannot follow, of a call's result, is read through
   the call's arrivals there: the rest taken from each argument both inside the arrival's slot and from the
   argument's root (a whole value cast is read back by its own structure), and, when neither names
   anything, all of the arrival (some object inside it). Elsewhere such a projection is every object below
   the position, approximate. Types never tell two objects apart, since a cast may read one object as
   another type (`CastCallHolds`' `deeper`).
   **Casts** (R-4.11): a `returned Value → a` call whose argument place differs structurally from its result's
   makes `recast(place(a), inner)`; a later read **of the recast node itself** (no step taken since) at a place
   structurally identical to `inner`'s restores `inner` exactly; a projection of a recast is a recast,
   approximate, never restored, so a child of a recast recursive value is not taken for its root
   (R-4.11.2). Its inner is the inner's own part at that step when the inner is built (a node or a delta,
   explicit structure) and its place has the step to the same place (the same field, index or element of
   the same object: `r.a` of `Js.to (Js.from { a = xs })` is `xs`), and the whole
   inner otherwise [#1132's review; `CastProjections` (core)]. The whole inner there took the part for the
   literal around it (`fresh`) and accepted an edit of `xs`. Retain the inner value interpretation, including its snapshot and loan overlay, not only its
   shape: an unstepped restoration restores those facts together (a recast and its inner are one position,
   §2.9, so what the snapshot stores at the inner and below it is read at the recast), while a stepped recast cannot recover
   a stronger certificate by finding a structurally equal type later; `(xs, xs)` read as a list of lists stays `shared`; casts compose to one `recast`.
   **A recast that keeps its whole inner is a node of its own** [#1310, #1311]. It stands for some value
   inside the inner, so its cells are the inner's reach, each one approximate. It is marked whole and
   interned apart from the plain recast of the same inner at the same place, whose cells are the inner's
   own. Every rebuild keeps the mark: a cast of it (a cast of a value inside the inner is still one), a
   call's image (there a parameter cell stands for what the actual reaches, not for the actual's own
   cells), a relabelling, a view's step and the block. A step into it is whole again, even where its
   place has the step to the inner's child: it is never the inner's own part. Its κ is what the leaf rule gives approximate
   cells: `lost`. The one rule therefore gives `lost` for `[*]` of `Js.to (Js.from xs)` when `xs` is a
   parameter, whether the cast is written inline or reached through a call of a declaration that casts.
   `excl π1` is a certificate that the cast lost, and v2 read it only where the two recasts were one
   node. There, the declaration that made the node first decided its cells, so the κ depended on
   declaration order. Without the mark, the result of `List.push (generic xss) [ 1 ]` took the actual's
   own cells (`[ l, l ]`, fresh) for its elements, and an edit of `l` through it was accepted. The
   fixtures are `CastCallHolds` (core), which holds v1's verdicts, and `CastOrder` (core), which is
   checked in both declaration orders.
   **A hold below a cast stays at the cast's path** [#1136]. The inner's structure can name a step the cast's
   place lacks (`Js.from [ xs ]`: `[*]` under `Js.Value`). The object there is still held by the cast value,
   somewhere the cast hides, so a holder walk (`Demands.holdPaths`) that cannot extend its path by the inner's
   step keeps the hold at the path it is at, approximate: every later use of the cast value, which reads all
   of it, finds it. Dropping the hold accepted an edit that JavaScript then saw. `CastHolds` (core) checks it
   with v1's verdicts.
10. **Schemas** (R-4.7.10, R-5.11): a run is a call of a row derived from the resolved schema plan
    (`check/SchemaPlan.zig`): `res` fresh at every place the direction builds, holding conversions' captured or
    top-level cells where a conversion runs (a conversion placing one list twice makes the answer `⊤`, R-5.11.2),
    `⊤` for an interpreting builder or an unplaceable schema, a runner handed on as a value with an unknown input
    part; a `default` fresh per decode (R-5.11.6); issues fresh (R-5.11.5, `p/SchemaIssuesFresh`); `Type` and
    `Encoded` are different places (R-4.7.10); schema constructors are §2.13.1's folded by their family's places
    (R-5.11.4); `Json.decode*` and a run of a schema built at run time answer no record twice: κ `yes` for records
    (R-5.11.3, `p/RecordSchemaRun`). The engine's obligation is trusted (R-5.10.7).
11. **Top-level values and initialization transfer** (R-4.9): a reference to a parameterless value yields its `res`
    with `shared` cells (`top-level (p)` on any write reaching them). Transfer: when the pre-pass counts exactly one
    read of a private parameterless value — direct, outside lambdas, deferred bodies counted — by a parameterless,
    non-recursive initializer of the same application module, with no explicit or inferred `where` evidence, no
    return-type dispatch, a non-function result and a successfully inferred class, the reader sees the value's `site`
    cells as its own; a `pub`, `foreign` or schema source, a second read, a read in a lambda, a recursive
    initializer or an unknown result transfers nothing (R-4.9.3); the destination is still top-level for a
    function; a fold's result keeps its provenance (R-4.9.4).
12. **`Maybe.withDefault (Maybe.map m f) d`** and the `Result` twin (R-4.2.3): the pre-pass recognises the two-call
    shape over variable paths `m`, `d`, `f` a lambda, partial application or top-level value, both calls resolved to
    the same core module; `Regions` makes it a two-arm region and `Transfer` reads it as `case m of Just x → f x;
    Nothing → d`. `d`'s read is in the other arm; `m` written inside `f` is a write of a capture under the arm; `d`
    aliasing `m`'s payload is the other arm's read of a cell the first arm wrote, compatible-exclusive, so accepted
    as a `case` is. Non-matching shapes are ordinary calls (`later-use`); a record default `held-operand`.
13. **Comparison** (R-5.13.1): a declaration `Dispatch` marks as a type's `eq`/`compare` whose class has `writes` is
    `comparison_changes_value` at its first demand on an arrival (or the call of the writing callee). Type dispatch
    is unknown (R-5.13.2). A derived eq/compare class joins the actual component eq/compare classes,
    including uses, result aliases, escapes, callback effects and `writes`. It is not an unconditional
    read-only row. Apply the existing `writes` prohibition after that join; do not introduce a separate
    ban on an `A`/`E` label instead of computing the class.
    **As built (S3b slice 5e, #1434):** a type's comparison is the module's value named `eq` or `compare`,
    `pub` or not (a private one answers `==` and `<` inside its module), whose scheme is the well-known one:
    two parameters, each a type variable or an application of a type `T` the module declares, and a type variable
    or the `Bool` (`Order`) result, the test the checker makes
    of a method (`Instances.writtenFor`, `fitsWellKnown`); a value of that name of another shape is an ordinary
    function. A comparison written as an alias (`compare = byLength`) is the function it names: that
    function's walk is the comparison's (`Groups.comparisonWalks`), so its writes are refused at the write.
    One that names another module's function is walked itself and left unbuilt at the name, since that
    module walked the function as no comparison: never taken for a read-only one. In a comparison's walk,
    every demand the six conditions of §2.8 accept as `param` (a write of what arrived, its own or through a
    callee, a user-written component comparison's call included) is refused with the cause `comparison`
    (R-6.3), a position rule, `comparison_changes_value`; a demand they refuse keeps its own cause, and a write
    of a fresh value stays accepted. So the class still carries the `W` and `writes`, and a caller's derived
    `==` over the type still composes it; its own demands are judged as any call's, the error being the
    comparison's own. A derived comparison has no body and no demand: its writes are its components', refused
    in their walks.
    **A comparison written in beni outside core is never derived** [2026-10-30, #1320]: when its walk is not built, or a
    limit stopped it, a call of it is unbuilt and the caller unchecked; it is not given the derived, read-only class.
    A derived or core container comparison (`List.compare`, a derived row over a field) is built from the classes of the
    user-written comparisons its argument's type reaches; one with no class leaves the call unbuilt, and one that writes
    makes the comparison write. Core is the core package (`--core-root` included), not every embedded module.
    The class is composed **at the places the components occur** [2026-10-30, #1331, #1349]: the walk of the argument's
    type stops at a type that has a user-written comparison of its own (its class is the whole of what that type does,
    so its fields are not entered: a read-only `Outer.eq` never calls the `Inner.eq` of its fields). At a component's
    place the argument is used as the component's class uses its parameters (`π1#Inner.0 W`, at any depth, the two
    parameters' uses merged path by path: a `Shape.join` of them is a `union` the read-off does not enter); everything else is only
    read, deeply. The use is built **once per place** (Tarjan's walk, a cycle settled when it closes and its places one
    deep leaf with the `E` and `W` of everything below), in growth, so its cost is the type's distinct places and not
    its paths (`EvidenceDagBuildDepth32`, mutually recursive types). A deep demand writes everything its base reaches
    (§2.8), so the summary's `W` reaches a parameter held by a fresh value under a deep leaf too: `( Inner xs, ys ) == …`,
    `[ Inner xs ] == []` and a recursive type built around `xs` at any depth write `xs`. There is no bound on the width
    of the use: each writing path is a demand of its own in a caller, and the cost of n of them is the caller's (#1334).
14. **`?`** (R-5.1.6): §2.6; an error type holding no cell adds nothing.
15. **Index exchange** (R-4.8.17, #869, `p/RecordIndexExchange`): a callback of `List.indexedMap` (its index
    supplied as a scalar) keeps the source's κ when it is an **exact permutation**, which is a *flat decision chain* on the index
    and nothing else: the body is `if i == e₁ then t₁ else if i == e₂ then t₂ … else r` — each test a `case` on
    `i == eₖ` (a `method_call` of `eq` that `Dispatch` resolves to `Int`'s, `bir/Lower.zig:2540–2547, 2621–2630, 2873–2891`) whose `True` arm is a take `tₖ` and whose `False` arm is the next test or the element parameter
    `r`, no other instruction between the tests, no take nested under another guard's arm (§2.5's region tree has
    the chain as a right spine of guards); each `eₖ` a local not rebound in the callback or an integer literal;
    each take `tₖ` bound outside the callback by a pattern on `List.get xs e'ₖ` (`Just rowₖ`), a list pattern, or `List.drop xs e'ₖ ▷ List.head`
    (a view of the same source then its head) from the *same* exclusive source — **the very local the `indexedMap`
    maps**, not a view, `drop` or copy of it, else a take from `xs` lands at another offset in `List.drop xs 1` —
    used in exactly one arm; and the
    guard indices `{eₖ}` and the take indices `{e'ₖ}` are the same set (locals by identity, literals by value).
    **And the chain must stay a permutation under every equality partition of its indices**, which holds in
    exactly two shapes: (a) every index is an integer literal and the literals are pairwise distinct — no two
    positions can coincide, so the chain places the row of `e'_{σ(k)}` at `eₖ` for a bijection σ and every other
    position keeps its row; (b) exactly two guards on locals, `if i == a then rowB else if i == b then rowA else r`
    with `rowA = get a`, `rowB = get b` (the one swap): with `a ≠ b` it exchanges the two rows; with `a = b` the first
    arm fires at the one position and places `rowB = xs[a]`, its own row, so the result is `xs`. A chain of three or
    more guards on locals is refused even when flat and with guard set = take set: with `a = 0, b = 1, c = 1`,
    `if i == a then rowB else if i == b then rowC else if i == c then rowA else r` puts `xs[1]` at positions 0 and 1
    — the arm for `c` is dead and `rowA` is never placed — and so does a product of two swaps whose locals coincide
    across the swaps (`a = c`: position `a` gets `rowB`, position `d` gets `rowC = xs[a]`, and `rowD` is lost);
    only the trivial partition keeps a k-cycle a bijection, and locals cannot prove it. The 3-cycle is a red twin of
    `p/RecordIndexExchange` beside `dup2`. A take whose index is not a guard (`dup`'s `i == a → rowB`) puts one row at two
    positions and is refused `exclusive`, as is one cell in two arms, an unguarded arm, three or more guards on
    locals, any chain mixing literals and locals, a literal repeated, or a take nested under
    another guard (`dup2`'s `if i == a then (if i == b then rowA else (if i == a then rowB else r)) else r`, whose
    guard and take sets agree yet position `b` keeps `rowB` beside position `a`'s `rowB`: a red twin of
    `p/RecordIndexExchange`). `swapAt` and `List.drop`
    over an exclusive source keep κ as a storage permutation and a view (R-4.10.11, §2.13.3).
16. **Core's library**: every function of `core/` not asserted (R-5.10.8) is inferred from its body (R-1.10).
    `List.base`, `offset`, `unsafeGet` and `sliceOf` read the runtime representation, so they are **`List` array
    primitives** under R-5.10.8. They are asserted with the result selectors below and pinned under R-5.10.7 (decided
    2026-10-25, Appendix C.9):
    - `base : returned List a → List a`: π₁ `RA`, res π₁.
    - `offset : borrowed List a → Int`: π₁ `R`, crossing.
    - `unsafeGet` and `at` use result `elementof`: π₁ `R`, `[*]` `A`, res π₁`[*]`.
    - `sliceOf` and `copy` use result `copyof`: fresh storage, `[*]` π₁`[*]`, list κ `lost`, record κ `excl π₁`.

    **`sortWith` is asserted with `copyof` and a pinned body [O 2026-10-26]** (R-5.10.8, C.9): fresh storage,
    `[*]` aliases π₁[*], list κ `lost`, record κ `excl π₁`, comparator many with borrowed supplies.
    **Fold accumulator element κ remains `lost` [O 2026-10-26]** unless S4 independently proves C.9
    gap 3's narrowed rule; a storage-write proof alone cannot strengthen that condition.

    The builders return fresh storage because they start in the `sequence` Builder
    with empty contents, whose `put` is `written`/`stored` and whose `done` preserves provenance/κ; the result word
    `concatenated`: `returned` π₁ with κ `lost` at `[*]` for lists and κ kept for records when each input is exclusive and
    they are separate (one condition, kind-filtered, R-4.10.7, R-4.10.8, `p/SchemaIssuesExclusive`). A worked
    derivation of `mapHelp` and `foldlFrom` (§2.2's materialisations in force, the `taken` result, the callee
    `put`'s `stored` word) is specified before walker code in Appendix C and verified by S2b/S4's acceptance tests.

17. **Worker callback protocols** (#1297, #1296, #1290). *Specified 2026-11-02; not built; slice S7-workers (§8).*
    The workers lane's contract is `workers-callback-contracts.md`, `workers.md` §2, §5 and §8, and
    `workers-api.md` §1–§2, on the `workers` branch of PR #1616 until they land. The owner's decision #1319
    adds no language: no `entry`, `sync` or ownership word on a record field. This item uses only what a summary
    promises (§2.10: `use`, `res`, `κ`, `fun(j)`'s needs, `classes`, `effects`, `refs`), together with the `slot`
    annotation and the `T` mark that §2.13.18 adds to that interface. It does not use how S3b or S4 represent a
    summary inside, so a change to the representation of recursive summaries leaves it standing.

    **Where the protocol comes from.** Not from the `entry` word: R-5.8.1 stays as it is, and this item does not
    widen it. A platform's `entryKinds` row names a constructor symbol, the zero-based index k of its entry
    parameter, a `callbackProtocol` (`handlers` or `machine`), a row version, and the role substitution that the
    loader resolved after alias expansion. The loader already refuses a missing, extra or ill-typed field with
    `invalid_entry_kind`. v2 reads the resolved row as an input column keyed by the resolved constructor symbol,
    as it reads `sender` roles (§2.13.5). Constructor and module names choose nothing. `Obligation.entry` gains a
    `source` (the `entry` word or a kind row) and the protocol. `Entry` maps each role to the parameter position
    that the row gives. For example, machine's `update` is `Context, msg, model`, so its model is π₃, not Tea's π₂.

    **Rows.** `Context`, `Reply`, `Sink` and `Scope` are crossing capabilities and supply no owned value (as
    `Host`, R-5.8.11). A value that arrives over the wire (`config`, `call`, `streamRequest`) is decoded fresh and
    owned, and is symbolic as `msg` is (R-5.8.8). Each row is an obligation on the class of the field's callback:

    | Protocol | Field | Obligation |
    |---|---|---|
    | handlers | `init` | **W1.** `S₀` is `res` at the `Ok` payload of the result. The `Result`-like carrier is resolved by its shape, as for `lentoptional`, with no name test. The `Err` payload is committed to the opener (`InitializationFailed`), so it carries `T` at its `transfer`-mode backing places. That is a `transfer` demand at `init`'s return point against `init`'s live holders, such as the escaped captures of a fiber that it started in the root scope. `S₀` gets a deep no-loan demand: a loan cannot outlive `init`'s region into root state (§2.13.7). A capture of `init` moves into `S₀` only when no other callback of the record keeps it (R-5.8.3). `S₀` is registered as the **root-state holder** `R`, live until root cleanup. |
    | handlers | `start`, `handle`, `stream` | **W2.** The state parameter is **borrowed**. At every path q of `use(π₂)` that is not below a `◆`, there is no `W` (cause `write`), no `S`, no `T` (§2.13.18) and no `consumed` or once-take use. This includes what the callback's callees and the closures it makes add, through their classes and keep edges (§2.11). `R`, `A` and `E` are accepted. The root holder stays live, so a later move of a state cell that escaped is refused at that demand by Dead or Unescaped (§2.8), not here. At or below a `◆`, §2.13.7's cell contract governs the cells: a slot operation on a state `Ref` is a `writer` on its `◆`, not a write of state. **A move is the exception** (revised 2026-11-02 after the review of #1672). A `T` below a `◆` of π₂ moves a backing taken out of a state slot. At the constructor, that move is checked against the **state slot fixpoint** Ŝ. Since the fourth review of #1672, Ŝ is not a special case. It is §2.13.18's general store and spawn rule (*Stores, spawns and outside aliases*) applied at the constructor. The runtime starts every protocol callback the way a spawn-like row starts its callback: `many` times, concurrently, at any later point. So Ŝ starts from `S₀`'s handles and `◆` contents, with their `slot` annotations, and applies the slot effects of `start`, `handle` and `stream` as spawned effects. Spawned effects include those of `init`'s, `start`'s and the handlers' own fibers, children, commands and subscriptions, which spawn-like rows apply at their spawn points. Ŝ is keyed by `◆` slot identity, not by a path from π₂. So a fiber that `init` starts, which captures a state `Ref` and stores into it later, writes the same slot as a handler that reaches that `Ref` through π₂. Keys that may alias are joined. A `new n` key that a handler creates (a `Ref` it makes and stores into state) becomes a key of Ŝ while iterating, one per creating site, and is resolved through Ŝ itself. Because concurrent handlers interleave at suspensions, Ŝ is a **union of every stored payload with no strong update**: `set views [ view b ]; sleep; set views []` leaves `view b` in Ŝ, even though the handler's net effect is `views = []`. Outside aliases are kept as members with no slot. The join is iterated to a fixed point by §2.12's sparse propagation, the same way §2.13.4 iterates the model. The move is refused unless no other handle in Ŝ, inside or outside a `◆`, may share the moved slot. Otherwise a later handler could read a detached view. For example, `init` stores `{ slot = Ref.make (Just buf), view = Uint8Array.view buf }`, one `handle` takes `buf` out and transfers it, and the next reads `s.view`. Or `handle₁` stores `[ view b ]` into `s.views`, `handle₂` moves `b`, and `handle₃` reads the views. When Ŝ is unknown at that path, the move is refused. The handler's result also counts as a move at its `transfer`-mode backing places, because the runtime commits it. A returned handle whose slot may alias a slot of Ŝ is refused (§2.13.18, *Values that a callback returns to the runtime*). |
    | machine | `init` | **W3.** `M₀` is `res` at the `.0` of the `Ok` payload, and `.1` (the commands) escapes (R-5.8.5). `M₀` gets a deep no-loan demand. The `Err` payload carries `T` at its `transfer`-mode places, as in W1. Then `M₀` is exactly §2.13.4's, with R-5.8.3. |
    | machine | `update` | **W4.** §2.13.4's `update` under the role substitution: model π₃ owned, message π₂ owned. The result's `.0` is the new model, joined into the sparse fixpoint over `M` and κ(M) (R-5.8.7), and `.1` escapes (R-5.8.5). Each `W{F}` on `π₃·q` is an `entry` demand on `M@q`. A command that captures or moves a model cell is checked against the installed model: moving a buffer out of the model is accepted only when `.0` no longer holds it (Dead against the model holder). A move out of a model `Ref` is checked as in W2, against the model's slot fixpoint. That fixpoint is the same general rule applied at the constructor: `M₀`'s handles and `◆` contents, joined with the slot effects and outside aliases of every `update` arm, and of every command, subscription and fiber that `init`, `update` or `subscriptions` starts, iterated with the model's own fixpoint. It is likewise a union with no strong update, with may-alias keys joined and `new n` keys resolved through itself. |
    | machine | `subscriptions` | **W5.** The model is `read-only` (R-5.8.6), with no `S`, `T` or `consumed` use of it. |
    | machine | `request`, `stream` | **W6.** No model. `call` and `streamRequest` are owned and fresh. The result joins the message domain as `msg`. |

    Serial, concurrent, Dedicated and Shared constructors use the same row, because admission policy is not
    ownership. A pool keeps its Program's row.

    **Through helpers, captures, generic forwarding and imports.** At the constructor call, the argument at k is a
    record value. Each field's class is read by projecting `A(arg)` at that field, whether a helper built the record,
    a record update did (S5), or it came from an imported block. When the field holds a known closure, its class is
    checked against its row at once. When the field's class comes from a function parameter port (a generic
    `mk handle = Worker.program { …, handle = handle }`), v2 does not guess. The check becomes a **protocol need**
    `pneed(j·q, protocol, role, row version)` on that port. It is published in the enclosing summary's `fun(j)`
    beside S4's `need`, and it is instantiated at each call in the same way (§2.11). The caller's actual class
    discharges it, and another forwarding port carries it on. A need that is still open when it reaches a reachable
