The dependency order is S1→S2→S2b→S3a→**S4-verifier**→S3b→S4→**S8-ref**→S5→S7→S8→S8b→S9→S10, with
**S7-workers** after S7, S8-ref and S6, beside the rest of S8.
S0 remains parallel; S6 starts after S5 and runs alongside S7/S8. S4-verifier is the feasibility
stop gate before call consumers; S4 still owns full callback inference and integration. Existing slice
ids and section numbers do not change. The spike does not promise a strengthened fold-element rule.

**The reorder after S3b [O 2026-11-02].** The owner moved two pieces of work forward for the web-workers
workstream (#1290; its feature PR #1616, and #1296, #1297, #1299). Before anything else from v2, that workstream
needs real callback analysis (S4: a worker's handlers are callbacks of a constructor) and owning extraction from a
`Ref` cell: `take slot = Ref.modify slot λold → ( old, Nothing )` must prove that the removed payload is consumable
and the slot empty, and `( old, old )` keeps a loan and is refused. So, after S3b: S4; then **S8-ref**, the
`Ref`/`Deferred` slot-state part of S8 (`Ref.modify` loan returns, the no-loan ◆, consumed and escape checks, the
ordinary stored loan propagation of §2.13.7, #1404's loan-dead rule); then S5, S7 and the rest of S8. No slice is
renumbered: S8 keeps its id for what remains, and S8-ref is named the way S4-verifier is. *Checked:* S8-ref needs
S4, because the selected callback write-back is S4's and the callbacks of `Ref.update`/`modify` are callbacks. It
needs neither S5 nor S7. The tuple result of a `modify` callback, and record and tuple *literals* that hold a loan,
and their projections, are S3a constructions. What does need S5 or S7 stays behind, and the S8-ref row names it: a
loan that reaches a send or a model (S7's `Send` and `Entry` create those demands), and a loan put by a record
update, with `Record.copy`'s fix (S5). Neither kind is accepted early. For the record-update case, S3a's pessimistic
class holds until S5. For the send and model cases, S3a's class lasts only until S5, so they need their own reason,
and they have one: until S7, neither a send nor an entry has a protocol class. A send in the alias form is a call of
a function value whose class is unknown (`⊤call`), so its argument escapes (O1, O10), and S8-ref's escape check
refuses a loan in it. An entry constructor is a platform call whose callbacks have no entry class, so a model that
`init` returns leaves its region by that return, and S8-ref's region rule refuses a loan in it. So between S5 and S7
these programs are refused, not accepted. S7 replaces those refusals with the precise send and entry demands, and
makes the copied-storage controls of `LoanSend` accept. The same workstream's two other requests, worker callback
protocol obligations and native backing-identity moves, are specified in §2.13.17 and §2.13.18 and are built in
**S7-workers**.

**S4-verifier: as built and verdict (#1180).** *Feasible: §2.12's independent base/preservation
verifier decides finite recursive obligation graphs with the existing summary/value algebra, keeps
every guarantee, and its work is linear in the graph. `within` fits the algebra as built once it is
re-derived (§2.12 *`within`: emission and discharge*): an ordinary κ atom emitted by W1–W3 with a
published certificate, and discharged by route. That costs S4's read-off and Calls five computed
facts (that section's list), and one precision loss (#1220). The witnesses supply those facts by hand
(Dead, affine closures, route tags, W2's guard, D2 without coinduction, consuming the certificate);
producing them is S4's, #1229. The fold-element condition stays `lost`.*
`Fix.Prover` (§5) is the verifier. A goal is a Boolean claim `(claim, port, arg)`; the layer above's
equations (test-written here, S4's walker and read-off later) expand it, once per settled generation,
into its settled alternatives. A goal holds when every alternative holds, and an alternative when its
local check passes and every goal it needs holds: there is no disjunction. An explicit-stack Tarjan
finds the components, dependencies first. A recursive component's **base** (the alternatives that need
no member) is read with no assumption at all; its **step** (the rest) under the explicit invariant
assumption that the members hold. A component with no base is `waiting`, which fails the demand
approximately. A component's refusal is exact when one of its alternatives failed exactly. The
induction is well founded because the evaluators admit an edge into a member only for a value made
strictly earlier or strictly inside: the incoming value of a fold (`inv`) or an activation strictly
inside this invocation (`gen`). The evaluators read values with `Shape.cellsAt` and `Cond.sep`:

- `gen` (R-5.4.8) is keyed by the answer's path (`genAt`). A callback's answer at `[*]` needs the
  family's `gen` at `[*]`, not at its root. `site` and `result` pass; a callback's or a closure's
  answer needs its family's `gen` at that cell's path; a feedback value, a supply, a capture or a
  top-level value fails.
- `inv`: the owned paths hold fresh objects or the incoming one at the same path. Each stated `sep`
  atom is re-read at the outgoing cells. An atom over the incoming value is discharged only when the
  invariant states it; an atom it does not state fails approximately.
- `within`, at a consumer, by route (§2.12, D1–D4): each cell comes with every route that reaches
  it, and the cell's label is never read. A minted result passes. A nested call needs its family's
  `gen` at the cell's path, or with no actual in hand owes the consumer's own `within`. A graft of a
  taken and owned supply needs each split certified `single` and the splits pairwise of one
  traversal. Everything else fails: `env` and `shared` exactly, the rest approximately.
- `apartCalls`, at a consumer, and `writesCaptures` for a writer called through a function value (a
  top-level capture is refused exactly).

`Prover.foldWithin` is the read-off's emission: `within(ℓ)` from the members M at P when W1–W3 hold,
else `lost`, and the certificate (P, ℓ, M) with each member's multiplicity. W2's `diverge` takes the
read-off's guard and does not pass through a folded component without its `within`. `prefixWithin` is
plain κ substitution, so `within` is versioned and invalidated as every κ atom is, with no store of
its own. `joinSupply`, `handOff` (A3: a supply reaching an `env` cell stays owned only under an
affine closure) and `translate` (owned ANDed with Dead at the call) are the supply facts D3 reads.
Rounds 1–3 kept a provenance store beside the atom instead: a pre-fold pair per label, an
invocation-only bit and a conflict state. Each round guessed the route from the label and missed a
neighbouring case, so the rule was re-derived. `Marks` carry §2.2's certificate: the container, the entry, `single`
and κ at the split. They follow the crossing rules and answer `Cond.Traversal`. Their word codec reads
an out-of-range id, or a `single` word that is neither of its two spellings, as unknown. The spellings
are far apart, so a flipped bit is caught. A rewrite to the other valid spelling, or to a valid but
wrong id, is not detectable by the codec; the block's integrity check must catch it (the S4 block
extension, S6's cache entry). `Families` are persistent sets of `(code, port, allocation)`
alternatives, so a join never pairs by index. `Uses` keep once tokens as two persistent sets: arms join
by union, and a sequence adds the intersection as "many". Settled generations: every port has a
version. An expansion records the versions it reads. Reverse reader and user edges carry their
publication epoch. `bump` invalidates exactly the readers and their consumers; if a reservation fails
part way, it invalidates every answer. A solve publishes all of its answers or none, and only when
every read and every published answer it used is still current; otherwise it solves again.

**Soundness finding (a tightening).** `gen` proves that each answer is allocated by its own invocation,
by its body or by a call it makes. That separates two invocations only when neither runs inside the
other. Two calls made by one activation are disjoint subtrees of the activation tree. A callback that
re-enters its caller is not: the outer invocation may answer the inner invocation's object, and `gen`
still holds of both. So `Fix.diverge` (two label chains that part at some instruction) is required of
two callback labels before `gen` separates them, and of every two members before `foldWithin` emits
`within` (W2). mapHelp's pair `(ι_rec·ι_f⋆, ι_rec·ι_rec⋆)` diverges. A call and
a call made inside it do not diverge.

**Witnesses** (`src/own2/Fix.zig`, 17 tests, each under 0.1 s). Every label in them is built by the
fold and instantiation rules above, not named by hand.

- **GrowFresh and GrowAlias:** GrowFresh is accepted; GrowAlias's base is refused exactly and its copy
  twin is accepted; a cycle with no base is `waiting`.
- **FoldCallbackIdentity:**
  - Two fresh invocations are apart.
  - Refused: one answer twice (exact), a capture (exact), a re-returned feedback value with or without
    a fresh other arm, a self-assuming cycle (`waiting`) and a re-entrant pair.
  - A folded accumulator holding one kids list at two depths: after the widen, the class's
    path-multiset obligation is `lost` and the write is refused. With distinct lists that obligation
    is `yes`; the whole read is still `lost`, but that loss comes from the widen's collapsed fold, as in
    Cond's #1125 test.
- **`within`'s emission (W1–W3):**
  - `[ cb ⊤, cb ⊤, x ]` folds to one `within`, and its certificate names the three members.
  - Two arms of one choice owe no `sep`.
  - Refused (`lost`): hole 4 (`x = once cb; [ cb ⊤, cb ⊤, x, x ]`, pre-fold κ `shared`), two members
    with no `sep` before the fold, a pair that does not fold into the named label, a re-entrant pair,
    and chains that part only below a folded component without its `within`. The same chains under a
    certified component are accepted.
  - A folded member met twice is accepted with its own `within`, and the published certificate
    keeps its multiplicity. Without that `within` it is refused, and so is FeedbackPrevTwice's
    folded split met twice. One member renames its own `within`.
  - The supply join: borrowed wins, a supply is taken only if both are, and both nodes and both κ
    are kept, so `handOff` agrees in either order.
  - A failing pre-fold κ is the answer, and one member keeps the pre-fold κ as it is.
- **`within`'s discharge (D1–D4):**
  - Kept: C.6's push (D3), `λ_ → [ 1 ]` (D1) and `edit` (D2 beside D3), each leaving exactly
    `excl xs`. A nested call with no actual in hand owes the consumer's own `within`.
  - Refused:
    - hole 1, `List.map xs (λ_ → r)` (`env`, exactly);
    - holes 2 and 6, a supply that is not taken;
    - hole 3, `f ⊤ = [ shared ]`, by `gen` at the cell's path;
    - hole 5, `[ List.map xs f, List.map xs f ]`: two traversals, pairwise;
    - hole 8, `List.map xs (λe → [ cb e, cb e ])`: the supply is not Dead at the first call;
    - hole 9, `twiceCall (λ_ → cb e)`: the supply reaches `env e` under a closure called twice. An
      affine closure is accepted.
    - Also refused: a projection of a supply, a nested route on a cell that no call answers, and
      one failing route beside a passing one (exactly).
  - Hole 7, order dependence, is gone by construction: the certificate is a pure function of the
    settled pre-fold class.
- **`gen` by path:** `f ⊤ = [ shared ]` refuses two calls' elements, though their roots are fresh.
- **C.6 and RefinementFeedbackTwice:**
  - C.6's held-once accumulator: the keeping arm is accepted, and the second store is refused exactly
    although the base passes.
  - The `[]`-push storage write is accepted, a returned capture is refused, and a missing base is
    `waiting`.
  - The first positive control: one traversal of exclusive `xs` edits each taken list once, after
    refinement folding. Its supply demand and the result's `within` each leave exactly `excl xs`.
- **FeedbackPrevTwice:** the step's duplicate is refused exactly, and after refinement folding the
  element condition is `lost` with or without a certified mark.
- **TwoTraversalsShared and FoldOverFoldShared:** two entries read `lost`; one traversal's splits are
  apart under κ(xs[*]); both folds' storage writes are accepted.
- **NestedTraversalShared:** the inner `within` instantiated at 500 and 600 refuses the uncertified
  split. The fresh-result green and the direct map are accepted.
- **Across a block** (the AcrossModules form, minus a real module boundary): the marks round-trip, and
  a corrupt, flipped or lost mark is refused.
- **RecursiveClassGrowth:** the three settle together, the shared base is refused exactly, `[ 0 ]` is
  accepted, and no base is `waiting`. This holds under both table orders and both roots, with three
  expansions.
- **JoinedClosurePorts:** unequal and reordered tables join by identity, and the shared-capture twin is
  refused by `writesCaptures`. Once tokens are counted across alias, arms and sequence.
- **CallFeedbackGeneration:** a supply's change invalidates 3 of the 6 goals, the other instance is
  served from its memo, the refusal replaces the earlier acceptance, and the change back is accepted
  again.
- **Generations:** a version that changes during a solve, through a read or through a published answer
  it used, causes exactly one rerun.
- **Failure rollback:** each of the 30 refused allowances publishes nothing and serves nothing stale.
  These tests found that publication could stop part way, and it is now all or none.

**Mutation checks.** Each rule was removed in turn: base, feedback freshness, entry, `single`,
the self pair, unstated atoms, captures, one label twice, each staleness check, consumer
invalidation, `gen`'s path, the codec's spellings and `writesCaptures`. For `within`: W1's `sep` and
its coexistence, W2's divergence and its guard, W3 for many members and for one, membership in the
fold, the published multiplicity, the supply join's owned and taken, A3's `env` test, Dead at the
call, D1, D2's `gen`, its `cb`-only check and its fallback, D3's owned, taken, self (`m.cond`),
`single` and pairwise checks, D4's exact and approximate arms, the refusal of a cell with no route, D1's
origin check, the join's node and κ, and a failing pre-fold κ kept. Each removal fails a witness.

**Measured proof work.** A chain and a ring of n + 1 families with a demand on top, at
n = 10 / 100 / 1,000: one expansion per goal (n + 2) and n + 1 (+ 1) dependency edges. The account's
growth for the whole proof, the algebra's records included, is 127 / 1,117 / 11,017 for the chain and
135 / 1,125 / 11,025 for the ring: 11 records per goal. In the chain, a change at the top family
invalidates 2 goals (it and the demand), and a following change at the base invalidates the n others.
In the ring, a change at the top invalidates all n + 2 goals. A re-proof expands exactly the
invalidated goals.

**The fold-element question (Appendix C.9 gap 3).** The narrowed rule is not proved, and `lost` stays.
The obstacle is the caller-side discharge. After instantiation, the fold callback's
`sep(current supply, earlier list)` names one folded split, `elem(xs·ι_l⋆)`, on both sides, and that
self pair reads `lost` (§2.9). That holds with or without a certified mark, and no pre-fold pair exists
from which `within` could come. Inside the step the verifier refuses FeedbackPrevTwice's safe twin
`( x, List.push st prev )` approximately too, but only because an `Invariant` may state `sep` atoms over
the incoming value alone. That is a limit of the invariant form, not the obstacle. Lifting it would
still leave the caller-side self pair. A proof needs a new caller-side fact, such as a visited-prefix
certificate tying the current supply to the earlier lists of one traversal, and its own review.

**Left to S3b/S4 (interface obligations, not gaps in the verdict).** S4's walker and read-off produce
the alternatives, the marks (by `cross`), the five facts of §2.12's *What S4's read-off and Calls
compute* (the members of each fold with their coexistence, multiplicity and `within`, W2's guard,
the supply facts, the route-tagged `res`, and `prefixWithin` from the settled κ port), and the
refutations for a step's escape, keep and capture effects (the verifier reads values only). Its
`Resolve` names a callee family's port; the verifier keys the goal by the cell's path. Calls must not
mint a fresh `result` cell for a value reached through a feedback, including through carried closures.
`Summary.join`'s positional nested tables give way to keyed families. Block and BlockRead write and
read the mark words under the block's integrity check (the S4 block extension), and S6 runs
NestedTraversalAcrossModules across a real module boundary.

**S3b slice 4: recursive groups — the plan (#1016).** *Specified 2026-10-30; not built. It starts
when #1346 (#1335: Holders, `foldCondOf` and the block codec on cycles with no node on them) has
merged.* A call of a declaration of the caller's own group, self-recursion or mutual recursion
among top-level declarations (§2.12's first instance), applies that member's class for the current
round, and `Fix` solves the group before any member publishes. Slices 1–3 leave such a call unbuilt
(`Groups.callee`), and with it every caller of the group. These stay out of slice 4, as the rows
assign them: calls of a function value and local groups (S4); polymorphic recursion, a group call
at an instantiation other than the member's own scheme (`PolyRec*`, S4: the call stays unbuilt, and
so does its group); and `within`'s emission (S4: slice 4's read-off creates the distinct pre-fold `sep`
pairs, §8 S4; moved from S3b's 5b, #1441).

*Ports.* Each member `f` has a class port (§2.12 *Settled generation*). Its value is an immutable
`ClassId`, and its version changes only when `Summary.eq` (mutual semantic inclusion, #1094) says
the value changed. The class's parts are separate dependency ids with their own versions:
`res.shape` (the `res` graph's nodes, places, kinds and steps, without cells), `res.cells`, `use(k)`
per parameter, `kappa` (κ with the fold obligations) and `xreq`. Two rules use these parts.
- **The wake rule** decides whether an inference walk runs again. A walk is woken only by a new
  version of `res.shape` of a member it calls. Every other part is a *fact*, which is delivered
  (from 4b) and wakes no inference walk.
- **The read vector** decides whether a walk may stand as the validation. It is recorded
  *coarsely*, at each group call: **every part** of the callee's port, at the version the call saw.

*Why coarse.* The lazy, memoised readers of a view record nothing on a hit: `force`,
`Cond.machine`, Holders' closure, `aggJoin` and `setAgg`. Take f, which forces `view(h@v)` and reads
`h.res.cells`, filling the memo, and then g, which hits that memo at the same version. A per-read
vector would hold the read for f but not for g. A later delivery into `h.res.cells` would then make
f stale but not g, and g's demand would be published against the old cells. `(port, version)` keys
do not help, because both reads are at one version.

The other cure is for each memo entry derived from a group view to store its dependency set, with
a hit adding that set to the reader's vector (§2.12 asks a request to record its exact vector,
absences included). That changes five memos, and every memo added later must do the same, or the
check is silently unsound. The coarse rule is recorded at the one place a walk can meet a group
class, its own group call. Views are never shared between calls (§2.11), and every class content a
walk reads comes in through one of them (`Views.add` appends, and `Shape.make` keys a view on its
environment's index). So the coarse rule is sound whatever a memo does.

The call records the eager reads inside `apply` too, in the same entry, because they read the
callee's class before any view exists:
- `marked()` over the use shapes, the `W`, `E` and `A` marks that become the call's demands;
- the `escaped` leaves;
- `xreq`, instantiated through `instSet`;
- in the identity-class case, where `apply` answers the actual itself and makes no view, its read of
  `cls.res`.

Its price is precision of the vector, not of the verdict. A delivery into any part of h makes
every walk that called h stale, so that walk is walked again (*Validation*). That is at most one
walk per member per pass of the stop rule. The rule applies in 4a too.

*What the worklist iterates.* `Fix.worklist(Instance)` (§5) is the driver. `Groups` passes it
`Instance{ctx, step, join, leq}`, where `step` is one walk of a member, so `Fix` (L10) never imports
`Walk` (L12).
- **Round 1.** Every port starts at the empty class ⊥: `res` is nothing (`isNothing`), with no
  marks, no κ and `xreq` yes. ⊥ is for inference only (§2.12 *Recursive proofs*): nothing is
  published from a walk that read a port before the group settled.
- **Rounds are synchronous.** Round r walks every member that round r−1 woke, each against the
  round's generation, the port versions after r−1. No walk reads a class that another walk of the
  same round made. The walks of a round run in Prepass order (text rank, §3.8), which fixes ids
  only: no answer depends on the order. A Gauss–Seidel order would let declaration order choose
  where widening happens, and so what a class is.
- **A call of the group.** `Groups.callee` answers a call of a member of the same group with that
  member's class at the round's generation. `Calls.apply` applies it by reference, as slice 2b does:
  the view's environment `E` holds `(port, version)`, so views of two generations never share a
  memo entry (§2.11 *Only settled classes*). The walk records the call's edges (*Fix.propagate*,
  below).
- **The new value.** Read-off gives `F_f`. The new value is `widen(x_f ⊔ F_f)`: `Summary.join`, then
  `res` and its κ through `Cond.widenValue`. When `F_f`'s `res` and κ are under `x_f`'s
  (`Shape.leq`, `kappaLeq`), `x_f`'s are the join's and nothing is propagated: a late round that
  moves only `xreq` joined the whole unchanged `res` again, 120 000 to 135 000 records a round
  for 4a's mutual writers `wa`/`wb` (#1423).
- **Who wakes.** In 4a, any change of a callee's port wakes its callers. From 4b, only a new
  `res.shape` of a callee wakes them (the wake rule, *Ports*). Every other fact is delivered by
  `Fix.propagate` and wakes no inference walk. Such a fact can still change what a walk's demands
  and call obligations decide, so the stop rule (*Validation*, below) walks the member again
  whenever its read vector is stale.
- **When `propagate` runs.** It runs to quiescence after each round's walks, before that round's
  wake decisions.
- **A delivery whose target position does not exist yet.** The two directions differ.
  - **Along a result edge**, this happens when the target member's `res` shape there is still
    nothing. The fact is not dropped. It stays on its edge. Such a delivery comes from a source
    position that a `res.shape` change created, and that change has woken the target. The target's
    next walk makes the position, and the edge's facts reach it then, by the new-edge replay.
  - **Along an argument edge**, a mark going backwards into a caller's use shape **makes its own
    parameter-path position**. A new `use(k)` path is not a `res.shape` change, so nothing would
    wake a walk to make it, and a mark kept on its edge would never arrive. The paths come from the
    parameter's place graph with `⟲` (*Termination*), a fixed inventory, so making one costs only
    the delivery that is charged anyway. `GroupRotate` stays at two walks.
- **Stable labels.** Inside a group, read-off numbers fresh cells by stable keys, not in the order
  they are met (§2.12): an own allocation by its instruction, and anything that a group call ι answers
  fresh (`result ι·k`, for any k and any chain below it) by one folded label `ι⋆`. The pairs of
  distinct pre-fold `sep` labels it merges are not recorded in S3b: none exists, and they first exist in S4 with the `cb` labels and `foldWithin`'s members, published as the certificate (P, ℓ, M) per §2.12 (#1441). *As built (4a):* the class is published with its stable labels. A relabelling through `map` at
  publication dropped the κ that a join keys below a choice (#1395's review), and the stable keys
  already depend on no declaration order. So the label inventory is bounded by the group's instructions, however many
  rounds run. *A note, not built in slice 4:* keying the fold by `(ι, the callee's top label)` would
  keep `sep` between a callee's two own allocations. It makes the inventory calls × allocations, a
  product of source, so it waits for S4, whose `within` needs those labels anyway.

*Termination.* At a fixed inventory every part rises in a finite lattice:
- `res` is widened, a quotient over the canonical paths of its place graph with `⟲` at every
  re-entry (§2.3);
- cells range over parameter paths and the group's stable labels;
- marks range over parameter paths;
- κ and `xreq` atoms range over the same inventory and only weaken (`and(A,A)=A`).

A round that changes anything therefore moves up, and the worklist stops at a round that changes
nothing. The bound on the number of rounds is the inventory: rounds ≤ the number of
`(res or use position, cell)` facts plus the number of atom pairs, and every one of those is charged.
That is **not** source-sized:
- a constructor of n list fields shifted by one field per round takes n rounds;
- nested aliased tuples have 2^d leaf paths from O(d) source;
- `apart` pairs that weaken one at a time take O(positions²) rounds.

R_f stops each of these before the work (§4.4), loudly, so they stay sound. There is no round cap
(R-7.4).

A knot needs no new mechanism. Round r's class may be cyclic. Its view expands to views that close
through the interned view id (§2.11 *Cycles, links and folds*). A cycle with no node on it is read at
its least fixed point (#1314, #1335). `widen` takes a cyclic source, because its union–find runs over
explicit edges. `Summary.eq` and `leq` are coinductive.

*Validation and publication: the stop rule.* Every walk keeps its lines and its read vector
(*Ports*: every part of every group callee, at the version its call saw) until the next walk of its
member replaces them. When an inference round wakes nobody, the group runs one loop to a **joint
fixpoint**:

```
repeat
  for every member whose read vector differs from the current x:   (the read check)
    walk it against x, keeping its lines and its new vector
  propagate to quiescence                     (its new edges and facts)
  for every member: Summary.leq F_f ⊑ x_f     (κ and fold obligations included)
    where it fails, x_f := widen(x_f ⊔ F_f)   (x only weakens)
  if a res.shape changed: run inference rounds until no one wakes
until a pass walks no member, delivers no fact and joins nothing
```

The check is performed, never argued from the wake rule: a delivered fact wakes no inference walk,
yet it changes what the walk's demands and call obligations decide. When the loop stops, each
member's last walk saw x* exactly. That walk is the member's final source validation walk (§2.12),
its read-off is F(x*) ⊑ x*, and its demands are the ones reported. No acceptance from an earlier
generation is published (§2.12). Then every member publishes at once, with its stable labels (*Stable labels*):
`results` receive the classes and the lines together.

"Its last walk saw x* exactly" holds only if a walk is a function of the ports: two walks against the
same x read off the same class, whatever the tables hold from earlier walks. *As built (#1582):* under the
hidden, test-only `--ownership-rewalk-check`, `Groups.assertRewalks` walks every member once more at the
joint fixpoint, as a validation walk on an account of its own, and panics unless the read-off equals the
last walk's both ways (`Summary.leq`). The corpus passes the flag to every `--ownership=v2` dump. It is a
flag, not a `runtime_safety` check, because the extra walk warms memos that a later declaration reads, and
the counted tests measure records in the safety build (*the call over a chain of nested choices* fell
from 1 513 to 906 records at D = 8, #1525). It found that `map`'s knot move
(§2.3, 4e, step 3) left the knot's entry behind: `LevelFresh`'s `dup`, walked a fourth time against its
settled port, read `#Node.0 {lost}` that the port did not have. `ownership/LevelFreshDup` pins it.

The general rule follows. **An inference walk that records a new edge is followed by a validation
walk**: the facts the new edge brings arrive after that walk's vector was taken.

The first walk of a member in the loop takes its validation lane, unless an earlier walk already
took that lane (*Charging*). Every later walk, delivery and join is growth, and the passes are
bounded by the inventory, as rounds are (*Termination*).

*Why the read check and not a resolution sweep.* §2.12 also allows a resolution sweep: each call's
direct obligation and each demand recorded symbolically and resolved again after propagation, with
no walk. That needs every member's frame (holders, liveness, regions) kept across rounds, and a
symbolic form of the demands in `Demands`. It saves at most one walk per member per pass of the
stop rule, and the first of those walks runs on the validation lane that §4.1 gives every body
anyway. A sweep over D demands is O(D) ≤ O(S_f),
the same order as the walk, so the sweep is not clearly cheaper. The read check reuses the walk as
it is.

So `go n xs = …; if n == 0 then xs else go (n − 1) xs` takes two walks and no growth (§4.1's proved
R-7.4 row). Round 1 walks against ⊥. Round 2 is woken because `res` went from nothing to `π2`; it
walks against x₁ and finds F(x₁) = x₁. Its read vector is x*, so it is the validation.

`rot a b n = if n == 0 then List.length (List.push a 0) else (r = rot b a (n − 1); r + List.length
b)` is the case the check exists for. Round 1 walks against ⊥, and x₁ gets `π1 W`. From 4b, the
argument edge delivers `W` to `b`, a parameter path, so x* has `π1 W, π2 W` and no inference walk
wakes. Round 1's read vector saw `use(1)` and `use(2)` at ⊥, which differs from x*, so `rot` is
walked again against x*. That walk refuses `7:13 call rot b` as `later-use`, since `b` is read again
at 8:13, exactly as v1 does.

*`Fix.propagate`: what flows along a group's edges* (§2.12's table, Morphic I:114-171). At each group
call ι of `h` with arguments a₁…aₙ, the walk records:
- **an argument edge per k**, from `h`'s parameter k to aₖ's node;
- **a result edge**, from `h`'s `res` to the call's result, carried on to the positions of `f`'s
  `res` that hold the call's view (where its eager image lands, §2.11 *The eager image*). **A
  projection of the view carries the edge too.** A pattern or a field read of the call's result that
  reaches `f`'s `res` records an edge from `h`'s `res` at that step path, `s·p`. Without such edges,
  every projected flow would be a read, and 4b would walk again for it.

**A parameter cell's image is an edge, not a snapshot.** When aₖ is itself a group view, as in
`f x = h (g x) n`, aₖ's cells keep growing as facts are delivered. So the image of πₖ·q is an edge to
`(aₖ's node, q)`, and it is chained through `g`'s result edge: a fact delivered into `g`'s `res`
reaches `h`'s parameter, and from there `f`, along the composed edges. A cell set copied at the
walk would miss every later delivery.

Three kinds of fact flow along these edges:
- **Marks, backwards along argument edges.** A mark `R`, `A`, `E` or `W{F}` (with `S`) at πₖ·q of
  `class(h)` becomes the same mark at the parameter paths of `f` that aₖ's cells at q are (a `⟲`
  path reads every position it stands for). The mark changes the call's demands whether or not the
  cell is a parameter. A written argument owes its `callsite` demand (§2.11 item 3), and a parameter
  is no exception: it may be read after the call, or have another alias (`rot`, above). The read
  check sends that demand to the validation walk.
- **Cells, forwards along result edges.** A cell at a position p of `h`'s `res` maps under ι:
  πₖ·q becomes aₖ's cells at q, `fresh` becomes `ι⋆`, `esc` becomes `esc ι⋆`, and `shared` and ⊤ are
  kept. The image goes to the positions of `f`'s `res` that the edge names, with its occurrence facts
  (the multiset aggregate that the fold certificate reads, below).
- **κ and `xreq` atoms, along both edges.** They are substituted as plain κ substitution, and each
  atom crosses each edge once.

The edge graph is condensed into SCCs (Tarjan, explicit stack). Facts are pushed in topological order
with persistent sets. Each `(edge, fact)` pair is delivered once, and a new edge receives the facts
already present once (§2.12 *Termination*). `rot a₁ … aN n` records N edges in one walk. Its `W`
reaches every parameter through propagation, not through N walks, and the read check then adds one
validation walk. A delivered fact wakes no inference walk, and the read check accounts for every
fact a demand or an obligation reads.

*The fold certificate (#1195).* Today a cyclic source saturates (`Cond.ClassAggs.saturated`): every
class the cycle reaches is all repeated, so `lost`. That is so both in read-off's `widenValue` and in
a call's folded read (`Calls.preimage`). It stays so for every knot except a group's own, which slice
4 certifies by induction on the S4-verifier (`Fix.Prover`, new claim `fold`):
- **Key.** A goal is `(fold, member, K)`. K is the image class's canonical path in the member's `res`
  (`Shape.Table.Fold.classAt`). Widen's quotient is by canonical path, so the key does not move from
  round to round, and a certificate is used only at its own key (#1195 (a)).
- **The hypothesis node.** A view of a group class, in the source a walk widens (or in an actual
  that `Calls.Pre` reads), is a *hypothesis node* for the multiset primitive (`arrivalAggs`,
  `Calls.Pre`). The walk does not enter the view's cycle. At each key below the view, the view
  contributes its member's certificate at the corresponding key, instantiated through `E`. That
  certificate is an **aggregate**, not only an atom (#1195 (d), §2.9). With its condition, it
  publishes its arrival keys: the symbolic arrivals (for example `π1⟲#Node.1`) with their
  multiplicity, and its own fresh arrivals. The view puts those arrivals, substituted at the actual's
  cells, into the caller's multiset as ordinary arrivals.
  - So `P (same t) (same t)`, where `same t = case t of Leaf → Leaf; Node l xs r → Node (same l) xs
    (same r)`, brings `t⟲#Node.1` in twice, coexisting: `repeated`, and a writer of every `xs` is
    refused.
  - `P (same t) (same t2)` brings in two distinct arrivals, which owe `apart`, and it is accepted.
  - An atom alone, `excl(t⟲xs)` from each side, would hold on both sides and accept the first.
  - A whole knot that occurs twice (`B [w] [w]`) still adds to `repeated` (#1195 (c)). The primitive
    counts the occurrences below the cycle and outside the component as it always does (b).
- **Alternatives, on x*'s validation walk.** The goal `(fold, f, K)` expands once, on the settled
  generation, from the source of `f`'s validation walk at K. Round 1's `fold_cond` no longer exists
  by then, and §2.12 forbids reading an earlier generation.
  - The **base** is the sources at K that reach no hypothesis node, checked with no assumption.
    "Reach no hypothesis node" is **transitive**, and classified by reachability, never by the
    source's own kind. A source reaches one in two ways:
    - in the arrival DAG, through the environment of a view that is not of the group, such as
      `List.reverse (h x)`, applied by reference to an earlier group's class whose actual is a
      group view;
    - through a κ read that crosses into an actual that is a group view (§2.11 *κ across a call*).

    Such a source belongs to the step.
  - The **step** is the rest: each hypothesis node it reaches needs the goal `(fold, h, K′)` and
    assumes it.
  - The Prover decides by component. A component in which no goal has a base alternative is
    `waiting`. Its classes read `lost` at those keys, approximately.
  - This is the induction on activation depth. An activation's occurrences at K are its own sources
    (the base) plus what its calls answer, and those calls are strictly inside it (the step).
- **The answer is joined.** The Prover's answer (`lost` where it waits) is joined into x before the
  next round. So when a late F(x*) ⋢ x* sends the group round again, the certificate only weakens.
  The published `fold_cond` is the answer of the last validation.
- **Witnesses** (#1195): a deeper unrolling that repeats a cell, and a round whose step breaks the
  certificate.
- **A call's folded read.** `Calls.preimage` over an actual whose cycle is a *certified* knot (a
  settled class whose certificate at that key the induction proved) reads the certificate instead
  of saturating, by the same rules (a)–(d), its arrival keys included. An uncertified knot stays
  `repeated`: a graft tie, a BlockRead tie without the mark, or a certificate at another key. The
  block's certified mark (Q3, decided) publishes the aggregate's arrival keys with the condition.
  **Across a block**, an arrival key that does not re-intern exactly onto the importer's place reads
  `repeated` (in the multiset) and `lost` (as its condition). It never reads as absent, because an
  absent key would drop an occurrence. That happens today to a parameterised constructor type named
  alone, which keeps the block's namespace (#1317, S6).
- **What the certificate does not cover.** A folded class whose members include `ι⋆` beside an own
  allocation owes W1–W3, and it reads `lost` until S4 emits `within`. The certificate gives a
  parameter-derived fold, such as `incAll`'s `res⟲#Node.1`, the actual's κ instead of `lost`.

*The fold certificate, specified (4c, #1195)* [M 2026-10-31, measured on 4d's head `74fbcc61e`, self-hosted
Debug, `dump --stage=ownership --ownership=v2 --jobs=1`; not built]. This note measures the plan above
first, then specifies the certificate fully, and ends with a fork that the manager decides.

**What the 4c-owned known entries are.** None of them is a cycle read `repeated`.

| Known entry | v1 | v2 | Why v2 is coarser |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FoldedBCall` 30:15 `incAll b#B.1[*]#B.1⟨B⟩` | absent (v1 writes the path `b#B.1[*]⟨B⟩#B.0`, accepted `param`) | rejected `exclusive (approx)` | The call's `xreq` holds `incAll`'s `apart [π1#B.0[*]⟲#B.0] [π1#B.0[*]⟲#B.1]` and its `#B.1` twin. At the actual `b`, an element of `incList`'s parameter, both sides image to one cell, `π1[*]#B.0⟲` (or `π1[*]#B.1⟲`), so the pair reads as a repeat: `lost`. The demand on the call's first write carries the call's whole `xreq`, so this one line is refused. §2.9 rule 3 is the fix. |
| `FoldedBCallImported` `Walk` 19:15, the same line | as above | as above | The same, through the block. |
| `LevelsApartRoutes` 23:15, the same line | as above | as above | The same. |
| The other 14 lines of `FoldedBCall` 30:15 and `FoldedBCallImported` 19:15 | `accepted` / absent | absent / `accepted` | Canonical path text only (§2.2): v1 writes `#B.0[*]⟨B⟩#B.0`, v2 writes `#B.0[*]#B.0⟨B⟩`. The verdict is the same. They carry the 4c note only because they share the root. |
| #1429, the mutual `wa a` (no fixture yet) | accepted `param` | accepted `param` | It does not reproduce on `74fbcc61e`, with the issue's types and bodies at the default allowance. The fixture is still owed. |

Instrumented, over the ownership corpus (324 files and 49 projects):
- `Calls.preimage`'s Tarjan walk never finds a cycle (0 of 373 roots), so a call's folded read never
  saturates.
- Read-off's `arrivalAggs` saturates in 13 roots: `CycleJoinRankWriter`, `FoldLevels`,
  `FoldedWriteCall`, `FoldedBCall`, `FoldSymbolicCall`, `FoldedPreimageCall`, `LevelFresh`,
  `LevelRecursiveUpdates`, `LevelsApartRoutes`, `MarkerAcross`, `RoseKidsHeld`, `WriteOneLevel` and
  `LevelsApart`.
- An oracle that reads each saturated cycle as **once** (unsound, scratch only) changes no verdict in those
  13 roots. It changes one summary: `LevelRecursiveUpdates`, where three `res` paths go from `{lost}` to
  `apart …, excl …`.

So the certificate's ceiling on today's corpus is **zero verdicts**. §2.9 rule 3 alone removes every
4c-owned refusal with v1's verdict (its *Measured*). With rule 3 and the oracle, the whole
`test-blackbox` corpus (ownership, `run/`, `browser/` and core's parity) differs only in those three
lines.

**The plan's own witnesses** (a scratch module over `Tree = Node Tree (List Int) Tree | Leaf`, with
`incAll` writing every list, `incP (P a b) = P (incAll a) (incAll b)` and `same` rebuilding a tree):

| Probe | v1 | v2 | Oracle | Plan |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `incP (P (same t) (same t))` | refused `disjoint` | refused `disjoint (approx)` | refused | refused |
| `incP (P (same t) (same t2))` | refused `exclusive (approx)` | refused `disjoint (approx)` | refused | **accepted** |
| `incAll (same t)` | refused `exclusive (approx)` | refused `disjoint (approx)` | refused | (accepted by the same rule) |
| `incAll (unroll t)`, a cell repeated deeper | refused | refused `disjoint (approx)` | refused | refused |
| `w = same t; incP (P w w)` | refused `disjoint` | refused `disjoint (approx)` | refused | refused |
| `case incAll t of Node l xs r → Node l (List.push xs 2) r` | **accepted** `param` | refused `element … (approx)` | refused | **accepted** |

The oracle does not accept a single witness. The loss is in two other places:
- `same`'s class reads `{lost}` at `res#Node.1` because its arrivals hold `~π1#Node.0⟲` and `~π1#Node.2⟲`.
  These are approximate cells: at a `⟲` step `Grafter.argAt` answers `recastWhole`, the actual's whole
  reach (§2.13.9, #1219). At the call, `incAll`'s Disjoint reads the actual `same t` through the same
  recast, so the call is refused `disjoint (approx)`. A certificate that counts occurrences once
  changes neither.
- The last probe, the parameter-derived knot, is a **holder** refusal, not a κ one. `incAll`'s `res` is a
  knot whose root class holds every level's list (`res #Node.1 π1#Node.0#Node.1 π1#Node.0⟲#Node.1 π1#Node.1
  …`), so `r` is taken to hold the root's `xs`. v1 accepts it, so it is a parity gap outside the corpus
  (#1483).

**The certificate, specified.** This is the design for the slice that builds it, whichever slice
that is (the fork, below). It refines the plan above. Nothing above is withdrawn.

- **What is proved.** For a member `f` of a group and a key `K` (a class of `f`'s `res`, named by its
  canonical path, `Fold.classAt`), the certificate `A(f, K)` is an **aggregate**: the arrival keys at
  `K` (each symbolic arrival with its multiplicity in {1, 2+}, each fresh arrival likewise), and the
  condition that the multiset reads (§2.9's three parts). The claim `(fold, f, K)` says that in every
  activation of `f`, of any depth, the source occurrences that the fold maps into `K` (the activation's
  own sources at `K` and everything its group calls answer there, at every depth) are covered by
  `A(f, K)` instantiated at that activation's parameters.
- **The order of the lattice.** One aggregate is under another when each arrival's multiplicity is not
  larger and the condition is not stronger. `F` is the transfer of one activation: its own sources plus
  each group call's certificate instantiated through `E` (sum where they coexist, maximum over a choice's
  arms, a set at one position for a union). `F` is monotone, because a sum, a maximum, substitution and
  the multiset read are monotone.
- **The induction (on activation depth).** Base: an activation whose sources at `K` reach no group view
  (*Alternatives* above: transitively, by reachability). Step: if every inner activation (strictly
  inside, so of smaller depth) is covered by `A`, the activation is covered by `F(A)`, and `F(A) ⊑ A`
  gives coverage by `A`. So `A` is proved when the base is under `A` and `F(A) ⊑ A`, checked once on the
  settled generation x*. A component with no base alternative is `waiting` and reads `lost` at its keys.
  Multiplicity saturates at 2, so "repeated" is one value, and the height of the lattice is bounded by
  2 · (arrival keys) plus the atom inventory.
- **When.** During rounds a hypothesis node reads the member's **current** aggregate at `K` from the
  port, version and all. That is a may-fact, and it is used for inference only: x grows as it does
  today, and the read check (*Validation*) covers what a demand reads of it. After the stop rule's loop
  ends, the Prover proves every `(fold, f, K)` that some walk read, on x*'s validation walks, before
  publication. Where the proof fails (a component waiting, or `F(A) ⋢ A`), `lost` is joined into
  `A(f, K)` and the group goes round again. That only weakens, so the loop still terminates. No
  acceptance rests on an unproved aggregate.
- **Widen and 4d.** The key is a canonical path, so it does not move between rounds, and 4d's drop of
  covered rounds and arms does not change it, because it changes nodes and never paths. An aggregate is
  a function of the denotation, below, so a drop that keeps `Summary.leq` keeps the read only if `leq`
  also compares the aggregates. **`Summary.leq` and `kappaLeq` compare `A(f, K)` pointwise** (each
  multiplicity, then the condition), and 4d's `dropCovered` reads them. Without that, an arm `[ x, x ]`
  could be dropped under an arm `[ x ]` whose cells are the same: `Shape.leq` compares sets.
- **Publication.** The class gains one entry per certified key: `(K, arrival keys with multiplicities,
  fresh arrivals, condition)`. The summary line prints it as `cert K {keys} κ`. `Summary.eq` and
  `Summary.leq` compare it. The block publishes the certified mark (Q3, decided) with a version bump.
  Each arrival key is a structural cell (§3.6), and K is a structural canonical path. A key that does
  not re-intern exactly reads `repeated` and `lost` (#1317, S6), never absent.
- **Readers.** There are three, and each reads a certified knot in place of a saturated one:
  1. read-off's `arrivalAggs`, at a view of a group class (the hypothesis node);
  2. `Calls.preimage`, at a cycle that a settled class's certificate covers;
  3. the graft through `⟲`. `Grafter.argAt` at a level step of an actual that is a view of a certified
     class reads the aggregate's cells exactly in place of `recastWhole`'s approximate reach. The
     Disjoint and `otherPaths` readers read the same cells. This third reader is new. Without it the
     witnesses stay refused (the table above). *Amended (#1485):* it reads at every step into a
     certified class, not only at a level step (*Reader 3 at every step*, below).

  Each reader instantiates the certificate by §2.9 rule 4, and Disjoint also reads it for what it meets
  inside one certified view (§2.11 item 3 (d)). Both rules are specified in *The two walls of #1485*, below.
- **Cost.** There is one goal per `(member, K)` that a walk read, and the alternatives are the
  validation walk's sources at `K` (each read once, as the walk already does). There is one edge per
  hypothesis node, and the aggregate work is the persistent multiset merges of §2.9 (O(log) per arrival).
  In all, O(S_validation + H · A log A), where H counts hypothesis nodes and A counts arrival keys per
  certificate. *Amended (the independent review of #1519):* that bound counts source keys, not images.
  A hypothesis node's instantiation by §2.9 rule 4 costs O(W_h + M_h log M_h), where W_h is its traversal
  and projection work and M_h its image occurrences. M_h exceeds A when the actual has alternatives
  (`same (if c1 then t1 else … tN)`: M_h = 5N). So the total is
  O(S_validation + Σ_h (W_h + M_h log M_h)). All of it is charged growth on the member that receives it (Q2). Rounds that only raise
  a multiplicity or weaken a condition are bounded by the inventory, as *Termination* says.

**Soundness by cycle shape** (each with the witness that refutes the unsafe reading).
- *Self-recursive* (`same`, `incAll`). There is one member and one key per class. This is the induction
  above, unchanged. `unroll` repeats a cell one level deeper, and the step's own sources hold it twice,
  so its multiplicity is 2+ and the write is refused. *Amended (#1485):* the step holds only with §2.9
  rule 4. Without it, four keys image to one cell at `same l` and the step reads that cell as a repeat
  (*The two walls of #1485*, below).
- *Mutual* (`incAll`/`incList`, `A`/`C`). One Prover component holds the goals of both members. `K`
  and `K′` correspond through `E` at each group call, and the induction runs over the joint activation
  tree. A component in which only one member has a base is still proved, because every step reaches the
  base through the other member's goal.
- *Through records* (`P (same t) (same t)`, `B [ w ] [ w ]`). The record is built outside the component,
  and its two coexisting hypothesis nodes sum. One actual `t` brings each symbolic arrival in twice: 2+,
  refused. Two actuals `t`, `t2` bring two distinct arrivals: `apart`, accepted. That needs reader 3, and §2.11 item 3 (d) for what the walk
  meets inside one view (#1485).
- *Through `positions`* (`[ incAll b, …incList rest ]`). A positions node's sides coexist, so they
  sum. #1471 keeps a member at most twice. Two is "repeated", so the aggregate of a member kept twice
  equals the aggregate of one kept k > 2 times (Lemma C1).
- *Through choice* (`if c then same l else same r`). The arms take the maximum, arm by arm. A choice
  never adds, so a seed in one arm is once. 4d's drop of a covered arm keeps the maximum, because the
  dropped arm's aggregate is under the kept one by `leq` (above).

**Lemmas: the read does not change with the representation.** In each of the last four slices, a rule
that was exact on paper changed a read when the representation changed. So each rule here has its
lemma and a `runtime_safety` check that tests it through a reader that does not share its walk.
- **C1, saturation.** The aggregate of a `positions` DAG depends only on each member's multiplicity
  capped at 2. *Check:* for a positions node that #1471's constructor saturated, the aggregate is
  computed again over the unsaturated sides that the constructor saw, and must be equal.
- **C2, forcing and flattening** (*withdrawn* by *As built, part 2*, for review). The aggregate of a view equals the aggregate of its answer, and a
  choice gives the same aggregate whether or not `joinAlternatives` flattened it, because `arrivalAggs`
  is defined on the denotation (choice: maximum; union: a set at one position; parts: sum). *Check:* on
  each proved goal, the step aggregate is computed a second time with every view forced and every
  choice flattened into one list of arms, and must be equal.
- **C3, drops.** A 4d drop does not change any `A(f, K)` that the class publishes. *Check:* every
  `dropCovered` that removes an arm asserts `aggLeq(A_arm, A_kept)` at each certified key below the arm.
- **C4, the block.** `decode(encode(A))` equals `A` where every key re-interns, and is `repeated`/`lost`
  where one does not. *Check:* the existing block round trip (§3.6) compares the certified marks too.
- **C5, the proof.** On each published certificate, `F(A) ⊑ A` is evaluated again from the published
  class alone, without the Prover's memo, and must hold. This is the post-fixpoint check of #1195's
  second comment. It runs where the class is made, and only under the hidden `--ownership-rewalk-check`
  flag or in the `-Downership-full-cross-check` build, never as an always-on `runtime_safety` check
  (*As built, part 2*, *Where it runs*).

**The fork (the manager's decision).** The certificate as planned is not what the 4c-owned entries need,
and it does not turn any witness green without reader 3.
- **(A) 4c builds §2.9 rule 3 only.** It closes the three 4c-owned refusals with v1's verdicts. The
  other 4c lines become canonical-path-text entries. The cost is one function in `Calls.zig` of about
  100 lines, and the corpus diff is those three roots (measured, above). The certificate stays specified
  here and is built as its own slice, with reader 3, before S4 first reads a certified knot. Cycles
  keep reading `repeated` until then, which costs no corpus verdict today.
- **(B) 4c builds rule 3, the certificate and reader 3 together.** That means the `fold` claim, two
  readers made certificate-aware and a third added, the class entry, the printer and the block's version
  bump. It buys only the witnesses above, and v1 refuses two of the three that should be accepted (precision
  beyond v1). The
  parameter-derived knot is a holder gap that none of this closes (#1483).
- **Decided: (A)** (the manager, 2026-10-31, on #1484). The certificate and reader 3 are #1485, which
  must land before S4 first reads a certified knot. The recommendation was (A): It is the exact repair of what the corpus shows, it is small, and it is
  measured. (B)'s size is not justified by any verdict that the corpus or v1 has. The plan's claim that
  "the certificate gives a parameter-derived fold the actual's κ instead of `lost`" holds for κ only.
  The witness it was meant to turn green is refused on holders.

*The two walls of #1485, specified* [M 2026-10-31, on master `8e1f195d6`, self-hosted Debug,
`dump --stage=ownership --ownership=v2 --jobs=1`; specified, not built]. #1485's implementer stopped
before code (rule 10). Even if the certificate were built exactly as *The fold certificate, specified*
says, it would not prove `same` or `incAll` (Wall 1). And Disjoint would still refuse the witnesses at
paths with no `⟲` (Wall 2). The manager took the issue's option 1: the certificate proves the witnesses,
the goal of #1485 is not narrowed, and nothing is deferred. Two rules close the walls. Each one reads by
position what the certificate already claims, where the reader read it by cell.

- **Wall 1 is §2.9 rule 4.** The derivation for `same` over `Tree = Node Tree (List Int) Tree | Leaf`:

  | Key of `A(same, #Node.1)` | m | Image at `same l` (`l = π1#Node.0`) | Image at `same r` (`r = π1#Node.2`) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `π1#Node.1` | 1 | `π1#Node.0#Node.1` | `π1#Node.2#Node.1` |
  | `π1#Node.0#Node.1` | 1 | `X = π1#Node.0⟲#Node.1` | `Y = π1#Node.2⟲#Node.1` |
  | `π1#Node.0⟲#Node.1` | 1 | `X` | `Y` |
  | `π1#Node.2#Node.1` | 1 | `X` | `Y` |
  | `π1#Node.2⟲#Node.1` | 1 | `X` | `Y` |

  Each call is one group: its actual is the leaf of `π1#Node.0` (or `π1#Node.2`), met at the empty
  prefix. The four keys that reach `X` take the maximum, 1, and owe `exclOf(X)`. With the own source
  `π1#Node.1`, `F(A) = A`. The base (`Leaf → Leaf`) has no arrival at `K`. So `A` is proved, with the
  condition `excl π1#Node.0⟲#Node.1 ∧ excl π1#Node.2⟲#Node.1`. The other pairs are distinct paths of one
  parameter, which the frame takes as apart and its callers check through the marks (§2.11 item 3 (c)).
  `incAll` has the same derivation, since its `List.push xs 1` answers `π1#Node.1`. Counted by cell
  (`aggAdd` today), `X` and `Y` read 2+, and the certificate reads `lost`.
  *Amended (#1559), under the atom rule* (§2.3, #1483). There are now three certificates, one per
  class, and the five keys split among them:
  - `A(same, #Node.1)` is `{π1#Node.1}`;
  - `A(same, #Node.0#Node.1)` is `{π1#Node.0#Node.1, π1#Node.0⟲#Node.1}`;
  - `A(same, #Node.2#Node.1)` is `{π1#Node.2#Node.1, π1#Node.2⟲#Node.1}`.

  At `same l` all three land in the caller's `#Node.0#Node.1`, so the table above is the read there.
  It holds only when rule 4 reads the three classes together (§2.9 rule 4, *Across the classes of
  one certificate*). Read class by class, `X` arrives from two classes, and both subtree classes read
  `lost`. With the rule, the prototype measures `same` as `res #Node.0#Node.1 π1#Node.0#Node.1
  π1#Node.0⟲#Node.1{apart [π1#Node.0#Node.1] [π1#Node.0⟲#Node.1], excl π1#Node.0⟲, excl
  π1#Node.0⟲#Node.1}, #Node.1 π1#Node.1, #Node.2#Node.1 π1#Node.2#Node.1 π1#Node.2⟲#Node.1{apart
  [π1#Node.2#Node.1] [π1#Node.2⟲#Node.1], excl π1#Node.2⟲, excl π1#Node.2⟲#Node.1}; cert`. The same
  change takes `incAll`'s subtree classes from `{lost}` to `{apart …, excl …}` in `ReturnedKids`,
  `LevelRecursiveUpdates`, `MarkerAcross` and `WriteOneLevel`, with no verdict changed there.
- **Wall 2 is §2.11 item 3 (d).** At `incP (P (same t) (same t2))`, each write of `incP` below `#P.0` has
  its spine meet the one view `V₁ = same t` at the prefix `#P.0`, with its rest in `K`. Every item that
  the walk meets inside `V₁` drops `K`, whether it stands at `K` (`π1#P.0#Node.0#Node.1` beside the
  write at `π1#P.0#Node.1`) or holds a tree whose reach holds `K` (`π1#P.0#Node.0 RA`). The call relies
  once on κ̂(V₁, K), which is `excl t#Node.0⟲#Node.1 ∧ excl t#Node.2⟲#Node.1`. The same holds below
  `#P.1` with `t2`. An item below `#P.1` is outside `V₁` and keeps its cells, `t2`'s keys, which are
  apart from `t`'s. `incAll (same t)` and `incRoot (same t)` meet `V` at the empty prefix. In
  `incRoot`, the answered subtrees `π1#Node.0` and `π1#Node.2` hold `K` only, so they keep nothing.
  (Whether those held marks shrink once rule 4 projects a leaf through `⟲` symbolically is not
  measured. (d) does not depend on it.)
- **Reader 3 at every step.** Wherever Disjoint and `otherPaths` read the cells of a certified view at a
  position in `K`, through a level step or a plain one, they read `A(f, K)`'s arrival keys instantiated by
  rule 4. The certificate covers every object at a position of `K`, so this is a sound cell set. It equals
  the class's own cells at `K` where those are exact, and it replaces an approximate cell such as
  `same`'s `~π1#Node.0⟲` today (the `recastWhole` reach). So a refusal across two views of one tree is
  exact: `disjoint`, v1's word, not `disjoint (approx)`.

**The witnesses.** v1 and v2 are measured on `8e1f195d6`. The verdict under the rules is derived on
paper, and the scratch model below agrees with it. *Concrete* is that model run on every tree of
height 3 or less whose lists are pairwise distinct, which is the `xreq` that a caller must meet. "Unsafe"
means that the in-place writes reach one list object twice.

| Probe | v1 | v2 today | Under rule 4 and (d) | Concrete |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `incP (P (same t) (same t))` | refused `disjoint` | refused `disjoint (approx)` | refused `disjoint`: `t#Node.1` at `#P.0#Node.1` and `#P.1#Node.1`, two views | unsafe on 25 of 26 |
| `incP (P (same t) (same t2))` | refused `exclusive (approx)` | refused `disjoint (approx)` | **accepted** `param`, with `excl` of each tree's lists below its first returns in `xreq` | safe on 130 of 130 |
| `incAll (same t)` | refused `exclusive (approx)` | refused `disjoint (approx)` | **accepted** `param`, likewise | safe on 26 of 26 |
| `incRoot (same t)`, `incRoot t = case t of Node l xs r → Node l (List.push xs 1) r` | accepted `param` | refused `disjoint (approx)` | **accepted** `param`: the answered `π1#Node.0` and `π1#Node.2` are inside `V` and drop `K` | safe on 677 of 677 (height ≤ 4): the root list is in no subtree |
| `incRoot (unroll t)` | refused `call (approx)` | refused `disjoint (approx)` | refused `disjoint (approx)`: `A(unroll)` is `lost` | unsafe on 676 of 677: the root list is also the left child's |
| `incAll (unroll t)`, `unroll t = Node (Node (unroll l) xs Leaf) xs (unroll r)` | refused `exclusive` | refused `disjoint (approx)` | refused `disjoint (approx)`: the own source `π1#Node.1` is met twice, so `A(unroll)` is `lost` | unsafe on 25 of 26 |
| `w = same t; incP (P w w)` | refused `disjoint` | refused `disjoint (approx)` | refused `disjoint`: `#P.0` against `#P.1`, one view at two occurrences | unsafe on 25 of 26 |
| `case incAll t of Node l xs r → Node l (List.push xs 2) r` | accepted `param` | refused `element … (approx)` | refused, unchanged: a holder gap (#1483), not a κ one | — |

So each refusal that the rules keep, other than #1483's holder gap, is genuine, and each new acceptance
is safe on every input that meets its `xreq`. `incRoot (same t)` is also a v1 parity line: v1 accepts it,
and before the review of #1519 this spec still refused it. `unroll`, `P w w` and `P (same t) (same t)` write one list twice on every tree that has a list.

concrete model agrees with the expected verdict, except the precision gaps, which are safe programs that
stay refused.

*The oracle.* It is a Node model of the 24 probes above (rows 11–13, 15–17 and the wrappers
aside). It runs each probe copying every write, and again in place at every line the dump
accepts, then compares the results. It uses every tree of height 3 or less with pairwise distinct
lists, both `Bool`s and `n` ∈ {0, 1, 2}: 42 744 runs.
- **0 unsafe with the rule**: 17 of the 24 probes have an accepted line.
- With every line forced to be accepted, it reports UNSAFE on 14 of the probes: those marked unsafe
  above.
- The verdicts by class, and the three unsound variants below, also give 0 unsafe on these programs.
  Each of them is refused by the frame's own κ too. So only the unit cases tell the variants apart:
  - the unit cases pass with the rule;
  - case (i) fails without the sum for each key;
  - case (iii) fails with the trie run for each class alone;
  - case (ii) checks that two groups add. `L` in the group's key is `ruleFourKey`'s, so a unit test of
    the group ids pins it: `a` at `#Node.0` and `a` at `#Node.2` of `Node a ys a` get two ids, and
    one key in two classes gets one id.

**Lemmas for the walls.** They extend C1–C5. Each has a `runtime_safety` check through a reader that does
not share its walk.
- **C6, rule 4.** Lemma R4 (§2.9). *Check:* `Grafter.assertRoutesApart` wherever a group merges keys.
  It compares the merged keys by `Cell.alias` and traces the one-position walk, and it unrolls nothing.
  C2's check computes the step aggregate again with every view forced and every choice flattened, and
  that computation applies rule 4 too, so C2 also tests R4 on the forced representation.
  *Extended (#1559).* Lemma R4′ (§2.9 rule 4, *Across the classes of one certificate*) is checked
  wherever two or more classes of one certificate land at one caller class:
  - the merged keys are pairwise distinct cells;
  - `Cell.alias` is `no` over the distinct keys of each group that passed (a′), across all the
    landing classes;
  - `Cond.assertClassesSum` recounts the read at the caller class from the landing classes' key
    sets, with no code shared with the rule's aggregate or with `certClassAgg`. It uses only the
    groups that passed (a′). In such a group, a key's multiplicity is the number of landing classes
    that hold it, and members of a union or a choice inside one class count once. A key in no group,
    a dropped group's included, counts every image occurrence. The recount must agree with the rule on which images are repeats and on
    which owe `exclOf`.
- **C7, Disjoint by certificate.** The read of §2.11 item 3 (d). *Check:*
  `TransferBeside.assertCertifiedDrop` wherever the rule drops `K` at an item. Inside a group being
  solved the check is deferred to publication, and it runs only if the verdict it covers is final.

**Cost.** Rule 4 is O(W + M log M) per instantiation, with W its traversal and projection work and M its
image occurrences (§2.9 rule 4, *Cost*), so the certificate's total is O(S_validation + Σ_h (W_h + M_h
log M_h)) (*Cost*, above). The counted test with N alternatives (`same (if c1 then t1 else … tN)`, N = 8 to
64) must be linear in N. Rule (d) adds O(1) per item of `otherPaths`' walk (one class id
carried) and, per `(call, V, K)`, one instantiation per class of `C` and one memoised union per class, so a
K-wide tree writer stays linear per call. Neither rule expands a join or adds a walk in a release build. No verdict of today's corpus moves before #1485
is built, because both rules read a certificate and no certificate exists yet. #1485 measures the
corpus with them. 4c's oracle (*What the 4c-owned known entries are*, above) found no corpus verdict that
certificates change, so the expected corpus diff is the new fixtures only.

column and the expected verdicts of the near misses. Under the count by cell, every self-recursive
certificate (`same`, `swap`, `incAll`) reads `lost` at `π1#Node.0⟲#Node.1` and `π1#Node.2⟲#Node.1`,

added after the review of #1519 (`incRoot`, `wrapR`) were checked concretely by a second script, on every
tree of height 4 or less, and derived on paper for the item form of (d) and the alias form of (a′).

*As built, part 1 (#1485, partial: the PR says what is left).* Self-hosted Debug,
`dump --stage=ownership --ownership=v2 --jobs=1`.
- **The root's `lost` was two keying gaps, not a transport gap.** The stop report traced the last
  refusal of `incAll (same t)` to `same`'s published root κ `{lost}`, and guessed that read-off's
  cyclic copy of a knot view lost its κ. Measured: `Shape.map` and the read-off's carry move every
  entry the frame holds, the copy's nodes included (the relabelled class κ sits at `view(n, E)` for
  each keyed `n`, and `Carry.node` maps it to the image). The class itself had no entry to carry:
  - *Widen keyed the union, not its built side.* At a fold position `propagate` writes one entry per
    state, keyed by the state's joined node. A knot rooted at `Leaf | Node …` is a `union` whose
    `node` side is widen's own record: no member snapshot holds it and no state is keyed by it, so a
    read of the union joins in that side's `lost` (O13). Now, while `widenValue` propagates, each
    built side of a union or choice at a fold that no state keys takes that state's κ
    (`Cond.Table.widen_sides`, `unionSides`). *Lemma:* the state's κ is the join of every member's
    read at that position; an object at the fold through that side is one of those members' objects
    (widen's quotient), so the join covers it. The entry is added only where nothing else keys the
    node, so no member's own entry is weakened.
  - *A port join collapsed the knot.* `Summary.joinRes` merged the two classes' snapshots first
    (`kappaMerge`). The port's knot is an exact fold at the root, the new round's root is not a fold,
    and §2.9 merges the two into a collapsed fold, where every built node reads `lost`. The widened
    join is now propagated from the two members, each at its own snapshot (`widenValueOf`).
    `propagate` is defined on a join of its members, widened or not (§2.9), so this reads what the
    members store, and the merged snapshot still serves the unwidened join.
  - *Check* (`runtime_safety`, `widenValueOf`): O15 on the widened value, every member's κ at its root
    under the widened root's. No ownership fixture fires it.
  So no second mechanism reads a hypothesis node's κ at the view: the copy reads the class's entries,
  which now exist. `same`'s published root is `yes`, and `incAll (same t)` and
  `incP (P (same t) (same t2))` are accepted on every line.
- **Reader 3 at every leaf.** `Grafter.argAt` projects an exact symbolic or refined leaf (no `⊤`, no
  approximate cell, none under a repeating split) through `⟲` symbolically at every call, not only at
  a certified view. *Argument:* such a leaf stands for exactly its cells' projections (§2.2: projecting
  a symbolic cell appends a step), and `Place.extend` names a `⟲` image as every position of its cycle,
  a join name where the place is a root or unsealed. So the projection names a superset of the
  positions `recastWhole` would reach, as exact cells instead of one approximate one. *Corpus:* no
  verdict changes over the ownership, `run/`, `browser/` and core corpora; `core.v2.unchecked` loses
  `Dict descend` (lines 604-611), which no longer stops at its limit. *Measured:* no `~…⟲` cell remains
  at `#Node.1[*]` or below in `same`, `incAll` or `unroll`, so none can alias a written key at
  `incAll (same t)` or `incRoot (same t)`.
- **A κ̂ that fails still tags its occurrence.** When κ̂(V, K) is `shared` or `lost`, the items inside
  `V` keep every class, `K` included, exact or approximate (`TransferBeside.Occ.fail`), so the write is
  refused `disjoint` or `disjoint (approx)`, as (d) says. The WIP fell back to the cell comparison
  there, and that is why `incAll (unroll t)`, `incRoot (unroll t)` and the safe row 4 (`deeper`) read
  a plain `disjoint`, a definite conflict the rule does not claim. They now read `disjoint (approx)`,
  as the witness table has them, so the table needs no amendment.

*As built, part B (#1485: the overlap trie and the cost tests).* Self-hosted Debug unless stated.
- **(a′) is `Cell.keysOverlap`, in every build.** The group's keys go into a trie over the path
  table's own nodes, keyed by `(origin, index, c, path)`. The test is O(Σ |k|). The keys overlap when
  a key's node is already in the trie or is above another key, or when a trie node has a `⟲` child and
  another child whose place is on that `⟲`'s cycle (`Place.sameCycle`). That is `pathsMayAlias`'s
  relation at the divergence node, so the verdict equals "some pair has `alias` not `no`".
  `KappaRead.certClassAgg` and `Grafter.ruleFourSides` both call it, once per group and before any
  maximum or `exclOf`. An overlapping group is dropped whole. The pairwise loops they used before are
  gone. So is the per-image run check, because a group that passes has no two keys that alias.
  - *Memo.* By the group's key set, a hash-consed `SetId` (`Cell.Table.overlap_memo`), so the
    answer is a function of the group and never of the order in which groups are tested. Each call
    reserves the test's Σ (depth + 1) steps, as an inspection charged to the instantiation's account,
    whether the memo hits or not. So no account depends on which call built the entry (§4.1).
  - *Check* (`runtime_safety`, on every call): the verdict is compared with `Cell.alias` on every pair
    of the set, which shares nothing with the trie. A difference panics. No ownership fixture fires it.
    This is C6's pairwise half. Part A's `assertRoutesApart` (the traced preimage walk) is separate.
- **A second quadratic term, found by the counted test and fixed.** `TransferBeside.keepReach`
  asked `holdsCanonical` once per parameter cell of the base, and each ask scanned the whole reach:
  O(|params| × |reach|). At `same (if … tN)` both are about 5N, and the beside read at
  `reachBeside` cost 51 680 / 205 280 / 819 680 inspections at N = 16 / 32 / 64. Now the reach is
  scanned once per `keepReach` (`Canon`). Its parameter cells, with their canonical cells, are kept
  in the reach's order and bucketed by `(origin, index, c)`, and each ask reads its own bucket.
  `Cell.below` and equality hold only within one bucket, so the answer is the same first cell in
  the reach's order. No verdict changes anywhere in the ownership corpus.
- **The counted tests** (`build_test.zig`). Records are deterministic, and each test runs one
  process: every size is a declaration of one module, so `incAll` and `same` are solved once.
  - *Over N alternatives*: `incAll (same (if n == 1 then t1 else … tN))` at N = 6 and 12, accepted.
    Twice N may cost twice the records plus a sixteenth of the cost at N = 6, which leaves room for
    the radix sets' log factor. This test catches the two quadratic terms.
  - *Through a shared DAG of built nodes*: `x{i} = if n == i then Node x{i-1} [] Leaf else x{i-1}`,
    `incAll (same x{N})`, at depth 4 and 8. Each key's walk goes through built nodes, and every
    choice names the one before it twice. Twice the depth may cost at most twice the records. The
    line is refused because `same` over a built node reads its root `lost` (row 14, part A); this
    test pins the cost only. It catches the projection memo.

  | build (self-hosted ReleaseSafe) | N = 6 | 12 | depth 4 | 8 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | this branch | 40 254 | 78 591 | 25 487 | 45 443 |
  | groups tested by pairs (the checkpoint's `certClassAgg`) | 42 683 | 89 812, fails | | |
  | `holdsCanonical` once per parameter cell | 43 134 | 91 551, fails | | |
  | `Shape.proj`'s memo hits ignored | | | 54 322 | 194 401, fails |

  Each mutant was applied to the source and run through the test step, which failed. Each test
  takes 0.6–0.65 s, under a host load average of 9–20.
  - *An image expanded per level path is not a matter of scale.* How many level paths a `⟲` stands
    for is a property of the type, so the expansion is a constant factor for any fixed type. A family
    that widens the type to multiply it widens the certificate's class quadratically: `incAll` over a
    `Tree` with two list fields, or a `W` with four recursive fields, already exceeds
    `ownership_summary_size` (the k-list-fields test documents the k² class). And for `Tree`,
    `Place.levelPaths` names no join at a root or a sealed return. So `expandLevels` on every image
    changes nothing: 53 478 against 52 390 at N = 8 over alternatives. So the property is pinned
    where it is decided. `Calls.zig`, *a group's image through `⟲` is one join name per member*,
    expects one image per member of a two-member group at the root join `root⟲`, which stands for two
    level paths (`levelsOf`). A mutant that expands images into `levelsOf`'s paths gives 8 images
    there instead of 2, and the test fails.
- **Rows 18 and 19** are in `o/FoldCertificate` (part 1) and refused `disjoint (approx)`. Neither
  needs the trie today: `h2`'s and `g2`'s classes read `lost`, because `h2` calls `same` on a built
  node (`same (Node t [] Leaf)`, row 14's open root `lost`). So the trie is tested directly:
  - `Cell.zig`, *rule 4 (a′): the trie …*: row 18's keys overlap and `same`'s five keys do not. Prefix
    and off-cycle siblings are covered. Row 19's `π1` group is apart and its `π2` group overlaps,
    in both orders.

  tests pass in the walk's order, under `otherPaths-spine-first`, and under that switch plus
